children.translated_text: <s>Devadeva</s> (the God of gods) said:
Between (the rivers) <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>, in <s>Kurujāṅgala</s>,
the ancient <s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>, seated in the excellent assembly,
was asked by the best of twice-born about the glory of the lake. // VamPSm 1.1 //

children.text: pramāṇaṃ saraso brūhi tīrthānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Tell us the extent of the lake and especially of the sacred fords (<s>tīrthas</s>),

children.text: devatānāṃ ca māhātmyamutpattiṃ vāmanasya ca // VamPSm_1.2 //
children.translated_text: and the greatness of the deities and the origin of <s>Vāmana</s>. // VamPSm 1.2 //
Having heard those words of theirs, accompanied by horripilation,
the ancient sage, having bowed down, spoke these words: // VamPSm 1.3 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: brahmaṇamagryaṃ kamalāsanasthaṃ viṣṇuṃ tathā lakṣmisamanvitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having bowed my head to <s>Brahmā</s>, the foremost, seated on the lotus, and to <s>Viṣṇu</s> accompanied by <s>Lakṣmī</s>,

children.text: rudraṃ ca devaṃ praṇipatya mūrdhnā tīrthaṃ mahad brahmasaraḥ pravakṣye // VamPSm_1.4 //
children.translated_text: and to <s>Rudra</s>, the god, I shall speak of the great <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford), <s>Brahmasaras</s> (the lake of <s>Brahmā</s>). // VamPSm 1.4 //
From <s>Rantuka</s> to <s>Aujasa</s>, and from <s>Pāvanā</s> to <s>Caturmukha</s>,

children.text: saraḥ saṃnihitaṃ proktaṃ brahmaṇā pūrvameva tu // VamPSm_1.5 //
children.translated_text: the lake called <s>Saṃnihita</s> was proclaimed by <s>Brahmā</s> in ancient times. // VamPSm 1.5 //
Between the <s>Kali</s> and <s>Dvāpara</s> (ages), by the great-souled <s>Vyāsa</s>,
the extent of the lake was proclaimed — hear that, O best of twice-born! // VamPSm 1.6 //
From <s>Viśveśvara</s> to <s>Asthipura</s>, (the place of) chariots, the maiden, and the old cow,
as far as (the river) <s>Oghavatī</s> is said (to extend), so far extends the lake <s>Saṃnihita</s>. // VamPSm 1.7 //

children.text: mayā śrutaṃ pramāṇaṃ yat paṭhyamānaṃ tu vāmane /
children.translated_text: I have heard the extent as it is recited in the <s>Vāmana</s> (Purāṇa) —

children.text: tacchṛṇudhvaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ puṇyaṃ vṛddhikaraṃ mahat // VamPSm_1.8 //
children.translated_text: hear that, O best of twice-born! It is sacred and greatly auspicious. // VamPSm 1.8 //
From <s>Viśveśvara</s>, O best of gods, from <s>Nṛpāvana</s>, (the river) <s>Sarasvatī</s> —
the lake <s>Saṃnihita</s> should be known as extending half a <s>yojana</s> on all sides. // VamPSm 1.9 //
Having resorted to this (lake), gods and sages assembled;

children.text: sevante muktikāmārthaṃ svargārthe cāpare sthitāḥ // VamPSm_1.10 //
children.translated_text: they worship it for the purpose of liberation, while others remain for the sake of heaven. // VamPSm 1.10 //
This was frequented by <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>yogin</s>, desiring creation;
it was frequented by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of <s>Hari</s>, desiring preservation. // VamPSm 1.11 //
And by <s>Rudra</s>, the great-souled one, who entered the middle of the lake,

children.text: sevya tīrthaṃ mahātejāḥ sthāṇutvaṃ prāptavān haraḥ // VamPSm_1.12 //
children.translated_text: the <s>tīrtha</s> was served, and <s>Hara</s>, of great splendor, attained the state of <s>Sthāṇu</s> (the immovable one). // VamPSm 1.12 //
This is the primordial altar of <s>Brahmā</s>; hence it is known as <s>Rāmahrada</s>;

children.text: karuṇā ca yataḥ kṛṣṭaṃ kurukṣetraṃ tataḥ smṛtam // VamPSm_1.13 //
children.translated_text: and because it was ploughed with compassion, it is known as <s>Kurukṣetra</s>. // VamPSm 1.13 //
That which lies between <s>Tarantuka</s> and <s>Ārantuka</s>, that which lies between <s>Rāmahrada</s> and <s>Caturmukha</s> —
this is <s>Kurukṣetra</s>-<s>Samantapañcaka</s>, called the northern altar of the Grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>). // VamPSm 1.14 //
Thus ends the first chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the sacred <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
Tell us the greatness of <s>Vāmana</s> and especially his origin,

children.text: yathā balirniyamito dattaṃ rājyaṃ śatakratoḥ // VamPSm_2.1 //
children.translated_text: how <s>Bali</s> was subdued and the kingdom was given to <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>). // VamPSm 2.1 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Hear, O delighted sages, of the great-souled <s>Vāmana</s>'s

children.text: utpattiṃ ca prabhāvaṃ ca nivāsaṃ kurujāṅgale // VamPSm_2.2 //
children.translated_text: origin, glory, and dwelling in <s>Kurujāṅgala</s>. // VamPSm 2.2 //
Hear then the lineage of the <s>Daityas</s>, O best of twice-born,

children.text: yasya vaṃśe samabhavad balirvairocaniḥ purā // VamPSm_2.3 //
children.translated_text: in whose lineage was born <s>Bali</s>, the son of <s>Virocana</s>, in ancient times. // VamPSm 2.3 //
The first man of the <s>Daityas</s> was <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> in ancient times;

children.text: tasya putro mahātejāḥ prahlādo nāma dānavaḥ // VamPSm_2.4 //
children.translated_text: his son, of great splendor, was the <s>Dānava</s> named <s>Prahlāda</s>. // VamPSm 2.4 //
From him <s>Virocana</s> was born, and from <s>Virocana</s> was born <s>Bali</s>.
When <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> was slain, having driven away the gods on all sides, // VamPSm 2.5 //

children.text: rājyaṃ kṛtaṃ ca teneṣṭaṃ trailokye sacarācare /
children.translated_text: he (Bali) performed the desired rule over the three worlds with all their moving and stationary beings.

children.text: kṛtayatneṣu deveṣu trailokye daityatāṃ gate // VamPSm_2.6 //
children.translated_text: When the gods had exerted their efforts and the three worlds had come under <s>Daitya</s> dominion, // VamPSm 2.6 //
with the conquest of the mighty <s>Maya</s> and <s>Śambara</s> as well,

children.text: śuddhāsu dikṣu sarvāsu pravṛtte dharmakarmaṇi // VamPSm_2.7 //
children.translated_text: when all the directions were purified and <s>dharma</s>-rituals were being performed, // VamPSm 2.7 //
when the <s>Daitya</s> path was established and the sun was stationed in its course,
with <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Śambara</s>, <s>Maya</s>, and <s>Anuhvāda</s> as well, // VamPSm 2.8 //
when all directions were at rest and the sky was protected by the <s>Daityas</s>,

children.text: deveṣu makhaśobhāṃ ca svargasthāṃ darśayatsu ca // VamPSm_2.9 //
children.translated_text: while the gods were showing the splendor of sacrifices in heaven, // VamPSm 2.9 //

children.text: prakṛtisthe tato loke vartamāne ca satpathe /
children.translated_text: when the world was in its natural state and proceeding on the good path,
in the absence of all sins and with <s>dharma</s> ever on the rise, // VamPSm 2.10 //
when <s>dharma</s> stood on four feet and <s>adharma</s> was reduced to a quarter,
when kings, devoted to the protection of their subjects, were shining,
and when the dwellers of the <s>āśramas</s> were engaged in their own <s>dharma</s>, // VamPSm 2.11 //
<s>Bali</s> was then consecrated by all the <s>Asuras</s> to the <s>Daitya</s> kingdom,
while the hosts of <s>Asuras</s> rejoiced and roared with delight. // VamPSm 2.12 //
Then <s>Lakṣmī</s> approached <s>Bali</s>, radiant as (if from) within a lotus,
the goddess, with lotus-raised hands, bestowing boons, of graceful entrance. // VamPSm 2.13 //
<s>Śrī</s> said:
O <s>Bali</s>, best of the mighty, O king of <s>Daityas</s>, of great splendor,

children.text: prītāsmi tava bhadraṃ te devarājaparājaye // VamPSm_2.14 //
children.translated_text: I am pleased with you — blessings upon you — in (your) defeat of the king of gods! // VamPSm 2.14 //
Since the kingdom of the gods was conquered by you in battle through valor,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā te paramaṃ sattvaṃ tato 'haṃ svayamāgatā // VamPSm_2.15 //
children.translated_text: having seen your supreme power, I have come of my own accord. // VamPSm 2.15 //
It is no wonder, O tiger among <s>Dānavas</s>, in the lineage of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,
that such deeds are yours, O lord of <s>Asuras</s>, born (in that line). // VamPSm 2.16 //
You have surpassed, O king, the <s>Daitya</s> lord, your great-grandfather,

children.text: yena bhuktaṃ hi nikhilaṃ trailokyamidamavyayam // VamPSm_2.17 //
children.translated_text: by whom this entire imperishable three worlds was enjoyed. // VamPSm 2.17 //

children.text: evamuktvā tu sā devī lakṣmīrdaityanṛpaṃ balim /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that goddess <s>Lakṣmī</s>, to the <s>Daitya</s> king <s>Bali</s>,
entered (his court), bestowing boons, worthy of worship, delighting the minds of all gods. // VamPSm 2.18 //

children.text: tuṣṭāśca devyaḥ pravarāḥ hrīḥ kīrtirdyutireva ca /
children.translated_text: And the foremost goddesses were pleased — <s>Hrī</s> (modesty), <s>Kīrti</s> (fame), <s>Dyuti</s> (radiance),

children.text: prabhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā bhūtir ṛddhirdivyā mahāmatiḥ // VamPSm_2.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhā</s> (light), <s>Dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>Kṣamā</s> (patience), <s>Bhūti</s> (prosperity), <s>Ṛddhi</s> (abundance), the divine <s>Mahāmati</s> (great wisdom), // VamPSm 2.19 //
<s>Śruti</s> (revelation), <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition), <s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Kīrti</s> (fame), <s>Śānti</s> (peace), <s>Puṣṭi</s> (nourishment), and <s>Kriyā</s> (action),
and all the divine <s>Apsaras</s>es, skilled in dance and song — // VamPSm 2.20 //
they all submitted to the lord of <s>Daityas</s>; the three worlds with all their moving and stationary beings
attained incomparable sovereignty under <s>Bali</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>. // VamPSm 2.21 //
Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the sacred <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
[Note: INVALID CHARACTERS IN SOURCE]
The sages said:

children.text: devānāṃ brūhi naḥ karma yadvṛttāste parājitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Tell us the deeds of the gods — what happened when they were defeated,
and how that god of gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, assumed the form of the dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>). // VamPSm 3.1 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: balisaṃsthaṃ ca trailokyaṃ dṛṣṭvā devaḥ purandaraḥ/
meruprasthaṃ yayau śakraḥ svamāturnilayaṃ śubham // VamPSm_3.2 //
children.translated_text: went to the slopes of <s>Meru</s>, to the auspicious abode of his mother, <s>Śakra</s>. // VamPSm 3.2 //
Seeing the three worlds under <s>Bali</s>'s dominion, the god <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>)

children.text: samīpaṃ prāpya mātuśca kathayāmāsa tāṃ giram /
children.translated_text: Having reached his mother's presence, he told her those words —

children.text: ādityāśca yathā yuddhe dānavena parājitāḥ // VamPSm_3.3 //
children.translated_text: how the <s>Ādityas</s> had been defeated in battle by the <s>Dānava</s>. // VamPSm 3.3 //
<s>Aditi</s> said:
If indeed, O son, <s>Bali</s>, the son of <s>Virocana</s>, cannot be slain in battle
by you and all the hosts of the <s>Maruts</s>, // VamPSm 3.4 //
he can be slain in battle only by the thousand-headed one (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),

children.text: tenaikena sahasrākṣa na sa hyanyena śakyate // VamPSm_3.5 //
children.translated_text: by him alone, O thousand-eyed one — for he cannot (be slain) by any other. // VamPSm 3.5 //
for the defeat of that great-souled <s>Daitya Bali</s>. // VamPSm 3.6 //
Therefore, I shall ask (your) father <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>,
Then <s>Aditi</s> together with the gods came to the presence of <s>Kaśyapa</s>;
there they beheld <s>Mārīca</s> (son of <s>Marīci</s>), the sage, a blazing treasure of austerity, // VamPSm 3.7 //
the foremost divine preceptor of the gods, resplendent with the radiance of <s>Brahman</s>,
in splendor like the sun, standing like the flame of fire, // VamPSm 3.8 //
who had set aside the staff (of a wandering ascetic), devoted to austerity, wearing a garment of black antelope skin,
clad in bark and antelope skin, as if blazing with splendor, // VamPSm 3.9 //
blazing like the sacrificial fire, with the fragrance of oblation-ghee before him,
their father, devoted to self-study, in form like embodied fire, // VamPSm 3.10 //
the lord, teacher of gods and <s>Asuras</s>, a speaker of <s>Brahman</s> and truth,
<s>Kaśyapa</s>, of blazing splendor, incomparable in <s>Brahmanical</s> glory, // VamPSm 3.11 //
who is the creator of all worlds, the supreme lord of creatures,
who is the third <s>Prajāpati</s> by his own special nature. // VamPSm 3.12 //

children.text: atha praṇamya te vīrāḥ sahādityā surarṣabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then those heroes, the foremost gods, together with <s>Aditi</s>, having bowed down,

children.text: ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve brahmāṇamiva mānasāḥ // VamPSm_3.13 //
children.translated_text: all spoke with joined palms, like the mind-born sons (addressing) <s>Brahmā</s>: // VamPSm 3.13 //
'<s>Bali</s>, the <s>Daitya</s>, unconquerable in battle by <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), superior in strength —

children.text: tasmād vidhatta naḥ śreyo devānāṃ puṣṭivardhanam // VamPSm_3.14 //
children.translated_text: therefore, devise for us something auspicious, that which increases the prosperity of the gods.' // VamPSm 3.14 //

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣāṃ putrāṇāṃ kaśyapaḥ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of his sons, the lord <s>Kaśyapa</s>,

children.text: akarod gamane buddhi brahmalokāya lokakṛt // VamPSm_3.15 //
children.translated_text: the creator of worlds, set his mind to going to <s>Brahmaloka</s>. // VamPSm 3.15 //
<s>Kaśyapa</s> said:
'O <s>Śakra</s>, let us go to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, supremely wondrous;

children.text: tathā parājayaṃ sarve brahmaṇaḥ khyātumudyatāḥ // VamPSm_3.16 //
children.translated_text: likewise, all (of us), prepared to declare the defeat to <s>Brahmā</s>.' // VamPSm 3.16 //
Then the gods with <s>Aditi</s> came to the hermitage of <s>Kāśyapa</s>;
they set out for the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, frequented by hosts of great sages. // VamPSm 3.17 //
Those (gods) of excellent radiance arrived in a moment at <s>Brahmaloka</s>,
those of great might, in divine wish-fulfilling chariots, each according to their rank. // VamPSm 3.18 //
Wishing to see <s>Brahmā</s>, the imperishable mass of austerities,

children.text: adhyagacchanta vistīrṇā brahmaṇaḥ paramāṃ sabhām // VamPSm_3.19 //
children.translated_text: they reached the vast, supreme assembly hall of <s>Brahmā</s>. // VamPSm 3.19 //
Sweet with the songs of bees, resounding with the chants of <s>Sāman</s> singers,
bringing welfare, destroying enemies — seeing it, they rejoiced. // VamPSm 3.20 //
The <s>Ṛg</s>-verses, recited by the foremost of the <s>Bahvṛca</s>s, with their <s>krama</s>, <s>pada</s>, and syllables,
the tigers among gods heard, while the rituals were being performed. // VamPSm 3.21 //
Those who knew the science of sacrifice and the <s>Vedas</s>, those who knew the <s>pada</s> and <s>krama</s> (recitation methods),

children.text: svareṇa paramarṣiṇāṃ sā babhūva praṇāditā // VamPSm_3.22 //
children.translated_text: by the chanting of the supreme sages, that (hall) was filled with sound. // VamPSm 3.22 //
By those who knew the praises of sacrifice, by twice-born versed in phonetics (<s>śikṣā</s>),
by those who knew the meanings of the meters (<s>chandas</s>), by those skilled in all sciences — // VamPSm 3.23 //
led by the foremost <s>Lokāyatikas</s>, they heard the chanting;

children.text: tatra tatra ca viprendrā niyatāḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ // VamPSm_3.24 //
children.translated_text: and in various places, the foremost among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, disciplined and of praised vows, // VamPSm 3.24 //
devoted to <s>japa</s> (recitation) and <s>homa</s> (oblation) — the foremost sons of <s>Kaśyapa</s> beheld (them).

children.text: tasyāṃ sabhāyāmāste sa brahma lokapitāmahaḥ // VamPSm_3.25 //
children.translated_text: In that assembly sat <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather of the world, // VamPSm 3.25 //
the glorious teacher of gods and <s>Asuras</s>, with his knowledge and Vedic <s>māyā</s>;

children.text: upāsanta ca tatraiva prajānāṃ patayaḥ prabhum // VamPSm_3.26 //
children.translated_text: and there they worshipped the lord, the lords of creatures. // VamPSm 3.26 //
<s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Pracetas</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, the best of twice-born,
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Nārada</s>, // VamPSm 3.27 //
the sciences, the atmosphere, wind, fire, water, radiance,

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhastathaiva ca // VamPSm_3.28 //
children.translated_text: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, // VamPSm 3.28 //
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Vikāra</s> (transformation), and whatever other great cause (exists),
the four <s>Vedas</s> with their limbs and sub-limbs, and the lord of the world, // VamPSm 3.29 //

children.text: nayāśca kratavaścaiva saṅkalpaḥ prāṇa eva ca /
children.translated_text: the polities and the sacrifices, will (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), and life-breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) itself —

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ svayaṃbhuvamupāsate // VamPSm_3.30 //
children.translated_text: these and many others worship the self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>). // VamPSm 3.30 //

children.text: artho dharmaśya kāmaśca krodho harṣaśca nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Wealth (<s>Artha</s>), <s>Dharma</s>, Desire (<s>Kāma</s>), Anger (<s>Krodha</s>), and Joy (<s>Harṣa</s>) perpetually,
<s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, and <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), // VamPSm 3.31 //
<s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Rāhu</s>, and all the planets were stationed there,

children.text: maruto viśvakarmā ca vasavaśca dvijottamāḥ // VamPSm_3.32 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, and the best of twice-born, // VamPSm 3.32 //
the Sun (<s>Divākara</s>) and the Moon (<s>Soma</s>), Day and Night as well,

children.text: arddhamāsāśca māsāśca ṛtavaḥ ṣaṭ ca saṃsthitāḥ // VamPSm_3.33 //
children.translated_text: the fortnights and the months, and the six seasons were established there. // VamPSm 3.33 //

children.text: tāṃ praviśya sabhāṃ divyāṃ brahmaṇaḥ sarvakāmikām /
children.translated_text: Having entered that divine assembly of <s>Brahmā</s>, fulfilling all desires,
<s>Kaśyapa</s>, the best of upholders of <s>dharma</s>, together with the gods, his sons, // VamPSm 3.34 //
(beheld the assembly) consisting entirely of splendor, divine, frequented by hosts of <s>Brahmarṣis</s>,

children.text: brāhmyā śriyā sevyamānām acintyāṃ vigataklamām // VamPSm_3.35 //
children.translated_text: attended by the glory of <s>Brahmā</s>, inconceivable, free from fatigue. // VamPSm 3.35 //
Having seen <s>Brahmā</s>, all of them, seated on the supreme seat,

children.text: śirobhiḥ praṇatā devaṃ devā brahmarṣibhiḥ saha // VamPSm_3.36 //
children.translated_text: The gods, together with the <s>Brahmarṣis</s> (Brahmin sages), bowed their heads to the Lord. // VamPSm_3.36 //
Then, having bowed at the feet of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), restrained (in mind),
they were freed from all sins, peaceful, and purged of all impurity. // VamPSm_3.37 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu tān surān sarvān kaśyapena sahāgatān /
children.translated_text: Seeing all those gods who had arrived together with <s>Kaśyapa</s>,

children.text: āha brahma mahātejā devānāṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ // VamPSm_3.38 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> of great splendor, the lord and master of the gods, spoke. // VamPSm_3.38 //
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: yadarthamiha saṃprāpta bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi /
children.translated_text: The purpose for which all of you have come here —
I too have been thinking about that very purpose from the beginning, O mighty ones. // VamPSm_4.1 //

children.text: bhaviṣyati ca vaḥ sarvaṃ kāṅkṣitaṃ yat surottamāḥ /
children.translated_text: All your desires shall be fulfilled, O best of gods;
there shall be one who will be the conqueror of <s>Bali</s>, the foremost of the <s>Dānavas</s>. // VamPSm_4.2 //

children.text: na kevalaṃ surādīnāṃ gatirmama sa viśvakṛt /
children.translated_text: Not merely the refuge of the gods and others — that creator of the universe is mine (too);

children.text: trailokyasyāpi netā ca devānāmapi sa prabhuḥ // VamPSm_4.3 //
children.translated_text: he is the leader of the three worlds and the lord of the gods as well. // VamPSm_4.3 //
He who is the lord of all worlds, the eternal lord of the universe,
this primordial one — they always call him the first god, the eternal one. // VamPSm_4.4 //
Even the great-souled gods do not know who he truly is;

children.text: devānāsmān śrutiṃ viśvaṃ sa vetti puruṣottamaḥ // VamPSm_4.5 //
children.translated_text: he, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), knows the gods, us, scripture, and the entire universe. // VamPSm_4.5 //

children.text: tasyaiva tu prasādena pravakṣye paramāṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: By his grace alone, I shall declare the supreme destination,

children.text: yatra yogaṃ samāsthāya tapaścarati duścaram // VamPSm_4.6 //
children.translated_text: where he, having established himself in <s>yoga</s>, performs difficult austerities. // VamPSm_4.6 //
On the northern shore of the Milk Ocean, in the northern direction, the creator of the universe —
the wise call that supreme abode '<s>Amṛta</s>' (the Immortal). // VamPSm_4.7 //
Go there, O you of well-praised vows, and through austerities,
having reached the abode called <s>Amṛta</s>, perform difficult austerities. // VamPSm_4.8 //
Then you shall hear the well-proclaimed (voice), smooth and deep in resonance,
like the sound of a cloud full of water at the end of summer. // VamPSm_4.9 //
Reddish, with well-formed syllables, delightful, fearless, always auspicious —
the speech of the supreme refinement of those who speak the truth of <s>Brahman</s>. // VamPSm_4.10 //
Divine, truth-bestowing, true, destroying all impurity —
(the speech) of that supreme god of all gods, that self-realized being. // VamPSm_4.11 //
Upon the completion of his vow, at the conclusion of his yogic observance,

children.text: amoghaṃ tasya devasya viśvatejo mahātmanaḥ // VamPSm_4.12 //
children.translated_text: the unfailing splendor of that great-souled god, whose radiance pervades all — // VamPSm_4.12 //

children.text: kasya kiṃ vo varaṃ devā dadāmi varadaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "What boon shall I give to whom among you, O gods? I stand ready as the giver of boons."
"Welcome to you, O best of gods, who have come into my presence." // VamPSm_4.13 //
Then <s>Aditi</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s> should receive the boon at that time,

children.text: praṇamya śirasā pādau tasmai devāya dhīmate // VamPSm_4.14 //
children.translated_text: having bowed with their heads at the feet of that wise god. // VamPSm_4.14 //

children.text: bhagavāneva naḥ putro bhavatviti prasīda naḥ /
children.translated_text: "May the Lord himself become our son — be pleased with us."

children.text: uktaśca parayā vācā tathāstvati sa vakṣyati // VamPSm_4.15 //
children.translated_text: And he, addressed with the supreme word, shall say "So be it." // VamPSm_4.15 //

children.text: devā bruvanti te sarve kasyapo 'ditireva ca /
children.translated_text: The gods all speak, and <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Aditi</s> as well:

children.text: tathāstviti surāḥ sarve praṇamya śirasā prabhum /
children.translated_text: "So be it!" — and all the gods, having bowed their heads to the Lord,

children.text: śvetadvīpaṃ samuddiśya gatāḥ saumyadiśaṃ prati // VamPSm_4.16 //
children.translated_text: departed toward the <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (White Island), in the northern direction. // VamPSm_4.16 //
They quickly arrived at the Milk Ocean, the lord of rivers,
as directed by the Lord <s>Brahmā</s>, the speaker of truth. // VamPSm_4.17 //

children.text: te krāntāḥ sāgarān sarvān parvatāṃśca sakānanān /
children.translated_text: They crossed all the oceans and mountains with their forests,

children.text: nadīśca vividhā divyāḥ pṛthivyāṃ te suroktamāḥ // VamPSm_4.18 //
children.translated_text: and various divine rivers on the earth, O best of gods. // VamPSm_4.18 //
They beheld a terrible darkness, devoid of all living beings,
without light, without boundaries, enveloped on all sides by darkness. // VamPSm_4.19 //
Having reached the abode called <s>Amṛta</s>, together with the great-souled <s>Kaśyapa</s>,

children.text: dīkṣitāḥ kāmadaṃ divyaṃ vrataṃ varṣa sahasrakam // VamPSm_4.20 //
children.translated_text: they were initiated into the divine, wish-fulfilling vow for a thousand years. // VamPSm_4.20 //
For the purpose of propitiating the Lord of gods, that wise one devoted to <s>yoga</s>,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the god, the thousand-eyed one, for (their) welfare. // VamPSm_4.21 //
Through celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), silence (<s>mauna</s>), standing posture and the heroic posture (<s>vīrāsana</s>),

children.text: krameṇa ca surāḥ sarve tapa ugraṃ samāsthitāḥ // VamPSm_4.22 //
children.translated_text: progressively, all the gods undertook fierce austerities. // VamPSm_4.22 //
There, the venerable <s>Kaśyapa</s>, for the purpose of propitiating the great-souled one,

children.text: udīrayata vedoktaṃ yamāhuḥ paramaṃ stavam // VamPSm_4.23 //
children.translated_text: recited the Veda-prescribed (hymn), which they call the supreme praise (<s>stava</s>). // VamPSm_4.23 //
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Saromāhātmya of the Śrī <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
kaśyapa uvāca
namo 'stu te devadeva ekaśṛṅga vṛṣārcce sindhuvṛṣa vṛṣākape suravṛṣa anādisaṃbhava rudra kapila viṣvaksena sarvabhūtapate dhruva dharmadharma vaikuṇṭha vṛṣāvarta anādimadhyanidhana dhanañjaya śuciśravaḥ pṛśnitejaḥ nijaya (5) amṛteśaya sanātana tridhāma tuṣita mahātattva lokanātha padmanābha viriñce bahurūpa akṣaya akṣara havyabhuja khaṇḍaparaśo śatakra muñjakeśa haṃsa mahādakṣiṇa hṛṣīkeśa sūkṣma mahāniyamadhara viraja lokapratiṣṭha arūpa agraja dharmaja dharmanābha (10) gabhastinābha śatakratunābha candraratha sūryatejaḥ samudravāsaḥ ajaḥ sahasraśiraḥ sahasrapāda adomukha mahāpuruṣa puruṣottama sahasrabāho sahasramūrte sahasrāsya paruṣottama sahasrabāho sahasramūrte sahasrāsya sahasrasaṃbhava sahasrasattvaṃ
tvamāhuḥ /
puṣpahāsa carama tvameva vauṣaṭ (15) vaṣaṭkāraṃ tvāmāhuragrayaṃ makheṣu prāśitāraṃ sahasradhāraṃ ca bhuśca bhuvaśca svaśca tvameva vedavedya brahmaśaya brāhmaṇapriya tvameva dyaurasi mātariśvāsi dharmo 'si hotā potā mantā netā homahetus tvameva agraya viśvadhāmnā tvameva digbhiḥ subhāṇḍa (20) ijyo 'si sumedho 'si samidhastvameva matir gatir dātā tvamasi /
mokṣo 'si yogo 'si /
sṛjasi /
dhātā paramayajño 'si somo 'si dīkṣito 'si dakṣiṇāsi viśvamasi /
sthavira hiraṇyanāma nārāyaṇa trinayana ādityavarma ādityatejaḥ mahāpuruṣa (25) puruṣottama ādidedeva suvikrama prabhākara śaṃbho svayaṃbho bhūtādiḥ mahābhūto 'si viśvabhūta viśvaṃ tvameva viśvagoptāsi pavitramasi viśvabhava ūrdhvakarma amṛta divaspate vācaspate ghṛtārce anantakarma vaṃśa pragvaṃśa viśvapāstvameva varārthināṃ varado 'si tvam /
(30) caturbhiśca caturbhiśca dvābhyāṃ pañjabhireva ca /
hūyate ca punardvābhyāṃ tubhyaṃ hotrātmane namaḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Kaśyapa</s> said:
Salutations to you, O God of gods! O <s>Ekaśṛṅga</s> (single-horned), <s>Vṛṣārcya</s> (worshipped by the righteous), <s>Sindhuvṛṣa</s> (bull of the oceans), <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> (monkey of righteousness), <s>Suravṛṣa</s> (bull of the gods), O one of beginningless origin, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, lord of all beings, <s>Dhruva</s> (steadfast), <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Adharma</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, <s>Vṛṣāvarta</s> (the whirlwind of righteousness), O one without beginning, middle, or end, <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (winner of wealth), <s>Śuciśravas</s> (of pure fame), <s>Pṛśnitejas</s> (of dappled splendor), <s>Nijaya</s> (5), O one who rests on the immortal (<s>Amṛteśaya</s>), O eternal one, O one of three abodes (<s>Tridhāman</s>), <s>Tuṣita</s> (the satisfied), <s>Mahātattva</s> (great principle), Lord of the world, <s>Padmanābha</s> (lotus-naveled), <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), O one of many forms, O imperishable one, O immutable one, O consumer of oblations, <s>Khaṇḍaparaśu</s> (wielder of the broken axe), <s>Śatakra</s> (of hundred powers), <s>Muñjakeśa</s> (of muñja-grass hair), <s>Haṃsa</s> (swan), <s>Mahādakṣiṇa</s> (of great sacrificial gifts), <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (lord of the senses), O subtle one, O great observer of disciplines, <s>Viraja</s> (stainless), O support of the world, O formless one, O firstborn, O born of <s>dharma</s>, <s>Dharmanābha</s> (10), <s>Gabhastinābha</s> (of ray-like navel), <s>Śatakratunābha</s> (navel of a hundred sacrifices), <s>Candraratha</s> (moon-charioteer), of the splendor of the sun, <s>Samudravāsas</s> (ocean-clad), O unborn one, O thousand-headed, thousand-footed, O downward-facing one, O great person (<s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>), O supreme person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), O thousand-armed, O thousand-formed, O thousand-faced, O one of thousand origins, O one of thousand essences — they call you thus.
You are the <s>Puṣpahāsa</s> (flower-laugh), the ultimate — you alone are <s>Vauṣaṭ</s>! (15) They call you the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call), the foremost in sacrifices, the <s>Prāśitṛ</s> (sacrificial taster), the thousand-streamed, and <s>Bhuḥ</s> and <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> and <s>Svaḥ</s> — you alone are that. O one knowable through the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>Vedavedya</s>), O one who rests in <s>Brahman</s>, O beloved of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — you alone are heaven, you are <s>Mātariśvan</s> (wind), you are <s>Dharma</s>, you are the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker), the <s>Potṛ</s> (purifier), the <s>Mantṛ</s> (counselor), the <s>Netṛ</s> (leader), the cause of oblation — you alone are the foremost, by universal abode — you alone are (worshipped) by the directions, O fair-shelled one (20), you are to be worshipped, you are of good intellect, you are the kindling sticks — you alone are thought, goal, and giver — you are.
You are <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), you are <s>yoga</s>.
You create.
You are the ordainer, the supreme sacrifice, you are <s>Soma</s>, you are the one initiated (<s>dīkṣita</s>), you are the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), you are the universe.
O <s>Sthavira</s> (elder), <s>Hiraṇyanāman</s> (golden-named), <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Trinayana</s> (three-eyed), <s>Ādityavarman</s> (sun-armored), of the splendor of the sun, O great person (25), O supreme person, O primordial god, O <s>Suvikrama</s> (of noble strides), O <s>Prabhākara</s> (radiance-maker), O <s>Śaṃbhu</s> (beneficent), O <s>Svayaṃbhu</s> (self-born), you are the origin of beings, the great element — you are the universal being, you are the universe itself, you are the protector of the universe, you are the purifier, O source of the universe, O one of upward action, O immortal one, O lord of heaven, O lord of speech, O one worshipped with ghee, O one of infinite action, O <s>Vaṃśa</s> (lineage), <s>Pragvaṃśa</s> (primordial lineage), you alone are the protector of the universe, you are the giver of boons to those who desire boons.
(30) With four and four, with two, with five, and again with two — the oblation is offered to you. Salutations to you, whose self is the <s>Hotra</s> (oblation)!
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Saromāhātmya of the Śrī <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>.
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, having heard this supreme praise,
uttered by the chief of the twice-born, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, who knows <s>Brahman</s>, // VamPSm_6.1 //
spoke a word that was well-formed, with full and clear syllables,

children.text: śrīmān prītamanā devo yadvadet prabhurīśvaraḥ // VamPSm_6.2 //
children.translated_text: pleased in mind, the glorious Lord — what the master and ruler would say: // VamPSm_6.2 //

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇudhvaṃ bhadraṃ vo varado 'smi surottamāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Choose a boon — may good fortune be yours! I am the giver of boons, O best of gods."
<s>Kaśyapa</s> said:

children.text: prīto 'si naḥ suraśreṣṭha sarveṣāmeva niścayaḥ // VamPSm_6.3 //
children.translated_text: "You are pleased with us, O best of gods — this is the conviction of all of us. // VamPSm_6.3 //
Be the younger brother of <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the increaser of joy among kinsmen,

children.text: adityā api ca śrīmān bhagavānasta vai sutaḥ // VamPSm_6.4 //
children.translated_text: and the glorious Lord, be the son of <s>Aditi</s> as well. // VamPSm_6.4 //
<s>Aditi</s>, the mother of the gods, this very supreme purpose —

children.text: putrārthaṃ varadaṃ prāha bhagavantaṃ varārthinī // VamPSm_6.5 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of a son, she, seeking a boon, spoke to the Lord, the giver of boons. // VamPSm_6.5 //
The gods said:
"For the highest good of all the divinities, O great lord,

children.text: trātā bhartā ca dātā ca śaraṇaṃ bhava naḥ sadā // VamPSm_6.6 //
children.translated_text: be our protector, sustainer, giver, and eternal refuge." // VamPSm_6.6 //
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s> addressed the gods and <s>Kaśyapa</s> as well:
"All those who will be enemies of all of you —

children.text: muhūrtamapi te sarve na sthāsyanti mamāgrataḥ // VamPSm_6.7 //
children.translated_text: they shall not stand before me even for a moment. // VamPSm_6.7 //
Having slain all the hosts of <s>Asuras</s>, (I shall restore) the foremost shares of the sacrifice,

children.text: havyādāṃśca surān sarvān kavyādāṃśca pitṛnapi // VamPSm_6.8 //
children.translated_text: and shall make all the gods receivers of <s>havya</s> (oblations) and all the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors) receivers of <s>kavya</s> (funeral offerings). // VamPSm_6.8 //
I shall accomplish this, O best of gods, by the supreme act;
return by the same route by which you came, O best of gods." // VamPSm_6.9 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
When this was spoken by the god <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-powerful,

children.text: tataḥ prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ pūjayanti sma taṃ prabhum // VamPSm_6.10 //
children.translated_text: then, with delighted minds, they worshipped that Lord, // VamPSm_6.10 //
the great-souled <s>Viśvedevas</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Aditi</s> as well.

children.text: namaskṛtya sureśāya tasmai devāya raṃhasā // VamPSm_6.11 //
children.translated_text: Having paid obeisance to the Lord of gods, to that divine being, with fervor, // VamPSm_6.11 //
they all departed toward the eastern direction, to the great hermitage of <s>Kaśyapa</s>;

children.text: te kaśyapāśramaṃ gatvā kurukṣetravanaṃ mahāt // VamPSm_6.12 //
children.translated_text: having gone to <s>Kaśyapa</s>'s hermitage, (they entered) the great forest of <s>Kurukṣetra</s>. // VamPSm_6.12 //

children.text: prasādya hyaditiṃ tatra tapase tāṃ nyayojayan/
tha sā cacāra tapo ghoraṃ varṣāṇāmayutaṃ tadā // VamPSm_6.13 //
children.translated_text: and she performed terrible austerities for ten thousand years. // VamPSm_6.13 //
Having propitiated <s>Aditi</s> there, they set her to austerities;

children.text: tasyā nāmnā vanaṃ divyaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: In that divine forest named after her, which grants all desires, auspicious —
for the propitiation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, she lived as one who had conquered speech and subsisted on air. // VamPSm_6.14 //
Seeing her sons rejected by the <s>Daityas</s>, O best of sages,
thinking 'I am a mother whose sons are in vain,' out of dejection and out of love for <s>Hari</s>,
she praised (him) with supreme words, she who had realized the highest truth. // VamPSm_6.15 //
She bowed to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the refuge-giver, the refuge itself, who is fond of his devotees,
who is constituted of gods and <s>Daityas</s>, and whose form encompasses the beginning, middle, and end. // VamPSm_6.16 //
<s>Aditi</s> said:
Salutations to the destroyer of the suffering of created beings; salutations to the one garlanded with lotuses;
salutations to the supremely auspicious one, to the auspicious one, to the primordial creator. // VamPSm_6.17 //
Salutations to the lotus-eyed one; salutations to the lotus-naveled one;
salutations to the one from whose origin the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) arose, the self-born one. // VamPSm_6.18 //
To the beloved of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), to the self-controlled, to the one visible to the self-controlled, to the wielder of the discus,
salutations to the one who holds the lotus and the sword; salutations to the one of golden seed. // VamPSm_6.19 //
To the one who is the sacrifice of self-knowledge, to the one contemplated by <s>yogins</s>, to the <s>yogin</s>,
to the one beyond qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), to the one of distinction, to <s>Hari</s>, to the one of the form of <s>Brahman</s>. // VamPSm_6.20 //

children.text: jagacca tiṣṭhate yatra jagato yo na dṛsyate /
children.translated_text: In whom the universe abides, who is not seen by the universe —

children.text: namaḥ sthūlātisūkṣmāya tasmai devāya śārṅiḍṇe // VamPSm_6.21 //
children.translated_text: salutations to the one who is both gross and supremely subtle, to that god, the wielder of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow. // VamPSm_6.21 //

children.text: yaṃ na paśyanti paśyanto jagadapyakhilaṃ narāḥ /
children.translated_text: He whom those who see do not see, even while seeing the entire world;
he who is seen dwelling in the heart by those who do not see (the world). // VamPSm_6.22 //

children.text: bahirjyoti ralakṣyo yo lakṣyate jyotiṣaḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is the light beyond (outer) light, imperceptible — who is perceived as beyond light;
in whom, from whom, and whose is this entire universe — // VamPSm_6.23 //
to that immortal one of all worlds — salutations, salutations!

children.text: ādyaḥ prajāpatiḥ so 'pi pitṝṇāṃ paramaḥ patiḥ /
children.translated_text: He is the first <s>Prajāpati</s> (lord of creatures), the supreme lord of the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors),

children.text: patiḥ surāṇāṃ yastasmai namaḥ kṛṣṇāya vedhase // VamPSm_6.24 //
children.translated_text: the lord of the gods — salutations to that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the creator. // VamPSm_6.24 //
He from whom detachment arises through works of engagement and withdrawal,
who bestows the fruits of heaven and liberation — salutations to that wielder of the mace. // VamPSm_6.25 //
He who, even while being merely contemplated, removes all sin —
salutations to that pure one, the supreme one, <s>Hari</s> of sacred intellect. // VamPSm_6.26 //
Those who see the foundation of all, the lord, the unborn, the imperishable —

children.text: na punarjanmamaraṇaṃ prāpnuvanti namāmi tam // VamPSm_6.27 //
children.translated_text: they do not again attain birth and death — I bow to him. // VamPSm_6.27 //
He who is the sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), who is worshipped by those devoted to sacrifice, who abides in sacrifice —

children.text: taṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ namāmi prabhumīśvaram // VamPSm_6.28 //
children.translated_text: I bow to that <s>Yajñapuruṣa</s> (the Person of sacrifice), <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord and master. // VamPSm_6.28 //
He who is sung in all the <s>Vedas</s> by the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>, the refuge of the wise —

children.text: yastasmai vedavedyāya nityāya viṣṇave namaḥ // VamPSm_6.29 //
children.translated_text: to that eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is to be known through the <s>Vedas</s> — salutations. // VamPSm_6.29 //
From whom the universe has arisen, in whom it shall dissolve,
to him who is the origin and support of the universe — salutations to that great-souled one. // VamPSm_6.30 //
By whom all that is moving and non-moving, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, is pervaded —
I bow to that <s>Upendra</s> who is elevated by the web of <s>māyā</s> (illusion). // VamPSm_6.31 //
He who, abiding here in the form of water, sustains all, the Lord,

children.text: viśvaṃ viśvapatiṃ viṣṇuṃ taṃ namāmi prajāpatim // VamPSm_6.32 //
children.translated_text: the universe, the lord of the universe — I bow to that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of creatures. // VamPSm_6.32 //
He who, in the form of the sun, destroys embodied darkness made of <s>asuras</s> (demons),

children.text: rātrijaṃ sūryarūpī ca tamupendraṃ namāmyaham // VamPSm_6.33 //
children.translated_text: and that which is born of night — I bow to that <s>Upendra</s>. // VamPSm_6.33 //
He whose two eyes are the moon and the sun, who constantly beholds

children.text: paśyataḥ karma satataṃ tamupendraṃ namāmyaham // VamPSm_6.34 //
children.translated_text: the auspicious and inauspicious deeds of all the worlds — I bow to that <s>Upendra</s>. // VamPSm_6.34 //
In whom, the lord of all, all this that has been spoken by me is true,

children.text: nānṛtaṃ tamajaṃ viṣṇuṃ namāmi prabhavāvyayam // VamPSm_6.35 //
children.translated_text: and nothing is false — I bow to that unborn <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the imperishable source. // VamPSm_6.35 //
If this that I have spoken is true, and furthermore, O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: satyena tena sakalāḥ pūryantāṃ me manorathāḥ // VamPSm_6.36 //
children.translated_text: then by that truth, may all my desires be fulfilled. // VamPSm_6.36 //
Thus ends the sixth chapter in the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> of the <s>Śrī Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ stuto 'tha bhagavān vāsudeva uvāca tām /
children.translated_text: Thus praised, the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> then spoke to her,

children.text: adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāḥ saṃdarśane sthitaḥ // VamPSm_7.1 //
children.translated_text: invisible to all beings, yet standing in her sight. // VamPSm_7.1 //
The Blessed Lord said:
O <s>Aditi</s>, the desires that you wish and long for,

children.text: tāṃstvaṃ prāpyasi dharmajñe matprasādānna saṃśayaḥ // VamPSm_7.2 //
children.translated_text: you shall obtain them, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, by my grace — there is no doubt. // VamPSm_7.2 //

children.text: śṛṇu tvaṃ ca mahābhāge varo yaste hṛti sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hear, O greatly fortunate one, the boon that is fixed in your heart;

children.text: maddarśanaṃ hi viphalaṃ na kadācid bhaviṣyati // VamPSm_7.3 //
children.translated_text: my appearance shall never be fruitless. // VamPSm_7.3 //

children.text: yaśceha tvadvane sthitvā trirātraṃ vai kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: And whoever, staying in your grove, observes a three-night [vow],

children.text: sarve kāmāḥ samṛdhyante manasā yānihecchati // VamPSm_7.4 //
children.translated_text: all desires that he wishes in his mind shall be fulfilled. // VamPSm_7.4 //

children.text: dūrastho 'pi vanaṃ yastu adityāḥ smarate naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Even a man who, from afar, remembers the grove of <s>Aditi</s>,

children.text: so 'pi yāti paraṃ sthānaṃ kiṃ punarnivasan naraḥ // VamPSm_7.5 //
children.translated_text: he too attains the supreme abode — how much more so one who dwells there! // VamPSm_7.5 //

children.text: yaśceha brāhmaṇān pañca trīn vā dvāvekameva vā /
children.translated_text: And whoever here feeds five, or three, or two, or even one <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: bhojayecchraddhayā yuktāḥ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim // VamPSm_7.6 //
children.translated_text: endowed with faith — he attains the supreme state. // VamPSm_7.6 //
<s>Aditi</s> said:

children.text: yadi deva prasannastvaṃ bhaktyā me bhaktavatsala /
children.translated_text: If, O Lord, you are pleased with my devotion, O one who is fond of devotees,
then let my son <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) become the sovereign of the three worlds. // VamPSm_7.7 //
His kingdom has been seized and his share of the sacrifices has been taken by the <s>asuras</s>;

children.text: tvayi prasanne parada tat prāpnotu suto mama // VamPSm_7.8 //
children.translated_text: since you are pleased, O giver of boons, may my son regain that. // VamPSm_7.8 //

children.text: hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ na duḥkhāya mama putrasya keśava /
children.translated_text: The loss of the kingdom does not cause me grief for my son, O <s>Keśava</s>;

children.text: prapannadāyavibhraṃśo bādhāṃ me kurute hṛti // VamPSm_7.9 //
children.translated_text: the fall of those who have sought refuge — that is what afflicts my heart. // VamPSm_7.9 //
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: kṛtaḥ prasādo hi mayā tava devi yathepsitam /
children.translated_text: I have already bestowed my grace upon you, O goddess, as you desired;

children.text: svāṃśena caiva te garbhe saṃbhaviṣyāmi kaśyapāt // VamPSm_7.10 //
children.translated_text: and with a portion of myself, I shall be born in your womb from <s>Kaśyapa</s>. // VamPSm_7.10 //
Born from your womb, I shall destroy those who are your enemies —

children.text: tānahaṃ ca haniṣyāmi nivṛttā bhava nandini // VamPSm_7.11 //
children.translated_text: be free from care, O blessed one. // VamPSm_7.11 //
<s>Aditi</s> said:
Be gracious, O lord of the gods of gods! Salutations to you, O creator of the universe!
I am unable to bear you in my womb, O Lord, O <s>Keśava</s>,
you in whom everything is established, you who are the womb of the universe, the Lord. // VamPSm_7.12 //

children.text: ahaṃ tvāṃ ca vahiṣyāmi ātmānaṃ caiva nandini /
children.translated_text: [The Lord said:] I shall bear both myself and you, O blessed one,

children.text: na ca pīḍāṃ kariṣyāmi svasti te 'stu vrajāmyaham // VamPSm_7.13 //
children.translated_text: and I shall not cause you pain. May it be well with you — I depart. // VamPSm_7.13 //
Having spoken thus, when the god disappeared, <s>Aditi</s> conceived the embryo.

children.text: garbhasthite tataḥ khṛṣṇe cacāla saralā kṣitiḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) was established in the womb, the steady earth trembled,

children.text: cakampire mahāśailā jagmuḥ kṣobhaṃ mahābdhayaḥ // VamPSm_7.14 //
children.translated_text: the great mountains shook, and the great oceans were agitated. // VamPSm_7.14 //
Wherever <s>Aditi</s> went and placed her exalted step,
there the earth bowed down from the weight, O best of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. // VamPSm_7.15 //
And when <s>Madhusūdana</s> was established in the womb, of all the <s>Daityas</s>
there was a diminution of splendor, as had been foretold by <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). // VamPSm_7.16 //
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> of the <s>Śrī Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Seeing the <s>asuras</s> bereft of splendor, the lord of the <s>asuras</s>,
<s>Bali</s>, questioned <s>Prahlāda</s>, his own grandfather. // VamPSm_8.1 //
<s>Bali</s> said:

children.text: tāta nistejaso daityā nirdagdhā iva vahninā /
children.translated_text: Grandfather, the <s>Daityas</s> are bereft of splendor, as if scorched by fire;
why are they all suddenly today as if struck by the rod of <s>Brahmā</s>? // VamPSm_8.2 //

children.text: duriṣṭaṃ kiṃ tu daityānāṃ ki kṛtyā vidhinirmitā /
children.translated_text: Has some inauspicious omen befallen the <s>Daityas</s>? Has some sorcery fashioned by fate
arisen for their destruction, by which the <s>asuras</s> are bereft of splendor? // VamPSm_8.3 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Thus questioned by his grandson, the best of <s>asuras</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: ciraṃ dhyātvā jagādedamasuraṃ taṃ tadā balim // VamPSm_8.4 //
children.translated_text: having pondered for a long time, spoke these words to that <s>asura</s> <s>Bali</s>: // VamPSm_8.4 //
<s>Prahlāda</s> said:
The mountains tremble, the earth suddenly abandons its stability,

children.text: sadyaḥ samudrāḥ kṣubhitā daityā nistejasaḥ kṛtāḥ // VamPSm_8.5 //
children.translated_text: the oceans are agitated, and the <s>Daityas</s> have been rendered bereft of splendor. // VamPSm_8.5 //

children.text: sūryodaye yathā pūrvaṃ tathā gacchanti na grahāḥ /
children.translated_text: The planets do not move as before at sunrise,

children.text: devānāṃ ca parā lakṣmīḥ karaṇenānumīyate // VamPSm_8.6 //
children.translated_text: and the supreme prosperity of the gods is inferred by these signs. // VamPSm_8.6 //
This is a great cause, O mighty-armed one, O lord of the <s>Dānavas</s>;

children.text: na hyalpamiti mantavyaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ kathañcana // VamPSm_8.7 //
children.translated_text: it should not be considered trivial by you in any way. // VamPSm_8.7 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Having spoken thus to the lord of the <s>Dānavas</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, that best of <s>asuras</s>,

children.text: atyarthabhakto deveśaṃ jagāma manasā harim // VamPSm_8.8 //
children.translated_text: supremely devoted, went with his mind to <s>Hari</s>, the lord of the gods. // VamPSm_8.8 //
Having set his mind upon the path of meditation, the <s>asura</s> <s>Prahlāda</s>

children.text: vicārayāmāsa tato yathā devo janārdanaḥ // VamPSm_8.9 //
children.translated_text: then contemplated where the god <s>Janārdana</s> was. // VamPSm_8.9 //
<s>Prahlāda</s> saw in the womb of <s>Aditi</s> one in the form of a dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>),
and within him the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s>, // VamPSm_8.10 //
the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Uragas</s> (serpents), and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: virocanaṃ ca tanayaṃ baliṃ cāsuranāyakam // VamPSm_8.11 //
children.translated_text: and his [own] son <s>Virocana</s>, and <s>Bali</s> the leader of the <s>asuras</s>, // VamPSm_8.11 //
<s>Jambha</s>, <s>Kujambha</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, and other <s>asuras</s>,

children.text: ātmānamurvīṃ gaganaṃ vāyuṃ vāri hutāśanam // VamPSm_8.12 //
children.translated_text: himself, the earth, the sky, the wind, water, and fire, // VamPSm_8.12 //
oceans, mountains, rivers, islands, lakes, animals, and the earth,
birds, humans, and all creeping creatures as well, // VamPSm_8.13 //
the creator of all the worlds, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) himself,
the planets, constellations, and stars, and <s>Dakṣa</s> and the other lords of creatures. // VamPSm_8.14 //
Beholding all this, filled with wonder, returning to his natural state after a moment,

children.text: prahlādaḥ prāha daityendraṃ baliṃ vairociniṃ tataḥ // VamPSm_8.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prahlāda</s> then spoke to the lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Bali</s> the son of <s>Virocana</s>: // VamPSm_8.15 //
All of that has been ascertained by me — the reason for which
this diminution of splendor has arisen for you — hear it in full. // VamPSm_8.16 //
The god of gods, the source of the universe, unborn yet the first-born of the universe,
without beginning yet the beginning of the universe, the most excellent, the boon-giver, <s>Hari</s>, // VamPSm_8.17 //
the supreme among the higher and the lower, the refuge of the highest and the lowest,
the Lord, the standard of measures, the teacher of the teacher of the seven worlds —

children.text: sthitiṃ kartu jagannāthaḥ so 'cintyo garbhatāṃ gataḥ // VamPSm_8.18 //
children.translated_text: that inconceivable lord of the universe has entered the womb to maintain [cosmic] order. // VamPSm_8.18 //
The Lord, supreme among lords, highest among the highest, without beginning, middle, or end, the Blessed, the infinite —
that great-souled one, alone, has descended as the son of <s>Aditi</s> to protect the three worlds with a portion [of himself]. // VamPSm_8.19 //

children.text: na yasya rudro na ca padmayonirnendro na sūryendumarīcimiśrāḥ /
children.translated_text: He whose true nature neither <s>Rudra</s>, nor the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), nor <s>Indra</s>, nor the sun, moon, and stars together,

children.text: jānanti daityādhipa yatsvarūpaṃ sa vāsudevaḥ kalayāvatīrṇaḥ // VamPSm_8.20 //
children.translated_text: can know, O lord of the <s>Daityas</s> — that <s>Vāsudeva</s> has descended with a fraction [of himself]. // VamPSm_8.20 //

children.text: yamakṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti viśanti yaṃ jñānavidhūtapāpāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whom the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s> call the Imperishable, whom those whose sins are purified by knowledge enter,

children.text: yasmin praviṣṭā na purarbhavanti taṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇamāmi devam // VamPSm_8.21 //
children.translated_text: and entering whom they are not born again — I bow to that <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the god. // VamPSm_8.21 //
From whom all beings come forth, as waves ceaselessly [arise] from water,

children.text: layaṃ ca yasmin pralaye prayānti taṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇato 'smyacintyam // VamPSm_8.22 //
children.translated_text: and in whom they go to dissolution at the time of <s>pralaya</s> (cosmic dissolution) — I bow to that inconceivable <s>Vāsudeva</s>. // VamPSm_8.22 //

children.text: na yasya rūpaṃ na balaṃ prabhāvo na ca pratāpaḥ paramasya puṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whose form, strength, might, and valor, of the Supreme Being,

children.text: vijñāyate sarvapitāmahādyaistaṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇamāmi nityam // VamPSm_8.23 //
children.translated_text: are not known by all the grandfathers (<s>Brahmā</s> and others) — I bow eternally to that <s>Vāsudeva</s>. // VamPSm_8.23 //

children.text: rūpasya cakṣurgrahaṇe tvageṣā sparśagrahitrī rasanā rasasya /
children.translated_text: The eye is for grasping form, the skin is the grasper of touch, the tongue for taste,

children.text: ghrāṇaṃ ca gandhagrahaṇe niyuktaṃ na ghrāṇacakṣuḥ śravaṇādi tasya // VamPSm_8.24 //
children.translated_text: the nose is appointed for grasping smell — but neither nose, eye, nor ear [can grasp] Him. // VamPSm_8.24 //

children.text: svayaṃprakāśaḥ paramārthato yaḥ sarveśvaro veditavyaḥ sa yuktyā /
children.translated_text: He who is self-luminous in the highest truth, who should be known as the Lord of all through reasoning,

children.text: śakyaṃ tamīḍyamanaghaṃ ca devaṃ grāhyaṃ nato 'haṃ harimīśitāram // VamPSm_8.25 //
children.translated_text: to that praiseworthy, sinless god who can be grasped [only by devotion] — I bow to <s>Hari</s>, the supreme ruler. // VamPSm_8.25 //
He who, with a single tusk, lifted up this earth with its mountains that supports everything,

children.text: śete grasitvā sakalaṃ jagad yastamīḍyamīśaṃ praṇato 'smi viṣṇum // VamPSm_8.26 //
children.translated_text: and who, having swallowed the entire universe, lies in sleep — I bow to that praiseworthy lord, <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // VamPSm_8.26 //

children.text: aṃśāvatīrṇena ca yena garbhe hṛtāni tejāṃsi mahāsurāṇām /
children.translated_text: He by whom, having descended with a portion into the womb, the splendors of the great <s>asuras</s> have been taken away —
I bow to that infinite lord, the god, the axe at the tree of the entire <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). // VamPSm_8.27 //

children.text: devo jagadyonirayaṃ mahātmā sa ṣoḍśāṃśena mahāsurendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: This god, the source of the universe, the great-souled one, O great lords of the <s>asuras</s>, with a sixteenth portion

children.text: surendramāturjaṭharaṃ praviṣṭo hṛtāni vastena balaṃ vapūṃṣi // VamPSm_8.28 //
children.translated_text: has entered the womb of the mother of the lord of the gods — by that, your strength and bodies have been taken. // VamPSm_8.28 //
<s>Bali</s> said:

children.text: tāta ko 'yaṃ harirnāma yato no bhayamāgatam /
children.translated_text: Grandfather, who is this <s>Hari</s> from whom fear has come to us?

children.text: santi me śataśo daityā vāsudevabalādhikāḥ // VamPSm_8.29 //
children.translated_text: I have hundreds of <s>Daityas</s> who surpass the strength of <s>Vāsudeva</s>. // VamPSm_8.29 //
<s>Vipracitti</s>, <s>Śibi</s>, <s>Śaṅku</s>, <s>Aya</s>, and <s>Śaṅku</s> as well,
<s>Hayaśirā</s>, <s>Aśvaśirā</s>, <s>Bhaṅgakāra</s>, and <s>Mahāhanu</s>, // VamPSm_8.30 //
<s>Pratāpī</s>, <s>Praghaśa</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, and the unconquerable <s>Kukkurākṣa</s> —

children.text: ete cānye ca me santi daiteyā dānavāstathā // VamPSm_8.31 //
children.translated_text: these and others, <s>Daiteyas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>, are mine. // VamPSm_8.31 //
Of great strength and great valor, capable of bearing the burden of the earth —

children.text: eṣāmekaikaśaḥ kṛṣṇo na vīryārddhena saṃmitaḥ // VamPSm_8.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> does not equal even half the prowess of each one of them. // VamPSm_8.32 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Having heard these words of his grandson, <s>Prahlāda</s>, the best of <s>Daityas</s>,
spoke angrily to <s>Bali</s>, who disparaged <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>): // VamPSm_8.33 //
The <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s> will go to destruction,
whose king is one such as you — foolish and lacking discernment. // VamPSm_8.34 //
The god of gods, the greatly fortunate <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the unborn, the all-pervading —

children.text: tvāmṛte pāpasaṅkalpa ko 'nya evaṃ vadiṣyati // VamPSm_8.35 //
children.translated_text: who other than you, O one of sinful resolve, would speak thus [of him]? // VamPSm_8.35 //

children.text: ya ete bhavatā proktāḥ samastā daityadānavāḥ /
children.translated_text: All these <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s> that you have mentioned,
and the gods including <s>Brahmā</s>, and all manifestations down to the immovable — // VamPSm_8.36 //
you and I and this universe with its mountains, trees, rivers, and forests,
this [world] with its oceans, islands, and realms, and all that is moving and unmoving — // VamPSm_8.37 //
of that Supreme Self who is to be saluted and worshipped, who is all-pervading,
all are born from a fraction of a fraction of a portion — who would speak thus of Him? // VamPSm_8.38 //
Except you alone, who face destruction, who lack discernment,
who are foolish, uncontrolled, and transgress the commands of the elders. // VamPSm_8.39 //

children.text: śocyo 'haṃ yasya me gehe jātastava pitādhamaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am pitiable, in whose family your father, the lowest, was born,
whose son you are — one who insults the god of gods. // VamPSm_8.40 //
While my devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the destroyer of the multitudes of many cycles of <s>saṃsāra</s>, stands firm,

children.text: kṛṣṇe bhaktirahaṃ tāvadavekṣyo bhavatā na kim // VamPSm_8.41 //
children.translated_text: should I not be regarded by you [with respect]? // VamPSm_8.41 //
Dearer to me than <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is not even this body of my own self —

children.text: iti jānātyayaṃ loko bhavāṃśca ditinandana // VamPSm_8.42 //
children.translated_text: this the world knows, and you know it too, O son of <s>Diti</s>. // VamPSm_8.42 //
Though knowing that <s>Hari</s> is dearer to me than my very life-breaths,

children.text: nindāṃ karoṣi tasya tvamakurvan gauravaṃ mama // VamPSm_8.43 //
children.translated_text: you censure Him, showing no respect for me. // VamPSm_8.43 //
<s>Virocana</s> is your father, I am his father too, O <s>Bali</s>,
and my guru, the guru of all the worlds, is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>. // VamPSm_8.44 //
You censure that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who is the guru of the guru of gurus;

children.text: yasmāt tasmādihaiva tvam aiśvaryād bhrāṃśameṣyasi // VamPSm_8.45 //
children.translated_text: therefore, here itself you shall fall from your sovereignty. // VamPSm_8.45 //

children.text: sa devo jagatāṃ nātho bale prabhurjanārdanaḥ /
children.translated_text: That god, the lord of the worlds, O <s>Bali</s>, the master, <s>Janārdana</s> —

children.text: nanvahaṃ pratyavekṣyaste bhaktimānatra me guruḥ // VamPSm_8.46 //
children.translated_text: should I not be regarded by you, I who am a devotee? He is my guru here. // VamPSm_8.46 //
Even this much, by you who censure the guru of the world,

children.text: nāpekṣitastvayā yasmāt tasmācchāpaṃ dadāmi te // VamPSm_8.47 //
children.translated_text: has not been considered; therefore I give you a curse. // VamPSm_8.47 //
Just as the cutting of my head would be a grave matter, O mighty one,
so too what you have said — the insult to <s>Acyuta</s> — (is grave). Fall, deprived of your kingdom! // VamPSm_8.48 //
Just as there is no other refuge besides <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the ocean of worldly existence,
so may I soon see you bereft of your kingdom. // VamPSm_8.49 //
Thus ends the eighth chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the revered <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>.
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Having heard this terrible and unpleasant speech, the lord of the <s>Daityas</s>

children.text: prasādayāmāsa guruṃ praṇipatya punaḥ punaḥ // VamPSm_9.1 //
children.translated_text: propitiated his guru, bowing down again and again. // VamPSm_9.1 //
<s>Bali</s> said:

children.text: prasīda tāta mā kopaṃ kuru mohahate mayi /
children.translated_text: "Be pleased, O father, do not be angry with me who am struck by delusion.
These words were uttered by me, who was foolish with the arrogance of power. // VamPSm_9.2 //
I am a sinner whose wisdom has been destroyed by delusion, O best of the <s>Diti</s>'s sons.
That I have been cursed, wicked as I am — that was rightly done by you. // VamPSm_9.3 //
I shall obtain the loss of kingdom and the loss of fame — and so

children.text: viṣaṇṇo 'si yathā tāta tathaivāvinaye kṛte // VamPSm_9.4 //
children.translated_text: I am despondent, O father, just as you are (despondent) over the impropriety committed. // VamPSm_9.4 //
Sovereignty over the three worlds and lordship, or anything else, is not very difficult to obtain;

children.text: sasāre durlabhāstāta guravo ye bhavadvidhāḥ // VamPSm_9.5 //
children.translated_text: but in <s>saṃsāra</s>, gurus like you are rare, O father. // VamPSm_9.5 //

children.text: prasīda tāta mā kopaṃ kartumarhasi daityapa /
children.translated_text: Be pleased, O father; do not deem it fit to be angry, O lord of the <s>Daityas</s>.
Burned by your anger, I grieve day and night." // VamPSm_9.6 //
<s>Prahlāda</s> said:

children.text: vatsa kopena me moho janitastena te mayā /
children.translated_text: "Child, delusion was generated in me by anger, and by that (delusion)

children.text: śāpo datto vivekaśca mohenāpahṛto mama // VamPSm_9.7 //
children.translated_text: a curse was given to you by me, and my discernment was stolen by delusion. // VamPSm_9.7 //

children.text: yadi mohena me jñānaṃ nākṣiptaṃ syānmahāsura /
children.translated_text: If my knowledge had not been overthrown by delusion, O great <s>Asura</s>,

children.text: tatkathaṃ sarvagaṃ jānan hariṃ kaccicchapāmyaham // VamPSm_9.8 //
children.translated_text: then how would I, knowing <s>Hari</s> to be all-pervading, ever curse him? // VamPSm_9.8 //

children.text: yo yaḥ śāpo mayā datto bhavato 'surapuṅgava /
children.translated_text: Whatever curse has been given by me to you, O best of <s>Asuras</s>,

children.text: bhāvyametena nūnaṃ te tasmāttvaṃ mā viṣīda vai // VamPSm_9.9 //
children.translated_text: this must surely come to pass for you; therefore do not grieve. // VamPSm_9.9 //
From this day forth, be devoted to the Lord of gods,

children.text: bhavethā bhaktimānīśe sa te trātā bhaviṣyati // VamPSm_9.10 //
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Acyuta</s> <s>Hari</s> — he shall be your protector. // VamPSm_9.10 //

children.text: śāpaṃ prāpya ca me vīra deveśaḥ saṃsmṛtastvayā /
children.translated_text: Having received my curse, O hero, if the Lord of gods is remembered by you,

children.text: tathā tathā vadiṣyāmi śreyastvaṃ prāpsyase yathā // VamPSm_9.11 //
children.translated_text: then I shall speak in such a way that you shall attain the highest good." // VamPSm_9.11 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
<s>Aditi</s>, having obtained the boon that fulfills all desires,

children.text: krameṇa hyudare devo vṛddhiṃ prāpto mahāyaśāḥ // VamPSm_9.12 //
children.translated_text: (bore the Lord who) gradually grew in her womb — that god of great fame. // VamPSm_9.12 //

children.text: tato māse 'tha daśame kāle prasava āgate /
children.translated_text: Then, in the tenth month, when the time of birth arrived,

children.text: ajāyata sa govindo bhagavān vāmanākṛtiḥ // VamPSm_9.13 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Govinda</s>, the Blessed Lord, was born in the form of <s>Vāmana</s> (the Dwarf). // VamPSm_9.13 //
When the Lord of the universe, that lord of all the immortals, descended,
the gods were released from sorrow, and so was <s>Aditi</s>, the mother of the gods. // VamPSm_9.14 //
Winds blew with a pleasant touch; the sky became free of dust;

children.text: dharme ca sarvabhūtānāṃ tadā matirajāyata // VamPSm_9.15 //
children.translated_text: and the minds of all beings turned toward <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). // VamPSm_9.15 //
There was no agitation in the bodies of humans, O best of twice-born;

children.text: tadā hi sarvabhūtānāṃ dharme matirajāyata // VamPSm_9.16 //
children.translated_text: for at that time, the minds of all beings turned toward <s>dharma</s>. // VamPSm_9.16 //
The blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather of the world,

children.text: jātakarmādikāṃ kṛtvā kriyāṃ tuṣṭāva ca prabhum // VamPSm_9.17 //
children.translated_text: having performed the birth-rites and the like, praised the Lord. // VamPSm_9.17 //
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
"Victory, O Lord! Victory, O unconquered one! Victory, O guru of the universe, <s>Hari</s>!
Victory, O one beyond birth, death, and old age! Victory, O infinite one! Victory, O <s>Acyuta</s>! // VamPSm_9.18 //
Victory, O unvanquished! Victory, O complete! Victory, O one abiding in the unmanifest!
O supreme meaning of reality, O omniscient one, O one who has emerged from knowledge, the known, and their meaning! // VamPSm_9.19 //
Victory, O complete! O witness of the universe! O creator of the universe! O guru of the universe!
O lord of the universe and the non-universe, who protects in the state of preservation — victory! // VamPSm_9.20 //
Victory, O complete! Victory, O all! Victory, O one who dwells in all hearts!
Victory, O one who pervades beginning, middle, and end — the supreme one made of all knowledge! // VamPSm_9.21 //
O one indescribable by those seeking liberation, O eternally joyful one, victory, O Lord!
O one adorned by virtues such as self-restraint, sought by <s>yogins</s> desiring liberation! // VamPSm_9.22 //
Victory, O supremely subtle, hard to know! Victory, O gross one, pervading the universe!

children.text: jaya sūkṣmātisūkṣma tvaṃ jayānindriya sendriya // VamPSm_9.23 //
children.translated_text: Victory, O subtler than the subtle! Victory, O one both without senses and with senses! // VamPSm_9.23 //
Victory, O one established in the <s>yoga</s> of your own <s>māyā</s>! O one who rests upon <s>Śeṣa</s>, victory, O imperishable!
Victory, O one who lifted the earth on the tip of a single tusk! // VamPSm_9.24 //
O <s>Nṛkesarin</s> (Man-Lion), O tearer of the chest of the enemy of the gods!

children.text: sāmprataṃ jaya viśvātman māyāvāmana keśava // VamPSm_9.25 //
children.translated_text: Now, victory, O soul of the universe, O <s>Keśava</s> in the illusory <s>Vāmana</s> form! // VamPSm_9.25 //
O <s>Janārdana</s>, O sustainer of the world, limited by your own <s>māyā</s>,
victory, O inconceivable one! Victory, O one who is of many forms yet of a single nature, O Lord! // VamPSm_9.26 //
Grow, O <s>Hari</s>, O one of <s>Prakṛti</s> who has caused many transformations to grow!
In you, O Lord of the universe, is established the path of <s>dharma</s> for all the worlds. // VamPSm_9.27 //

children.text: na tvāmahaṃ na ceśāno nendrādyāstridaśā hare /
children.translated_text: Neither I, nor <s>Īśāna</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), nor <s>Indra</s> and the other gods, O <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: jñātumīśā na munayaḥ sanakādyā na yoginaḥ // VamPSm_9.28 //
children.translated_text: nor the sages, nor <s>Sanaka</s> and others, nor <s>yogins</s> are capable of knowing you. // VamPSm_9.28 //
You are covered by the veil of <s>māyā</s> in this world, O Lord of the world;

children.text: kastvāṃ vetsyati sarveśa tvatprasādaṃ vinā naraḥ // VamPSm_9.29 //
children.translated_text: who can know you, O Lord of all, without your grace? // VamPSm_9.29 //
Only he upon whom you, when worshipped, bestow your grace with a pleased countenance, O Lord,

children.text: sa eva kevalaṃ devaṃ vetti tvāṃ netaro naja // VamPSm_9.30 //
children.translated_text: he alone knows you, the God — no other, O Unborn one. // VamPSm_9.30 //
Therefore, O Lord of the lords of lords, O all-pervading, O cause (of all), grow!
For the welfare of this universe, O soul of the universe, O wide-eyed one!" // VamPSm_9.31 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: elaṃ stuto hṛṣīkeśaḥ sa tadā vāmanākṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus praised, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, in the form of <s>Vāmana</s>,
smiling, spoke words that were deep in meaning and full of majesty. // VamPSm_9.32 //
"I was previously praised by you, by <s>Indra</s> and the others, and by <s>Kaśyapa</s>;

children.text: mayā ca vaḥ pratijñātamindrasya bhuvanatrayam // VamPSm_9.33 //
children.translated_text: and by me a promise was made to you: the three worlds for <s>Indra</s>. // VamPSm_9.33 //
And I was praised by <s>Aditi</s>, and by her too it was heard from me

children.text: yathā śakrāya dāsyāmi trailokyaṃ hatakaṇṭakam // VamPSm_9.34 //
children.translated_text: that I shall give to <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) the three worlds, freed from thorns (enemies). // VamPSm_9.34 //

children.text: so 'haṃ tathā kariṣyāmi yathendro jagataḥ patiḥ /
children.translated_text: I shall act in such a way that <s>Indra</s>, the thousand-eyed one, shall be

children.text: bhaviṣyati sahasrākṣaḥ satyametad bravīmi vaḥ // VamPSm_9.35 //
children.translated_text: lord of the world. This is the truth I tell you." // VamPSm_9.35 //
Then <s>Brahmā</s> gave a black antelope skin to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>;

children.text: yajñopavītaṃ bhagavān dadau tasya bṛhaspatiḥ // VamPSm_9.36 //
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Bṛhaspati</s> gave him the sacred thread. // VamPSm_9.36 //
<s>Marīci</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, gave an <s>Āṣāḍha</s>-wood staff;
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> gave a water-pot; <s>Aṅgiras</s> gave a <s>kuśa</s>-grass garment;

children.text: āsanaṃ caiva pulahaḥ pulastyaḥ pītavāsasī // VamPSm_9.37 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pulaha</s> gave a seat, and <s>Pulastya</s> gave yellow garments. // VamPSm_9.37 //
The <s>Vedas</s>, adorned with the sound of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), attended upon him,
as did all the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures), and the doctrines of <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>. // VamPSm_9.38 //

children.text: sa vāmano jaṭī daṇḍī chatrī dhṛtakamaṇḍaluḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Vāmana</s>, wearing matted locks, bearing a staff, holding an umbrella and a water-pot,
that God who embodies all gods, went to <s>Bali</s>'s sacrifice. // VamPSm_9.39 //

children.text: yatra yatra padaṃ viprā bhūbhāge vāmano dadau /
children.translated_text: Wherever the <s>Vāmana</s> placed his foot upon the surface of the earth, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
the earth gave way, pressed down at each spot. // VamPSm_9.40 //
That <s>Vāmana</s>, walking with a slow gait, stepping softly, shook
the entire earth with its mountains, oceans, and islands. // VamPSm_9.41 //
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> slowly showed him the auspicious path;
and (the Lord), for the purpose of play and amusement, assumed an appearance of extreme simplicity. // VamPSm_9.42 //
Then the great serpent <s>Śeṣa</s>, emerging from <s>Rasātala</s> (the netherworld),
rendered assistance to the God of gods, the wielder of the discus. // VamPSm_9.43 //
And that supreme place of the serpent's crawling is famous even today;

children.text: tasya saṃdarśanādeva nāgebhyo na bhayaṃ bhavet // VamPSm_9.44 //
children.translated_text: by merely seeing it, there is no fear from serpents. // VamPSm_9.44 //
Thus ends the ninth chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the revered <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>.
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Seeing the earth with its mountains and forests agitated, <s>Bali</s>
asked <s>Śukra</s>, the son of <s>Uśanas</s>, bowing down with joined palms. // VamPSm_10.1 //
"O teacher, the earth with its oceans and mountains is trembling;

children.text: kasmācca nāsurān bhāgān pratigṛhṇanti vahnayaḥ // VamPSm_10.2 //
children.translated_text: and why are the (sacrificial) fires not accepting the shares of the <s>Asuras</s>?" // VamPSm_10.2 //

children.text: iti pṛṣṭo 'tha balinā kāvyo vedavidāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus asked by <s>Bali</s>, <s>Kāvya</s> (<s>Śukra</s>), the best among knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: uvāca daityādhipatiṃ ciraṃ dhyātvā mahāmatiḥ // VamPSm_10.3 //
children.translated_text: spoke to the lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, having reflected for a long time, that great-minded one. // VamPSm_10.3 //
"<s>Hari</s>, the source of the universe, has descended into the house of <s>Kaśyapa</s> —
the eternal supreme Self, in the form of <s>Vāmana</s>. // VamPSm_10.4 //
He is surely coming to your sacrifice, O best of <s>Dānavas</s>;
from the tremor of his footsteps, this earth has been shaken. // VamPSm_10.5 //
These mountains tremble; the abodes of sea-creatures are agitated;

children.text: neyaṃ bhūtapatiṃ bhūmiḥ samarthā voḍhumīśvaram // VamPSm_10.6 //
children.translated_text: this earth is unable to bear the Lord of beings, the Supreme Lord. // VamPSm_10.6 //
Along with gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>,
by him alone are upheld the earth, the waters, fire, wind, and the sky;
he bears all the gods, humans, and great <s>Asuras</s>. // VamPSm_10.7 //
This is the deep <s>māyā</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sustainer of the world,
by which the world is bound in the relation of supporter and supported. // VamPSm_10.8 //
Due to his proximity, the <s>Asuras</s>, the enemies of the gods, are not worthy of shares;

children.text: bhuñjate nāsurān bhāgānapi tena trayo 'gnayaḥ // VamPSm_10.9 //
children.translated_text: therefore the three fires do not partake of the <s>Asura</s> shares." // VamPSm_10.9 //
Hearing the words of <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Bali</s>, with hair standing on end (in joy), said:
"Blessed am I, and meritorious, for the Lord of sacrifices himself

children.text: yajñamabhyāgato brahman mattaḥ ko 'nyo 'dhikaḥ pumān // VamPSm_10.10 //
children.translated_text: has come to my sacrifice! O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, what man is greater than I? // VamPSm_10.10 //
He whom the <s>yogins</s>, ever striving, desire to behold —
the imperishable supreme Self — that God will come to my sacrifice!
Whatever I should do, O teacher, please instruct me." // VamPSm_10.11 //
<s>Śukra</s> said:
"The gods partake of sacrificial shares by the authority of the <s>Vedas</s>, O <s>Asura</s>;

children.text: tvayā tu dānavā daitya yajñabhāgabhujaḥ kṛtāḥ // VamPSm_10.12 //
children.translated_text: but by you, O <s>Daitya</s>, the <s>Dānavas</s> and <s>Daityas</s> were made partakers of sacrificial shares. // VamPSm_10.12 //

children.text: ayaṃ ca devaḥ sattvasthaḥ karoti sthitipālanam /
children.translated_text: This God, established in <s>sattva</s> (goodness), performs the preservation (of the world);

children.text: visṛṣṭaṃ ca tathāyaṃ ca svayamatti prajāḥ prabhuḥ // VamPSm_10.13 //
children.translated_text: and this very Lord himself consumes the beings that he has created. // VamPSm_10.13 //

children.text: bhavāṃstu vandī bhavitā nūnaṃ viṣṇuḥ sthitau sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: You will surely become a captive; <s>Viṣṇu</s>, established in preservation (will prevail).

children.text: viditvaivaṃ mahābhāgā kuru yat te manogatam // VamPSm_10.14 //
children.translated_text: Knowing this, O greatly fortunate one, do what is in your mind." // VamPSm_10.14 //
"No promise should be made to him by you, O lord of the <s>Daityas</s>,

children.text: pratijñā naiva voḍhavyā vācyaṃ sāma tathāphalam // VamPSm_10.15 //
children.translated_text: even regarding a trifling matter; and words of conciliation should be spoken, and (the result will be) fruitless. // VamPSm_10.15 //
When the God who has accomplished his purpose and who acts for the sake of the gods

children.text: alaṃ dadyāṃ dhanaṃ deve tvetadvācyaṃ tu yācataḥ /
children.translated_text: (comes) — 'I shall give wealth to the God' — this is what should be said when he asks,
to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who is engaged for the prosperity of the gods, O great <s>Asura</s>." // VamPSm_10.16 //
<s>Bali</s> said:
"O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, how can I say 'I have nothing' even when asked by anyone else?
How much less (can I say it) to the God whose very presence destroys sin? // VamPSm_10.17 //
The Lord <s>Hari</s>, who is attained through various vows and fasts,

children.text: sa me vakṣyati dehīti govindaḥkimato 'dhikam // VamPSm_10.18 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Govinda</s> will say to me 'Give!' — what could be greater than this? // VamPSm_10.18 //
He for whose sake great sacrifices are performed

children.text: yajñā kriyante yajñeśaḥ sa me dehīti vakṣyati // VamPSm_10.19 //
children.translated_text: by those endowed with self-restraint, purity, and virtue — that Lord of sacrifices will say 'Give!' to me! // VamPSm_10.19 //

children.text: tatsādhu sukṛtaṃ karma tapaḥ sucaritaṃ canaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, excellent is our good deed, our austerity, and our good conduct,

children.text: yanmā dehīti viśveśaḥ svayameva vadiṣyati // VamPSm_10.20 //
children.translated_text: since the Lord of the universe himself will say to me 'Give!' // VamPSm_10.20 //
I shall not say 'I have nothing,' O guru, to that Lord who has come;

children.text: prāṇatyāgaṃ kariṣye 'haṃ na tu nāsti jane kvacit // VamPSm_10.21 //
children.translated_text: I would rather give up my life than say 'there is nothing' to anyone whatsoever! // VamPSm_10.21 //
Since I have never said 'I have nothing' even to other supplicants,
how then shall I say it when <s>Acyuta</s>, the Immortal, has now arrived? // VamPSm_10.22 //
Indeed, for heroes, the encounter (with danger) arising from generosity is praiseworthy;

children.text: na bādhākāri yaddānaṃ tadaṅgaṃ balavat smṛtam // VamPSm_10.23 //
children.translated_text: a gift that causes no harm is considered the powerful limb (of duty). // VamPSm_10.23 //

children.text: madrājye nāsukhī kaścinna daridro na cāturaḥ /
children.translated_text: In my kingdom, no one is unhappy, no one is poor, no one is a rogue,

children.text: na duḥkhito na cobdigno na śamādivivarjitaḥ // VamPSm_10.24 //
children.translated_text: no one is suffering, no one is tormented, no one is devoid of tranquility and other (virtues). // VamPSm_10.24 //
Joyful, content, fragrant, satisfied, and endowed with all happiness,

children.text: janaḥ sarvo mahābhāga kimutāhaṃ sadā sukhī // VamPSm_10.25 //
children.translated_text: all people are thus, O greatly fortunate one — how much more so am I, who am always happy! // VamPSm_10.25 //
In this most excellent matter, I obtain the fruit of the seed of giving;
this is known to me, O tiger among sages, as heard from your mouth. // VamPSm_10.26 //
Pleased by my devotion, <s>Hari</s> has surely been worshipped through sacrifice;

children.text: mama dānamavāpyāsau puṣṇāti yadi devatāḥ // VamPSm_10.27 //
children.translated_text: if, having received my gifts, he nourishes the gods, // VamPSm_10.27 //
then when the seed of giving falls upon the best of recipients in this excellent field of seeds,

children.text: janārdane mahāpātre kiṃ na prāptaṃ tato mayā // VamPSm_10.28 //
children.translated_text: upon <s>Janārdana</s>, the great vessel — what have I not obtained thereby? // VamPSm_10.28 //
My giving is most excellent, and the gods are fully satisfied;
giving that is a hundredfold greater than enjoyment is said to bring happiness. // VamPSm_10.29 //
Pleased by my devotion, <s>Hari</s> has surely been worshipped through sacrifice;
therefore he approaches — there is no doubt — being a benefactor even by his sight. // VamPSm_10.30 //
Or if he approaches in anger, due to the obstruction of the gods' share,

children.text: māṃ nihantuṃ tato hi syād vadhaḥ ślāghyataro 'cyutāt // VamPSm_10.31 //
children.translated_text: to slay me — then death at the hands of the Imperishable One (<s>Acyuta</s>) would be even more glorious! // VamPSm_10.31 //
Knowing this, O best of sages, when <s>Govinda</s>, the Lord of the universe, has arrived,

children.text: naiva bhāvyaṃ jagannāthe govinde samupasthite // VamPSm_10.32 //
children.translated_text: I should not be concerned with any obstructor of my giving. // VamPSm_10.32 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
While he was speaking thus, <s>Janārdana</s> arrived there,
comprising all the gods, eternal, bearing the illusory form of a dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>). // VamPSm_10.33 //

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā yajñavāṭaṃ tu praviṣṭamasurāḥ prabhum /
