children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> who are devoted to that place,

children.text: snātā bhaktiyutāḥ sarve paśyanti paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_15.77 //
children.translated_text: having bathed there with devotion, all behold the supreme abode. // VamPSm_15.77 //
Even one who, being far away, remembers <s>Kurukṣetra</s> along with <s>Vāmana</s>,
that person too attains liberation — how much more so one who dwells there! // VamPSm_15.78 //
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter of the Saromāhātmya in the glorious <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: pavanasya hrade snātvā dṛṣṭvā devaṃ maheśvaram /
children.translated_text: Having bathed in the lake of <s>Pavana</s> (the Wind God) and having beheld Lord <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: vimuktaḥ kaluṣaiḥ sarvaiḥ śaivaṃ padamavāpnuyāt // VamPSm_16.1 //
children.translated_text: freed from all impurities, one attains the abode of <s>Śiva</s>. // VamPSm_16.1 //
<s>Pavana</s> (the Wind God), afflicted by grief for his son, became hidden in that lake.
Then, by the gods along with <s>Brahmā</s>, he was propitiated and made to manifest again. // VamPSm_16.2 //
From there one should go to the immortal abode of the Trident-bearer (<s>Śūlapāṇi</s>),

children.text: yatra devaiḥ sagandharvaiḥ hanumān prakaṭīkṛtaḥ // VamPSm_16.3 //
children.translated_text: where <s>Hanumān</s> was made to manifest by the gods together with the <s>Gandharvas</s>. // VamPSm_16.3 //
Having bathed in that <s>tīrtha</s>, a man attains immortality.
Having reached <s>Kulottāraṇa</s>, the best of twice-born <s>tīrtha</s>-pilgrims, // VamPSm_16.4 //
delivers all his families — maternal grandfathers and paternal grandfathers alike.
The <s>tīrtha</s> of the royal sage <s>Śālihotra</s> is renowned in the three worlds. // VamPSm_16.5 //
Having bathed there, one is freed from impurities born of the body.

children.text: śrīkuñjaṃ tu sarasvatyāṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam // VamPSm_16.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīkuñja</s> on the <s>Sarasvatī</s> is a <s>tīrtha</s> renowned in the three worlds. // VamPSm_16.6 //

children.text: tatra snātvā naro bhaktyā agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet /
children.translated_text: Having bathed there with devotion, a man obtains the fruit of an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> (fire sacrifice).

children.text: tato naimiṣakuñjaṃ tu samāsādya naraḥ śuciḥ // VamPSm_16.7 //
children.translated_text: Then, having reached <s>Naimiṣakuñja</s>, a man, being pure, // VamPSm_16.7 //

children.text: naimiṣasya ca snānena yat puṇyaṃ tat samāpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: obtains the same merit as bathing at <s>Naimiṣa</s>.

children.text: tatra tīrthaṃ mahākhyātaṃ vedavatyā niṣevitam // VamPSm_16.8 //
children.translated_text: There is a greatly renowned <s>tīrtha</s>, frequented by <s>Vedavatī</s>. // VamPSm_16.8 //
O best of twice-born, when <s>Rāvaṇa</s> seized her by the hair,

children.text: tadvadhāya ca sā prāṇān mumuce śokakarśitā // VamPSm_16.9 //
children.translated_text: she gave up her life, consumed by grief, for the purpose of his destruction. // VamPSm_16.9 //

children.text: tato jātā gṛhe rājño najakasya mahātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then she was born in the house of the great-souled king <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: sītā nāmeti vikhyātā rāmapatnī pativratā // VamPSm_16.10 //
children.translated_text: renowned by the name <s>Sītā</s>, the faithful wife of <s>Rāma</s>. // VamPSm_16.10 //
She was carried off by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> to this place, which led to his own destruction.

children.text: rāmeṇa rāvaṇaṃ hatvā abhiṣicya vibhiṣaṇam // VamPSm_16.11 //
children.translated_text: After <s>Rāma</s> slew <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and consecrated <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> as king, // VamPSm_16.11 //
<s>Sītā</s> was brought home, as glory returns to one possessed of self-control.

children.text: tasyāstīrthe naraḥ snātvā kanyāyajñaphalaṃ labhet // VamPSm_16.12 //
children.translated_text: Having bathed in her <s>tīrtha</s>, a man obtains the fruit of a <s>Kanyāyajña</s> (gift of a maiden). // VamPSm_16.12 //

children.text: vimuktaḥ kaluṣaiḥ sarvaiḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ padam /
children.translated_text: Freed from all impurities, he attains the supreme abode.

children.text: tato gaccheta sumahad brahmaṇaḥ sthānamuttamama // VamPSm_16.13 //
children.translated_text: Then one should go to the great and supreme abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, // VamPSm_16.13 //

children.text: yatra varṇāvaraḥ snātvā brāhmaṇyaṃ labhate naraḥ /
children.translated_text: where, having bathed, even a man of the lowest <s>varṇa</s> (caste) attains <s>Brāhmaṇya</s> (the status of a Brāhmaṇa).
And a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, with purified soul, attains the supreme abode. // VamPSm_16.14 //
Then one should go to the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Soma</s> (the Moon), which is rare even in the three worlds,
where <s>Soma</s>, having performed <s>tapas</s> (austerities), regained his sovereignty among the twice-born. // VamPSm_16.15 //

children.text: tatra snātvār'cayitvā ca svapitṝn daivatāni ca /
children.translated_text: Having bathed there and having worshipped one's ancestors and the deities,
one goes to heaven, spotless, like the moon in the month of <s>Kārttikī</s>.
The <s>Saptasārasvata</s> <s>tīrtha</s> (confluence of the seven Sarasvatīs) is rare even in the three worlds,

children.text: yatra sapta sarasvatya ekībhūtā vahanti ca // VamPSm_16.17 //
children.translated_text: where the seven <s>Sarasvatīs</s>, having become one, flow together. // VamPSm_16.17 //
<s>Suprabhā</s>, <s>Kāñcanākṣī</s>, <s>Viśālā</s>, <s>Mānasahradā</s>,
the one named <s>Sarasvatī-Oghā</s>, <s>Suveṇu</s>, and <s>Vimalodakā</s>. // VamPSm_16.18 //
When the Grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>, i.e. <s>Brahmā</s>) was performing sacrifice, stationed at <s>Puṣkara</s>,

children.text: abruvan ṛṣayaḥ sarve nāyaṃ yajño mahāphalaḥ // VamPSm_16.19 //
children.translated_text: all the sages said: 'This sacrifice will not bear great fruit, // VamPSm_16.19 //
since the best of rivers, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, is not seen here.'

children.text: tachrutvā bhagavān prītaḥ sasmārātha sarasvatīm // VamPSm_16.20 //
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the blessed Lord, pleased, remembered <s>Sarasvatī</s>. // VamPSm_16.20 //
Summoned by the Grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>) performing sacrifice at <s>Puṣkara</s>,

children.text: suprabhā nāma sā devī tatra khyātā sarasvatī // VamPSm_16.21 //
children.translated_text: the goddess renowned there as the <s>Sarasvatī</s> named <s>Suprabhā</s> came. // VamPSm_16.21 //

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā munayaḥ prītā vegayuktāṃ sarasvatīm /
children.translated_text: Having seen the swift-flowing <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the sages were delighted.

children.text: pitāmahaṃ mānayantīṃ te tu tāṃ bahu menire // VamPSm_16.22 //
children.translated_text: Honoring the Grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>), they greatly esteemed her. // VamPSm_16.22 //
Thus this best of rivers, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, stationed at <s>Puṣkara</s>,
was brought to <s>Kurukṣetra</s> by the great-souled <s>Maṅkaṇa</s>. // VamPSm_16.23 //
The sages — <s>Śaunaka</s> and others, rich in <s>tapas</s> — stationed at <s>Naimiṣa</s>,

children.text: te pṛcchanti mahātmānaṃ paurāṇaṃ lomaharṣaṇam // VamPSm_16.24 //
children.translated_text: asked the great-souled <s>Paurāṇika</s> (narrator of Purāṇas), <s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>: // VamPSm_16.24 //
'How may our sacrifice bear fruit and proceed on the right path?'
Then, the blessed ones, bowing their heads to the sages, he spoke: // VamPSm_16.25 //

children.text: sarasvatī sthitā yatra tatra yajñaphalaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: 'Where <s>Sarasvatī</s> is present, there the fruit of sacrifice is great.'
Having heard this, the sages, versed in various branches of Vedic recitation, // VamPSm_16.26 //
having assembled together, all remembered <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.text: sā tu dhyātā tatastatra ṛṣibhiḥ satrayājibhiḥ // VamPSm_16.27 //
children.translated_text: She, being meditated upon by the sages performing the <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session), // VamPSm_16.27 //
came there for the purpose of bathing at the sacrifice of those great souls.

children.text: naimiṣe kāñcanākṣī tu smṛtā maṅkaṇakena sā // VamPSm_16.28 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Naimiṣa</s>, she who was remembered by <s>Maṅkaṇaka</s> is known as <s>Kāñcanākṣī</s>. // VamPSm_16.28 //
The holy-watered <s>Sarasvatī</s> came to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.
When <s>Gaya</s> was performing the great sacrifice at <s>Gayā</s>, // VamPSm_16.29 //
the best of rivers, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, was summoned to <s>Gaya</s>'s sacrifice.

children.text: viśālāṃ nāma tāṃ prāhurṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ // VamPSm_16.30 //
children.translated_text: The sages of firm vows called her <s>Viśālā</s>. // VamPSm_16.30 //

children.text: sarit sā hi samāhūtā maṅkaṇena mahātmanā /
children.translated_text: That river, summoned by the great-souled <s>Maṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: kurukṣetraṃ samāyātā praviṣṭā ca mahānadī // VamPSm_16.31 //
children.translated_text: came to <s>Kurukṣetra</s> and entered as a great river. // VamPSm_16.31 //
In the northern region of <s>Kosala</s>, a holy place frequented by divine sages,

children.text: uddālakena muninā tatra dhyātā sarasvatī // VamPSm_16.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvatī</s> was meditated upon by the sage <s>Uddālaka</s>. // VamPSm_16.32 //
The best of rivers came to that region for the sake of the sage,
being worshipped by hosts of sages clad in bark garments and deer skins. // VamPSm_16.33 //
She is renowned as <s>Manoharā</s> (the enchanting one), the destroyer of all sins.
She was summoned to <s>Kurukṣetra</s> by the great-souled <s>Maṅkaṇa</s>,
and entered that supreme <s>tīrtha</s> for the honor of the sage. // VamPSm_16.34 //
The <s>Sarasvatī</s> renowned as <s>Suveṇu</s> at <s>Kedāra</s>,
should be known as the destroyer of all sins, frequented by accomplished sages. // VamPSm_16.35 //
She too, by that sage who propitiated <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord),
was brought into <s>Kurukṣetra</s> for the benefit of the sages. // VamPSm_16.36 //
When <s>Dakṣa</s> was performing sacrifice, that <s>Sarasvatī</s> at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s> (the gate of the Gaṅgā),
the blessed <s>Vimalodā</s> (she of pure waters), was made manifest by <s>Dakṣa</s>. // VamPSm_16.37 //
She was summoned and came there by the great-souled <s>Maṅkaṇa</s>.

children.text: kurukṣetre tu kuruṇā yajitā ca sarasvatī // VamPSm_16.38 //
children.translated_text: At <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s> was worshipped through sacrifice by <s>Kuru</s>. // VamPSm_16.38 //
She was brought to the middle of the lake by the wise <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>,
who praised the blessed, holy-watered <s>Sarasvatī</s>. // VamPSm_16.39 //
Where the perfected <s>Maṅkaṇaka</s>, stationed at <s>Saptasārasvata</s>,
while dancing, was stopped by Lord <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // VamPSm_16.40 //
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter of the Saromāhātmya in the <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
How did <s>Maṅkaṇaka</s> become perfected? From whom was the great sage born?

children.text: nṛtyamānastu devena kimarthaṃ sa nivāritaḥ // VamPSm_17.1 //
children.translated_text: And for what reason was he, while dancing, stopped by the god? // VamPSm_17.1 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
A mind-born son of <s>Kaśyapa</s> was born — the sage <s>Maṅkaṇa</s>.

children.text: snānaṃ kartuṃ vyavasito gṛhītvā valkalaṃ dvijaḥ // VamPSm_17.2 //
children.translated_text: The twice-born one, having taken his bark garment, set out to bathe. // VamPSm_17.2 //
There had come the <s>Apsarases</s> — <s>Rambhā</s> and others, lovely to behold.
Those beautiful and graceful ones were bathing together with him, blameless. // VamPSm_17.3 //
Then, from the agitation of the sage, his seed fell into the water.

children.text: tadretaḥ sa tu jagrāha kalaśe vai mahātapāḥ // VamPSm_17.4 //
children.translated_text: That seed, the great ascetic collected in a pot. // VamPSm_17.4 //

children.text: saptadhā pravibhāgaṃ tu kalaśasthaṃ jagāma ha /
children.translated_text: It divided sevenfold while in the pot.

children.text: tatrarṣayaḥ spata jātā viduryān marutāṃ gaṇān /
children.translated_text: From that were born seven sages — know them as the hosts of the <s>Maruts</s> (wind gods).
<s>Vāyuvega</s>, <s>Vāyubala</s>, <s>Vāyuhā</s>, <s>Vāyumaṇḍala</s>,
<s>Vāyujvala</s>, <s>Vāyureta</s>, and the mighty <s>Vāyucakra</s>. // VamPSm_17.6 //
These offspring of that sage sustain the moving and the unmoving world.

children.text: purā maṅkaṇakaḥ siddhaḥ kuśāgreṇeti me śrutam // VamPSm_17.7 //
children.translated_text: In ancient times, <s>Maṅkaṇaka</s> became perfected — by the tip of a <s>kuśa</s> grass blade, so I have heard. // VamPSm_17.7 //
O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, his hand was cut, and from it flowed plant sap.

children.text: sa vai śākarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣāviṣṭaḥ pranuttavān // VamPSm_17.8 //
children.translated_text: Having seen the plant sap, he was seized with joy and began to dance. // VamPSm_17.8 //

children.text: tataḥ sarvaṃ pranṛttaṃ ca sathāvaraṃ jaṅmaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: Then everything — both the stationary and the moving — began to dance.

children.text: pranuttaṃ ca jagad dṛṣṭvā tejasā tasya mohitam // VamPSm_17.9 //
children.translated_text: Seeing the world dancing, bewildered by his <s>tejas</s> (spiritual power), // VamPSm_17.9 //
<s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, along with the sages rich in <s>tapas</s>,

children.text: vijñapto vai mahādevo munerarthe dvijottamāḥ // VamPSm_17.10 //
children.translated_text: entreated <s>Mahādeva</s> for the sake of the sage, O best of twice-born. // VamPSm_17.10 //

children.text: nāya nṛtyed yathā deva tathā tvaṃ kartumarhasi /
children.translated_text: 'May he not dance thus — O Lord, you should act so that this ceases.'

children.text: tato devo muniṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣāviṣṭamatīva hi // VamPSm_17.11 //
children.translated_text: Then the god, seeing the sage overwhelmed with excessive joy, // VamPSm_17.11 //
desiring the welfare of the gods, <s>Mahādeva</s> spoke:
'What is this cause for joy, O best of sages,
for you, an ascetic established on the path of <s>dharma</s>, O best of twice-born?' // VamPSm_17.12 //

children.text: kiṃ na paśyasi me brahman karācchākarasaṃ srutam /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Brahman</s>, do you not see the plant sap flowing from my hand?

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvāhaṃ pranutto vai harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ // VamPSm_17.13 //
children.translated_text: Seeing which, I have been dancing, filled with great joy!' // VamPSm_17.13 //

children.text: taṃ prahasyābravīd devo muniṃ rāgema mohitam /
children.translated_text: The god, laughing, spoke to the sage who was deluded by passion:

children.text: ahaṃ na vismayaṃ vipra gacchāmīha prapaśyatām // VamPSm_17.14 //
children.translated_text: 'I, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, do not feel wonder at this — behold!' // VamPSm_17.14 //
Having spoken thus to the best of sages, the god of gods, of great splendor,

children.text: aṅgulyagreṇa viprendrāḥ svāṅguṣṭhaṃ tāḍayad bhavaḥ // VamPSm_17.15 //
children.translated_text: with the tip of his finger, O foremost of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) struck his own thumb. // VamPSm 17.15 //
Then ash, resembling snow, emerged from that wound;

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā vrīḍitovipraḥ pādayoḥ patito 'bravīt // VamPSm_17.16 //
children.translated_text: seeing that, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, ashamed, fell at his feet and said: // VamPSm 17.16 //
'I know no other god than the great-souled wielder of the trident (<s>Śūlapāṇi</s>);
you are the boon of the universe of moving and stationary beings, O bearer of the trident. // VamPSm 17.17 //
The gods, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, are seen to depend on you, O sinless one;

children.text: pūrvastvamasi devānāṃ kartā kārayitā mahat // VamPSm_17.18 //
children.translated_text: you are the first among the gods, the great doer and cause of all deeds. // VamPSm 17.18 //
By your grace, all the gods rejoice, free from the fear of disturbance.'

children.text: evaṃ stutvā mahādevamṛṣiḥ sa praṇato 'bravīt // VamPSm_17.19 //
children.translated_text: Having thus praised <s>Mahādeva</s>, the sage, bowing down, said: // VamPSm 17.19 //

children.text: bhagavaṃstvaprasādāddhi tapo me na kṣayaṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: 'O Blessed One, by your grace may my austerity not come to destruction.'

children.text: tato devaḥ prasānnātmā tamṛṣiṃ vākyamabravīt // VamPSm_17.20 //
children.translated_text: Then the god, with a pleased mind, spoke these words to that sage: // VamPSm 17.20 //
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
'May your austerity increase a thousandfold by my grace, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: āśrame ceha vatsyāmi tvayā sārddhamahaṃ sadā // VamPSm_17.21 //
children.translated_text: and I shall always dwell here in your hermitage with you. // VamPSm 17.21 //
The man who, having bathed at <s>Saptasārasvata</s>, worships me —

children.text: na tasya durlabhaṃ kiñcidiha loke paratra ca // VamPSm_17.22 //
children.translated_text: nothing shall be unattainable for him in this world or the next. // VamPSm 17.22 //

children.text: sārasvataṃ ca taṃ lokaṃ gamiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: He shall go to the world of <s>Sārasvata</s>, there is no doubt,

children.text: śivasya ca prasādena pāpnoti paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_17.23 //
children.translated_text: and by the grace of <s>Śiva</s>, he shall attain the supreme state.' // VamPSm 17.23 //
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the sacred <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Then one should go to the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Auśanasa</s>, endowed with faith;

children.text: uśanā yatra saṃsiddho grahatvaṃ ca samāptavān // VamPSm_18.1 //
children.translated_text: where <s>Uśanas</s> (<s>Śukra</s>) attained perfection and achieved the status of a planet. // VamPSm 18.1 //
Having bathed therein, one is freed from sins born of (previous) births;

children.text: tato yāti paraṃ brahma yasmānnāvartate punaḥ // VamPSm_18.2 //
children.translated_text: then one goes to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, from which one does not return again. // VamPSm 18.2 //

children.text: rahodaro nāma muniryatra mukto babhūva ha /
children.translated_text: There a sage named <s>Rahodara</s> was liberated;
he had been seized by a great skull, (but was freed) through seeing the greatness of the <s>tīrtha</s>. // VamPSm 18.3 //
'How was <s>Rahodara</s> seized? How did he attain liberation?
We wish to hear with reverence the greatness of that <s>tīrtha</s>.' // VamPSm 18.4 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
In ancient times, in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, by the great-souled <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>),
while dwelling there, O tigers among twice-born, <s>Rākṣasas</s> were slain. // VamPSm 18.5 //
There, the head of a certain evil-natured <s>Rākṣasa</s> was severed

children.text: kṣureṇa śitadhāreṇa tat papāta mahāvane // VamPSm_18.6 //
children.translated_text: by a sharp-edged razor (-arrow); it fell in the great forest. // VamPSm 18.6 //
By chance, it became stuck on <s>Rahodara</s>'s shin

children.text: vane vicāratastatra asthi bhittvā viveśa ha // VamPSm_18.7 //
children.translated_text: while he was wandering in the forest — having pierced through the bone, it entered. // VamPSm 18.7 //

children.text: sa tena lagnena tadā dvijātirna śaśāka ha /
children.translated_text: On account of that which was stuck to him, the twice-born, greatly wise,
was unable to visit the <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords) and temples. // VamPSm 18.8 //
The great sage, afflicted by the putrid, oozing wound,

children.text: jagāma sarvatīrthāni pṛthivyāṃ yāni kāni ca // VamPSm_18.9 //
children.translated_text: went to all the <s>tīrthas</s> on earth, whatsoever they be. // VamPSm 18.9 //
Then he told (his plight) to the sages of purified minds;

children.text: te 'bruvan ṛṣayo vipraṃ prayāhyaiśanasaṃ pratiḥ // VamPSm_18.10 //
children.translated_text: the sages said to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'Go to the <s>Aiśanasa</s> <s>tīrtha</s>.' // VamPSm 18.10 //

children.text: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā jagāma sa rahodaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard their words, that <s>Rahodara</s> went;
then, when he performed ablutions at the <s>Aiśanasa</s> <s>tīrtha</s>, // VamPSm 18.11 //
that skull, releasing his leg, fell into the water, O twice-born.

children.text: tataḥ sa virajo bhūtvā pūtātmā vītakalmaṣaḥ // VamPSm_18.12 //
children.translated_text: Then, having become purified, with a cleansed soul and freed from sin, // VamPSm 18.12 //
he returned to his hermitage joyfully and related everything.
Having heard the supreme greatness of the <s>tīrtha</s>, all the sages,
having assembled, gave it the name <s>Kapālamocana</s> (Liberation from the Skull). // VamPSm 18.13 //
There too is a very great <s>tīrtha</s>, the renowned one of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,

children.text: brāhmaṇyaṃ labdhavān yatra viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ // VamPSm_18.14 //
children.translated_text: where the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> obtained <s>Brahmanhood</s>. // VamPSm 18.14 //
Having bathed in that foremost <s>tīrtha</s>, one certainly obtains <s>Brahmanhood</s>;
and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of purified soul attains the supreme state. // VamPSm 18.15 //
Then one should go to <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>, disciplined and controlled in diet;

children.text: tatra siddhastu brahmarṣi ruṣaṅgurnāma nāmataḥ // VamPSm_18.16 //
children.translated_text: there a <s>Brahmarṣi</s> (Brahman-sage) attained perfection, named <s>Ruṣaṅgu</s>. // VamPSm 18.16 //
<s>Ruṣaṅgu</s>, possessing memory of past births, always dwelt at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>;
seeing the time of death approaching, he spoke these words to his sons:

children.text: iha śreyo na pasyāmi nayadhvaṃ māṃ pṛthūdakam // VamPSm_18.17 //
children.translated_text: 'I see no welfare here — take me to <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>.' // VamPSm 18.17 //
Understanding the intention of that <s>Ruṣaṅgu</s>, those rich in austerity,

children.text: taṃ vai tīrthe upāninyuḥ sarasvatyāstapodhanam // VamPSm_18.18 //
children.translated_text: they brought that treasure of austerity to the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Sarasvatī</s>. // VamPSm 18.18 //

children.text: sa taiḥ putraiḥ samānītaḥ sarasvatyāṃ samāplutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Brought by his sons, he bathed in <s>Sarasvatī</s>;
remembering all the merits of the <s>tīrthas</s>, that best of sages said: // VamPSm 18.19 //
'He who abandons his body at the <s>tīrtha</s> north of <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: pṛthūdake japyaparo nūnaṃ cāmaratāṃ vrajet // VamPSm_18.20 //
children.translated_text: at <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>, devoted to recitation, shall surely attain the state of immortality.' // VamPSm 18.20 //
There too is the <s>Brahmayoni</s> (source of <s>Brahmā</s>), where <s>Brahmā</s> performed creation;
resorting to <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>, stationed on the bank of <s>Sarasvatī</s>, // VamPSm 18.21 //
for the purpose of creating the four <s>varṇas</s> (social orders), he became absorbed in self-knowledge.
While he, <s>Brahmā</s>, born of the unmanifest, was meditating upon creation, // VamPSm 18.22 //
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were born from his mouth, <s>Kṣatriyas</s> from his arms,
<s>Vaiśyas</s> from his thighs, and <s>Śūdras</s> from his feet. // VamPSm 18.23 //
Having then seen the four <s>varṇas</s> established in their respective <s>āśramas</s>,

children.text: evaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmayonīti saṃjñitam // VamPSm_18.24 //
children.translated_text: thus was the <s>tīrtha</s> established, known by the name <s>Brahmayoni</s>. // VamPSm 18.24 //

children.text: tatra snātvā muktikāmaḥ punaryoniṃ na paśyati /
children.translated_text: Having bathed there, one desiring liberation does not see the womb again.
There too is a <s>tīrtha</s> well-known by the name <s>Avakīrṇa</s>. // VamPSm 18.25 //
At which <s>tīrtha</s>, <s>Baka Dālbhya</s> offered the wrathful <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>

children.text: juhāva vāhanaiḥ sārdhaṃ tatrābudhyat tato nṛpaḥ // VamPSm_18.26 //
children.translated_text: together with his mounts as oblation — there that king was awakened (to wisdom). // VamPSm 18.26 //
The sages said:
'How was the <s>tīrtha</s> established with the name <s>Avakīrṇa</s>?

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājñā ca sa kimarthaṃ prasāditaḥ // VamPSm_18.27 //
children.translated_text: And for what purpose was king <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> propitiated by him?' // VamPSm 18.27 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: ṛṣayo naimiṣeyā ye dakṣiṇārthaṃ yayuḥ purā /
children.translated_text: The sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s> went forth in ancient times seeking sacrificial fees;

children.text: tatraiva ca bako dālbhyo dṛtarāṣṭrā mayācata // VamPSm_18.28 //
children.translated_text: there <s>Baka Dālbhya</s> made a request to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>. // VamPSm 18.28 //

children.text: tenāpi tatra nindārthamuktaṃ paśvanṛtaṃ tu yat /
children.translated_text: By him (the king), however, an insult and a falsehood about cattle were spoken there for the purpose of mockery;

children.text: tataḥ krodhena mahatā māṃsamutkṛtya tatra ha / /
children.translated_text: then, with great anger, having cut flesh there, // VamPSm 18.29 //
at the great <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>, known by the name <s>Avakīrṇa</s>,
he offered the kingdom of king <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> as oblation. // VamPSm 18.30 //
While the kingdom was being offered in oblation and the sacrificial rite was underway,

children.text: akṣiyata tato rāṣṭraṃ nṛpaterduṣkṛtena vai // VamPSm_18.31 //
children.translated_text: the kingdom was destroyed by the king's own evil deeds. // VamPSm 18.31 //
Then he (the king) reflected upon the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s deed;
accompanied by his priest, taking all (kinds of) jewels, // VamPSm 18.32 //
he then went to <s>Avakīrṇa</s> for the purpose of propitiating the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: prasāditaḥ sa rājñā ca tuṣṭaḥ provāca taṃ nṛpam // VamPSm_18.33 //
children.translated_text: propitiated by the king, the pleased (sage) spoke to that king: // VamPSm 18.33 //
'<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> should not be slighted by a discerning man;

children.text: avajñāto brāhmaṇastu hanyāt tripuruṣaṃ kulam // VamPSm_18.34 //
children.translated_text: a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who is slighted can destroy three generations of a family.' // VamPSm 18.34 //

children.text: evamuktvā sa nṛpatiṃ rājyena yaśasā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to the king, he restored him with his kingdom and fame,

children.text: utthāpayāmāsa tatastasya rājño hite sthitaḥ // VamPSm_18.35 //
children.translated_text: established in the welfare of that king. // VamPSm 18.35 //

children.text: tasmiṃstīrthe tu yaḥ snāti śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who bathes at that <s>tīrtha</s> with faith and with senses controlled —

children.text: sa prāpnoti naro nityaṃ manasā cintitaṃ phalam // VamPSm_18.36 //
children.translated_text: that man always obtains the fruit desired by the mind. // VamPSm 18.36 //

children.text: tatra tīrthaṃ suvikhyātaṃ yāyātaṃ nāma nāmataḥ /
children.translated_text: There is a <s>tīrtha</s> well-known by the name <s>Yāyāta</s>,

children.text: yasyeha yajamānasya madhu susrāva vai nadī // VamPSm_18.37 //
children.translated_text: where, while the sacrificer was performing (the rite), the river flowed with honey. // VamPSm 18.37 //

children.text: tasmin snāto naro bhaktyā mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ /
children.translated_text: A man who bathes there with devotion is freed from all sins

children.text: phalaṃ prāpnoti yajñasya aśvamedhasya mānavaḥ // VamPSm_18.38 //
children.translated_text: and obtains the fruit of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice). // VamPSm 18.38 //

children.text: madhusravaṃ ca tatraiva tīrthaṃ puṇyatamaṃ dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: There too is the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Madhusrava</s> (honey-flowing), most sacred, O twice-born;

children.text: tasmin snātvā naro bhaktyā madhunātarpayet pitṝn // VamPSm_18.38 //
children.translated_text: having bathed there, a man should, with devotion, offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) to the ancestors with honey. // VamPSm 18.38 //
There too is a very great <s>tīrtha</s> known as <s>Vasiṣṭhodvāha</s>;

children.text: tatra snāto bhaktiyukto vāsiṣṭhaṃ lokamāpnuyāt // VamPSm_18.39 //
children.translated_text: having bathed there with devotion, one attains the world of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. // VamPSm 18.39 //
There too is a very great <s>tīrtha</s> known as <s>Vasiṣṭhodvāha</s>;

children.text: tatra snāto bhaktiyukto vāsiṣṭhaṃ lokamāpnuyāt // VamPSm_18.40 //
children.translated_text: having bathed there with devotion, one attains the world of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. // VamPSm 18.40 //
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the sacred <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
'How did the carrying away of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> come about?

children.text: kimarthaṃ sā saricchreṣṭhā tamṛṣiṃ pratyavāhayat // VamPSm_19.1 //
children.translated_text: For what reason did that foremost river carry away that sage?' // VamPSm 19.1 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Between the royal sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: bhṛśaṃ vairaṃ babhūveha tapaḥsparddhākṛte mahat // VamPSm_19.2 //
children.translated_text: there was a great enmity here, born of rivalry in austerity. // VamPSm 19.2 //

children.text: āśramo vai vasiṣṭhasya sthāṇutīrthe babhūva ha /
children.translated_text: The hermitage of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> was at <s>Sthāṇutīrtha</s>;
on its western side was (the hermitage) of the wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. // VamPSm 19.3 //
Where the blessed <s>Sthāṇu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), having sacrificed and having worshipped <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
the lord of the gods established <s>Sarasvatī</s> in the form of a <s>liṅga</s>. // VamPSm 19.4 //
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> was established there in austerity of fierce form;

children.text: tasyeha tapasā hīno viśvāmitro babhūva ha // VamPSm_19.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, being surpassed by his austerity, // VamPSm 19.5 //
summoned <s>Sarasvatī</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: vasiṣṭhaṃ munisārdūlaṃ svena vegena ānaya // VamPSm_19.6 //
children.translated_text: 'Bring <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the tiger among sages, here with your current.' // VamPSm 19.6 //

children.text: ihāhaṃ taṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ haniṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I shall slay that foremost of twice-born here, there is no doubt.'

children.text: etacchratvā tu vacanaṃ vyathitā sā mahānadī // VamPSm_19.7 //
children.translated_text: Having heard those words, that great river was distressed. // VamPSm 19.7 //

children.text: tathā tāṃ vyathitāṃ dṛṣṭvā vepamānaṃ mahānadīm /
children.translated_text: Seeing her distressed, the great river trembling,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, enraged, said: 'Bring <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> quickly!' // VamPSm 19.8 //
Then the foremost river, having gone to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the best of sages,

children.text: kathayāmāsa rudatī viśvāmitrasya tad vacaḥ // VamPSm_19.9 //
children.translated_text: weeping, related the words of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. // VamPSm 19.9 //
And to her, worn out by austerity and practice, deeply overcome with grief,

children.text: uvāca sa saricchreṣṭhāṃ viśvāmitrāya māṃ vacaḥ // VamPSm_19.10 //
children.translated_text: he said to the foremost river: 'Tell <s>Viśvāmitra</s> my words.' // VamPSm 19.10 //

children.text: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kṛpāśīlasya sā satit /
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of that compassionate one, she, the virtuous one,
dislodged him from his place with the flow of her waters. // VamPSm 19.11 //
And he, the son of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, being eroded from the bank,

children.text: uhyamānaśca tuṣṭāva tadā devīṃ sarasvatīm // VamPSm_19.12 //
children.translated_text: while being carried away, praised the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>: // VamPSm 19.12 //
'You have issued forth from the lake of the Grandfather (<s>Brahmā</s>), O <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: vyāptaṃ tvayā jagat sarvaṃ tavaivāmbhobhiruttamaiḥ // VamPSm_19.13 //
children.translated_text: the entire universe is pervaded by you, by your supreme waters. // VamPSm 19.13 //
You yourself, O goddess, moving through the sky, release water in the clouds;
all waters are indeed you — from you we study (the sacred knowledge). // VamPSm 19.14 //

children.text: puṣṭirdhṛtistathā kīrtiḥ siddhiḥ kāntiḥ kṣamā tathā /
children.translated_text: Nourishment (<s>Puṣṭi</s>), steadfastness (<s>Dhṛti</s>), fame (<s>Kīrti</s>), perfection (<s>Siddhi</s>), radiance (<s>Kānti</s>), patience (<s>Kṣamā</s>),

children.text: svadhā svāhā tathā vāṇī tavāyattamidaṃ jagat // VamPSm_19.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Svadhā</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>, and Speech (<s>Vāṇī</s>) — this world depends on you. // VamPSm 19.15 //
You yourself are present in all beings in the form of Speech (<s>Vāṇī</s>).'

children.text: evaṃ sarasvatī tena stutā bhagavatī tadā // VamPSm_19.16 //
children.translated_text: Thus praised by him, the blessed <s>Sarasvatī</s>, // VamPSm 19.16 //
gently carried the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> toward the hermitage of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>;

children.text: nyavedayattadā khinnā viśvāmitrāya taṃ munim // VamPSm_19.17 //
children.translated_text: exhausted, she then presented that sage to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>. // VamPSm 19.17 //
Seeing him brought by <s>Sarasvatī</s>, filled with anger,
he then sought a weapon that would end <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. // VamPSm 19.18 //
But seeing him enraged, the river, out of fear of <s>Brahma</s>-cide,
carried <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> away into the midst of her waters,

children.text: ubhayoḥ kurvatī vākyaṃ vañcayitvā ca gādhijam // VamPSm_19.19 //
children.translated_text: fulfilling the words of both, yet deceiving the son of <s>Gādhi</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>). // VamPSm 19.19 //
Then, seeing the best of sages, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, carried away,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, of great austerity, with eyes red with anger, said: // VamPSm 19.20 //
Since, O best of rivers, having deceived me, you have departed,
carry blood, O auspicious one, accompanied by the chief of <s>Rākṣasas</s>! // VamPSm_19.21 //
Then <s>Sarasvatī</s>, cursed by the wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
flowed with water mixed with blood for a year. // VamPSm_19.22 //
Then the sages, the gods, the <s>Gandharvas</s>, and the <s>Apsarases</s>,
seeing <s>Sarasvatī</s> in that state, became greatly distressed. // VamPSm_19.23 //
At that excellent and sacred <s>tīrtha</s> (pilgrimage site), she carried blood,
and then <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), <s>piśācas</s> (ghouls), and <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) gathered there. // VamPSm_19.24 //
All of them, drinking the blood, dwelt in happiness,
satiated and greatly pleased by it, free from fever,
dancing and laughing as if they had conquered heaven. // VamPSm_19.25 //
After some time, sages rich in austerity
came on pilgrimage to [the river] <s>Sarasvatī</s>, O rich in austerity. // VamPSm_19.26 //
Seeing the great river being drunk by terrible <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: paritrāṇe sarasvatyāḥ paraṃ yatnaṃ pracakrire // VamPSm_19.27 //
children.translated_text: they made the greatest effort for the protection of <s>Sarasvatī</s>. // VamPSm_19.27 //

children.text: te tu sarve mahābhāgāḥ samāgamya mahāvratāḥ /
children.translated_text: All those greatly fortunate ones of great vows, having assembled,
summoned the best of rivers and spoke these words: // VamPSm_19.28 //

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ saricchreṣṭhe śoṇitena hlado hyayam /
children.translated_text: What is the cause, O best of rivers, that this stream with blood

children.text: evamākulatāṃ yātaḥ śrutvā vetsyāmahe vayam // VamPSm_19.29 //
children.translated_text: has come to such a troubled state? Having heard, we shall understand. // VamPSm_19.29 //
Then she related everything about the doings of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
Thereupon those sages, pleased, brought to <s>Sarasvatī</s>
the [river] <s>Aruṇā</s>, whose sacred waters destroy all misdeeds. // VamPSm_19.30 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā toyaṃ sarasvatyā rākṣasā duḥkhitā bhṛśam /
children.translated_text: Seeing the [purified] waters of <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the <s>rākṣasas</s>, greatly distressed,

children.text: ūcustān vai munīn sarvān dainyayuktāḥ punaḥ punaḥ // VamPSm_19.31 //
children.translated_text: spoke to all those sages again and again, filled with wretchedness: // VamPSm_19.31 //

children.text: vayaṃ hi kṣudhitāḥ sarve dharmahīnāśca śāśvatāḥ /
children.translated_text: We are all hungry, eternally bereft of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: na ca naḥ kāmakāroyaṃ yad vayaṃ pāpakāriṇaḥ // VamPSm_19.32 //
children.translated_text: and it is not by our own will that we are sinful. // VamPSm_19.32 //
By your displeasure and by [our] evil deeds,

children.text: pakṣo 'yaṃ vardhate 'smākaṃ yataḥ smo brahmarākṣasāḥ // VamPSm_19.33 //
children.translated_text: our ranks increase, since we are <s>brahma-rākṣasas</s> (brahmin-demons). // VamPSm_19.33 //
Thus <s>Vaiśyas</s>, <s>Śūdras</s>, and <s>Kṣatriyas</s> through their misdeeds,

children.text: ye brāhmaṇān pedviṣanti te bhavantīha rākṣasāḥ // VamPSm_19.34 //
children.translated_text: who hate <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — they become <s>rākṣasas</s> in this [world]. // VamPSm_19.34 //
And through the fault of the womb of sinful women,
this lineage of ours grows — this is our eternal destiny. // VamPSm_19.35 //
You are capable of saving all the worlds;

children.text: teṣāṃ te munayaḥ śrutvā kṛpāśīlāḥ punaśca te // VamPSm_19.36 //
children.translated_text: hearing their [plea], those sages, compassionate by nature, // VamPSm_19.36 //

children.text: ūcuḥ parasparaṃ sarve tapyamānāśca te dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: all spoke to one another, those twice-born ones, burning [with compassion]:
Food that has been contaminated by hunger-insects, and that which has been eaten as leftovers, // VamPSm_19.37 //
food into which hair has fallen, which has been shaken about, or polluted by the breath of wind —

children.text: ebhiḥ saṃsṛṣṭamannaṃ ca bhāgaṃ vai rakṣasāṃ bhavet // VamPSm_19.38 //
children.translated_text: food mixed with these [impurities] shall be the share of the <s>rākṣasas</s>. // VamPSm_19.38 //
Therefore, knowing this, a wise person should always discard such foods;

children.text: rākṣasānāmasau bhuṅkte yo bhuṅkte annamīdṛśam // VamPSm_19.39 //
children.translated_text: whoever eats such food eats the share of the <s>rākṣasas</s>. // VamPSm_19.39 //
Having purified that <s>tīrtha</s>, those sages rich in austerity,

children.text: mokṣārthaṃ rakṣasāṃ teṣāṃ saṃgamaṃ tatra kalpayan // VamPSm_19.40 //
children.translated_text: for the liberation of those <s>rākṣasas</s>, established a confluence there. // VamPSm_19.40 //
At the world-renowned confluence of the <s>Aruṇā</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
one who bathes there after fasting for three nights is freed from all sins. // VamPSm_19.41 //
When the terrible <s>Kali</s> age arrives and <s>adharma</s> is at hand,
a person who bathes at the confluence of the <s>Aruṇā</s> attains liberation. // VamPSm_19.42 //
Then all those <s>rākṣasas</s>, having bathed, freed from sin,
wearing divine garlands and garments, attained the state of heaven. // VamPSm_19.43 //
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter in the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> of the <s>Śrī Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Four oceans were formerly brought there by <s>Darvin</s>;

children.text: pratyekaṃ tu naraḥ snāto gosahasraphalaṃ labhet // VamPSm_20.1 //
children.translated_text: a person who bathes in each one obtains the merit of [donating] a thousand cows. // VamPSm_20.1 //
Whatever austerity is performed at that <s>tīrtha</s>, O best of twice-born,
all of it becomes fully fruitful, even for one who has committed evil deeds. // VamPSm_20.2 //
The <s>Śatasāhasrika-tīrtha</s> and the <s>Śatika-tīrtha</s>, O twice-born,

children.text: ubhayorhi naraḥ snāto gosahasraphalaṃ labhet // VamPSm_20.3 //
children.translated_text: a person who bathes in both obtains the merit of [donating] a thousand cows. // VamPSm_20.3 //
And there also is the <s>Somatīrtha</s>, situated on the bank of <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: yasmin snātastu puruṣo rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet // VamPSm_20.4 //
children.translated_text: in which a person who bathes obtains the merit of the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice. // VamPSm_20.4 //
Having reached the hermitage of <s>Reṇukā</s>, with faith and self-control,

children.text: mātṛbhaktyā ca yatpuṇyaṃ tatphalaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ // VamPSm_20.5 //
children.translated_text: the merit that comes from devotion to one's mother — that fruit a person obtains. // VamPSm_20.5 //
One becomes eternally freed from the debts arising from gods, sages, and ancestors.

children.text: kumārasyābhiṣekaṃ ca ojasaṃ nāma viśrutam // VamPSm_20.6 //
children.translated_text: And the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) of <s>Kumāra</s>, known as <s>Ojasa</s>, // VamPSm_20.6 //

children.text: tasmin snātastu puruṣo yaśasā ca samanvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: a person who bathes there becomes endowed with glory,

children.text: kumārapuramāpnoti kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ tu mānavaḥ // VamPSm_20.7 //
children.translated_text: and performing <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites), a person attains the realm of <s>Kumāra</s>. // VamPSm_20.7 //

children.text: caitraṣaṣṭhyāṃ site pakṣe yastu śrāddhaṃ kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: On the sixth day of the bright fortnight in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, whoever performs <s>śrāddha</s>,

children.text: gayāśrāddhe ca yatpuṇyaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ // VamPSm_20.8 //
children.translated_text: the merit that comes from <s>śrāddha</s> at <s>Gayā</s> — that merit a person obtains. // VamPSm_20.8 //
Just as <s>śrāddha</s> performed at <s>Saṃnihiti</s> during an eclipse of the sun by <s>Rāhu</s>,

children.text: tathā śrāddhaṃ tatra kṛtaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // VamPSm_20.9 //
children.translated_text: so is <s>śrāddha</s> performed there — no deliberation is needed regarding this. // VamPSm_20.9 //

children.text: ojase hyakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ vāyunā kathitaṃ purā /
children.translated_text: At <s>Ojasa</s>, <s>śrāddha</s> is imperishable — this was declared by <s>Vāyu</s> in former times;

children.text: tasmāt sarvaprayatnena śrāddhaṃ tatra samācaret // VamPSm_20.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore, with every effort, one should perform <s>śrāddha</s> there. // VamPSm_20.10 //
And whoever, with faith, performs a bath on the sixth of <s>Caitra</s>,
imperishable water-offerings arise for his ancestors. // VamPSm_20.11 //
There is the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Pañcavaṭa</s>, renowned in the three worlds,

children.text: mahādevaḥ sthito yatra yogamūrtidharaḥ svayam // VamPSm_20.12 //
children.translated_text: where <s>Mahādeva</s> himself stands, bearing the form of yoga. // VamPSm_20.12 //
Having bathed there and worshipped <s>Maheśvara</s>, the god of gods,
one attains leadership among the <s>gaṇas</s> and rejoices with the gods. // VamPSm_20.13 //

children.text: kurutīrthaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ kuruṇā yatra vai tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the renowned <s>Kurutīrtha</s>, where <s>Kuru</s> performed

children.text: taptaṃ sughoraṃ kṣetrasya karṣaṇārthaṃ dvijottamāḥ // VamPSm_20.14 //
children.translated_text: terrible austerities for the purpose of cultivating the sacred field, O best of twice-born. // VamPSm_20.14 //

children.text: tasya ghoreṇa tapasā tuṣṭa indrobravīd vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Pleased by his terrible austerity, <s>Indra</s> spoke these words:
'O royal sage, I am pleased by this austerity of yours, O one of excellent vows. // VamPSm_20.15 //

children.text: yajñaṃ ye ca kurukṣetre kariṣyanti śatakratoḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who perform sacrifice at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, O <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>),
they shall go to the worlds of the meritorious, freed from sin.' // VamPSm_20.16 //

children.text: avahasya tataḥ śakro jagāma tridivaṃ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Having laughed, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the lord, then went to heaven,

children.text: āgamyāgamya caivainaṃ bhūyo bhūyo 'vahasya ca // VamPSm_20.17 //
children.translated_text: and coming again and again, laughed at him repeatedly. // VamPSm_20.17 //
<s>Śatakratu</s>, unwearied, having questioned him again and again, departed.
When [<s>Kuru</s>] had emaciated his own body with fierce austerity,

children.text: tataḥ śakro 'bravīt prītya brūhi yatte cikīrṣitam // VamPSm_20.18 //
children.translated_text: then <s>Śakra</s> said with delight: 'Tell me what you desire.' // VamPSm_20.18 //
<s>Kuru</s> said:
Those faithful people who dwell in this <s>tīrtha</s>,

children.text: te prāpnuvantu sadanaṃ brahmaṇaḥ paramātmanaḥ // VamPSm_20.19 //
children.translated_text: may they attain the abode of <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self. // VamPSm_20.19 //
Those who have committed sins elsewhere, defiled by the five great sins,

children.text: asmistīrthe narāḥ snātvā muktā yāntu parāṃ gatim // VamPSm_20.20 //
children.translated_text: having bathed in this <s>tīrtha</s>, may they be freed and go to the supreme destination. // VamPSm_20.20 //
In <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, the most sacred <s>Kurutīrtha</s>, O best of twice-born —

children.text: te dṛṣṭvā pāpamuktastu paraṃ padamavāpnuyāt // VamPSm_20.21 //
children.translated_text: having seen it, one freed from sin attains the supreme state. // VamPSm_20.21 //

children.text: kurutīrthe naraḥ snāto mukto bhavati kilviṣaiḥ /
children.translated_text: A person who bathes at <s>Kurutīrtha</s> is freed from sins;

children.text: kuruṇā samanujñātaḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_20.22 //
children.translated_text: approved by <s>Kuru</s>, he attains the supreme state. // VamPSm_20.22 //
Then one should go to <s>Svargadvāra</s> (the Gate of Heaven), situated at the door of <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: tatra snātvā śivadvāre prāpnoti paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_20.23 //
children.translated_text: having bathed at the door of <s>Śiva</s>, one attains the supreme state. // VamPSm_20.23 //
Then one should go to the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Anaraka</s> (freedom from hell), renowned in the three worlds,

children.text: yatra pūrve sthito brahma dakṣiṇe tu maheśvaraḥ // VamPSm_20.24 //
children.translated_text: where <s>Brahmā</s> stands in the east and <s>Maheśvara</s> in the south, // VamPSm_20.24 //
the consort of <s>Rudra</s> in the west, and <s>Padmanābha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) in the north;

children.text: madhye anarakaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyasyāpi durlabham // VamPSm_20.25 //
children.translated_text: in the middle is the <s>Anaraka-tīrtha</s>, rare even in the three worlds. // VamPSm_20.25 //
Having bathed there, one is freed from major and minor sins.

children.text: vaiśākhe ca yadā ṣaṣṭhī maṅgalasya dinaṃ bhavet // VamPSm_20.26 //
children.translated_text: When the sixth day of <s>Vaiśākha</s> falls on the day of <s>Maṅgala</s> (Tuesday), // VamPSm_20.26 //

children.text: tadā snānaṃ tatra kṛtvā mukto bhavati pātakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: then having bathed there, one is freed from sins.
Whoever donates four water-vessels filled with food-offerings, // VamPSm_20.27 //
and also gives a water-pot adorned with cakes,
should first please the deities with water-vessels filled with food. // VamPSm_20.28 //
Then one should give a water-pot that destroys all sins.

children.text: anenaiva vidhānena yastu snānaṃ samācaret // VamPSm_20.29 //
children.translated_text: Whoever performs a bath according to this rite, // VamPSm_20.29 //

children.text: sa muktāḥ kaluṣaiḥ sarvaiḥ prayāti paramaṃ padam /
children.translated_text: freed from all impurities, he attains the supreme state.

children.text: anyatrāpi yadā ṣaṣṭhī maṅgalena bhaviṣyati // VamPSm_20.30 //
children.translated_text: On any other occasion too when the sixth day coincides with Tuesday, // VamPSm_20.30 //
even then the rite performed there will bear the fruit of liberation.

children.text: tīrthe ca sarvatīrthānāṃ yasmin snāto dvijottamāḥ // VamPSm_20.31 //
children.translated_text: And at the <s>tīrtha</s> of all <s>tīrthas</s>, whoever bathes there, O best of twice-born, // VamPSm_20.31 //
approved by all the gods, attains the supreme state.

children.text: kāmyakaṃ ca vanaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam // VamPSm_20.32 //
children.translated_text: And the sacred <s>Kāmyaka</s> forest, which destroys all sins — // VamPSm_20.32 //
merely upon entering it, one is freed from sins.

children.text: yamāśritya vanaṃ puṇyaṃ savitā prakaṭaḥ sthitaḥ // VamPSm_20.33 //
children.translated_text: In that sacred forest, the Sun (<s>Savitṛ</s>) stands revealed, // VamPSm_20.33 //
[known as] <s>Pūṣan</s>, O best of twice-born — by seeing him one attains liberation.

children.text: ādityasya dine prāpte tasmin snātastu mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the day of the Sun (<s>Āditya</s>) arrives, a person who bathes there

children.text: viśuddhadeho bhavati manasā cintitaṃ labhet // VamPSm_20.34 //
children.translated_text: becomes purified in body and obtains what he desires in his mind. // VamPSm_20.34 //
Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> of the <s>Śrī Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
To the east of <s>Kāmyaka</s>, there is a grove frequented by the gods;

children.text: tasya tīrthasya saṃbhūtiṃ vistareṇa bravīhi naḥ // VamPSm_21.1 //
children.translated_text: tell us in detail about the origin of that <s>tīrtha</s>. // VamPSm_21.1 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Hear, all you sages, the supreme greatness of the <s>tīrtha</s>;

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ caritaṃ śrutvā mukto bhavati kilbiṣaiḥ // VamPSm_21.2 //
children.translated_text: having heard the deeds of the sages, one is freed from sins. // VamPSm_21.2 //
The sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s>, having gathered at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>,

children.text: sarasvatyāstu snānārthaṃ praveśaṃ te na lebhire // VamPSm_21.3 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of bathing in <s>Sarasvatī</s>, could not gain entry. // VamPSm_21.3 //
Then they established the <s>tīrtha</s> called <s>Yajñopavītika</s> (of the sacred thread);

children.text: śeṣāstu munayastatra na praveśaṃ hi lebhire // VamPSm_21.4 //
children.translated_text: but the remaining sages there could not gain entry either. // VamPSm_21.4 //
From the hermitage of <s>Rantuka</s> up to the <s>Sacakra-tīrtha</s>,

children.text: brāhmaṇaiḥ paripūrṇaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā devī sarasvatī // VamPSm_21.5 //
children.translated_text: seeing it filled with <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, // VamPSm_21.5 //

children.text: hitārthaṃ sarvaviprāṇāṃ kutvā kuñjāni sā nadī /
children.translated_text: for the benefit of all the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, making bends, that river

children.text: prayātā paścimaṃ mārgaṃ sarvabhūtahite sthitā // VamPSm_21.6 //
children.translated_text: went westward, devoted to the welfare of all beings. // VamPSm_21.6 //
One who bathes in the eastern flow obtains the merit of bathing in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: pravāhe dakṣiṇe tasyā narmadā saritāṃ varā // VamPSm_21.7 //
children.translated_text: in the southern flow of hers is the <s>Narmadā</s>, the best of rivers. // VamPSm_21.7 //

children.text: paścime tu diśābhāge yamunā saṃśritā nadī /
children.translated_text: In the western direction, the river <s>Yamunā</s> is present,

children.text: yadā uttarato yāti sindhurbhavati sā nadī // VamPSm_21.8 //
children.translated_text: and when she flows northward, that river becomes the <s>Sindhu</s>. // VamPSm_21.8 //
Thus the sacred <s>Sarasvatī</s> flows in the directions;

children.text: tasyāṃ snātaḥ sarvatīrthe snāto bhavati mānavaḥ // VamPSm_21.9 //
children.translated_text: one who bathes in her is as one who has bathed in all <s>tīrthas</s>. // VamPSm_21.9 //
Then one should go, O best of twice-born, to the world-renowned <s>tīrtha</s>

children.text: tīrthaṃ trailokyavikhyātaṃ vihāraṃ nāma nāmataḥ // VamPSm_21.10 //
children.translated_text: of the great-souled <s>Madana</s>, known by the name <s>Vihāra</s>. // VamPSm_21.10 //
Where the gods, having assembled, desiring to see <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: samāgatā na cāpaśyan devaṃ devyā samanvitam // VamPSm_21.11 //
children.translated_text: came together but could not see the god accompanied by the goddess. // VamPSm_21.11 //
They praised <s>Nandin</s>, the leader of the <s>gaṇas</s>, [who attends] <s>Mahādeva</s>;

children.text: tataḥ prasanno nandīśaḥ kathayāmāsa ceṣṭitam // VamPSm_21.12 //
children.translated_text: then the pleased <s>Nandīśa</s> related the doings — // VamPSm_21.12 //

children.text: bhavasya umayā sārdhaṃ vihāre krīḍitaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: the great sport of <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) together with <s>Umā</s> in the pleasure-grove.
Having heard that, the gods summoned their wives and sported there. // VamPSm_21.13 //
Pleased by their play and amusement, <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) spoke:
"He who bathes at this <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford) in the pleasure-ground with faith — // VamPSm_21.14 //
he becomes endowed with wealth, grain, and beloved ones — there is no doubt about this.

children.text: durgātīrthaṃ tato gacched durgayā sevitaṃ mahat // VamPSm_21.15 //
children.translated_text: Then one should go to the <s>Durgā Tīrtha</s>, the great (ford) frequented by <s>Durgā</s>. // VamPSm_21.15 //

children.text: yatra snātvā pitṛn pūjya na durgatimavāpḥṛyāt /
children.translated_text: Having bathed there and worshipped the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>), one would not attain a bad destination.

children.text: tatrāpi ca sarasvatyāḥ kūpaṃ trailokyaviśrutam // VamPSm_21.16 //
children.translated_text: And there too is the well of <s>Sarasvatī</s>, renowned in the three worlds. // VamPSm_21.16 //
By seeing it, one obtains liberation, freed from all sins.

children.text: yastatra tarpayet devān pitṝṃś ca śraddhayāntavitaḥ // VamPSm_21.17 //
children.translated_text: He who there offers oblations to the gods and the ancestors with faith — // VamPSm_21.17 //
he obtains everything imperishable; the <s>Pitṛ Tīrtha</s> (ford of the ancestors) is preeminent.

children.text: mātṛhā pitṛhā yaśca brahmahā gurutalpagaḥ // VamPSm_21.18 //
children.translated_text: He who has killed his mother, he who has killed his father, he who has killed a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he who has violated his teacher's bed — // VamPSm_21.18 //
having bathed, he attains purification where the eastern <s>Sarasvatī</s> (flows),
which entered the divine path and emerged through the divine path. // VamPSm_21.19 //
The eastern <s>Sarasvatī</s> is sacred even for those of evil deeds.

children.text: trirātraṃ ye kariṣyanti prācīṃ prāpya sarasvatīm // VamPSm_21.20 //
children.translated_text: Those who observe a three-night (fast), having reached the eastern <s>Sarasvatī</s> — // VamPSm_21.20 //

children.text: na teṣāṃ duṣkutaṃ kiñcid dehamāśritya tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: no evil deed whatsoever remains clinging to their body.

children.text: naranārāyaṇau devau brahmā sthāṇustathā raviḥ // VamPSm_21.21 //
children.translated_text: The gods <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Sthāṇu</s> (Śiva), and <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun) — // VamPSm_21.21 //

children.text: pracīṃ diśaṃ niṣevante sadā devāḥ savāsavāḥ /
children.translated_text: the gods together with <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) always frequent the eastern direction.

children.text: ye tu śrāddhaṃ kariṣyanti prācīmāśritya mānavāḥ // VamPSm_21.22 //
children.translated_text: Those people who will perform <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) at the eastern (Sarasvatī) — // VamPSm_21.22 //

children.text: teṣāṃ na durlabhaṃ kiñcidiha loke paratra ca /
children.translated_text: nothing is unattainable for them, in this world or the next.

children.text: tasmāt prācī sadā sevyā pañcamyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ // VamPSm_21.23 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the eastern (Sarasvatī) should always be visited, and especially on the fifth day (<s>pañcamī</s>). // VamPSm_21.23 //
He who worships on the <s>pañcamī</s> is born as one endowed with <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity).
There is the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Uśanas</s> (Śukra), difficult to obtain for the three worlds. // VamPSm_21.24 //
Where <s>Uśanas</s> attained perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) by worshipping the Supreme Lord,

children.text: grahamadhyeṣu pūjyate tasya tīrthasya sevanāt // VamPSm_21.25 //
children.translated_text: he is worshipped among the planets — by visiting that <s>tīrtha</s>. // VamPSm_21.25 //
Thus, this supreme <s>tīrtha</s> was frequented by the sage <s>Śukra</s>;

children.text: ye sevante śraddadhānāste yānti paramāṃ gatim // VamPSm_21.26 //
children.translated_text: those who frequent it with faith attain the supreme destination. // VamPSm_21.26 //

children.text: yastu śrāddhaṃ naro bhaktyā tasmiṃstīrthe kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: He who performs <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) at that <s>tīrtha</s> with devotion —
his ancestors will be liberated — there is no doubt. // VamPSm_21.27 //
The <s>Brahma Tīrtha</s> (ford of Brahmā), with four faces, is a lake established within boundaries.

children.text: ye sevante caturdaśyāṃ sopavāsā vasanti ca // VamPSm_21.28 //
children.translated_text: Those who visit it on the fourteenth day (<s>caturdaśī</s>) and dwell there fasting — // VamPSm_21.28 //
on the eighth day of the dark fortnight in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, O best of twice-born —

children.text: te paśyanti paraṃ sūkṣmaṃ yasmānnāvartate punaḥ // VamPSm_21.29 //
children.translated_text: they behold the supreme subtle (reality), from which there is no return. // VamPSm_21.29 //
Then one should go to the <s>Sthāṇu Tīrtha</s> (ford of Śiva), adorned with a thousand <s>liṅgas</s>;

children.text: tatra sthāṇuvaṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā mukto bhavati kilbiṣaiḥ // VamPSm_21.30 //
children.translated_text: having seen the <s>Sthāṇu</s> banyan tree there, one becomes freed from sins. // VamPSm_21.30 //
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter in the Saromāhātmya of the Śrī <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
O great sage, (tell us) the greatness of the <s>Sthāṇu Tīrtha</s> and of the banyan tree,
the origin of the <s>Sānnihitya</s> lake, its filling with sand, // VamPSm_22.1 //

children.text: liṅgānāṃ darśanāt puṇyaṃ sparśanena ca kiṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: the merit from seeing the <s>liṅgas</s>, and what fruit comes from touching them,
and likewise the greatness of <s>Sara</s> (the lake) — tell us everything completely. // VamPSm_22.2 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇvantu munayaḥ sarve purāṇaṃ vāmanaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: Listen, all you sages, to the great <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>,

children.text: yacchrutvā muktimāpnoti prasādād vāmanasya tu // VamPSm_22.3 //
children.translated_text: hearing which one obtains liberation by the grace of <s>Vāmana</s>. // VamPSm_22.3 //
<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, seated near the banyan tree of <s>Sthāṇu</s>,
by the sages <s>Bālakhilya</s> and others, the great-souled sons of <s>Brahmā</s> — // VamPSm_22.4 //
the sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, having approached him there with humility,

children.text: papraccha saramāhātmyaṃ pramāṇāṃ ca sthitiṃ tathā // VamPSm_22.5 //
children.translated_text: asked about the greatness of the lake (<s>Sara</s>) and the extent of its dimensions. // VamPSm_22.5 //
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
O son of <s>Brahmā</s>, O greatly fortunate one, O one versed in all scriptures,
tell me the greatness of the lake (<s>Sara</s>), which brings the destruction of all sins. // VamPSm_22.6 //
What <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords) are to be seen? What are the hidden ones, O best of the twice-born?
What <s>liṅgas</s> of supreme merit are near <s>Sthāṇu</s>? // VamPSm_22.7 //
By the mere sight of which a person attains liberation —

children.text: vaṭasya darśanaṃ puṇyamutpatti kathayasva me // VamPSm_22.8 //
children.translated_text: tell me the merit of seeing the banyan tree and its origin. // VamPSm_22.8 //
What merit is there in circumambulation? What fruit comes from bathing at the <s>tīrtha</s>?
And what merit arises from seeing the hidden (sacred sites)? // VamPSm_22.9 //
How the god of gods, <s>Sthāṇu</s> (Śiva), is established in the middle of the lake,

children.text: kimarthaṃ pāṃśunā śakrastīrthaṃ pūritavān punaḥ // VamPSm_22.10 //
children.translated_text: and why <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) filled the <s>tīrtha</s> with sand — // VamPSm_22.10 //
the greatness of the <s>Sthāṇu Tīrtha</s>, the fruit of the <s>Cakra Tīrtha</s>,

children.text: sūryatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ somatīrthasya brūhi me // VamPSm_22.11 //
children.translated_text: the greatness of the <s>Sūrya Tīrtha</s>, the <s>Soma Tīrtha</s> — tell me. // VamPSm_22.11 //

children.text: saṃkarasya ca kuhyāni viṣṇoḥ stānāni yāni ca /
children.translated_text: The hidden (sites) of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) and the abodes of <s>Viṣṇu</s> —
tell us in detail, O greatly fortunate one, about <s>Sarasvatī</s>. // VamPSm_22.12 //
Tell the greatness of the god of gods of gods, in truth, O divine one;

children.text: viriñjasya prasādena viditaṃ sarvameva ca // VamPSm_22.13 //
children.translated_text: by the grace of <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), everything indeed is known (to you). // VamPSm_22.13 //
<s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s> said:
Having heard <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>'s words, that great sage, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>,
with great devotion to the <s>tīrtha</s>, his mind inclined (toward it) — // VamPSm_22.14 //
relaxing his cross-legged posture and bowing to <s>Maheśvara</s> (Śiva),

children.text: kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ yacchrutaṃ brahmaṇaḥ purā // VamPSm_22.15 //
children.translated_text: he narrated all that he had heard previously from <s>Brahmā</s>. // VamPSm_22.15 //
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Having bowed to <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, the boon-giver, <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: utpatti ca pravakṣyāmi tīrthānāṃ brahmabhāṣitām // VamPSm_22.16 //
children.translated_text: I shall declare the origin of the <s>tīrthas</s> as spoken by <s>Brahmā</s>. // VamPSm_22.16 //
In the beginning, in the terrible single ocean, when all that was stationary and moving had perished,
there was a single great egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>), the seed-origin of all creatures. // VamPSm_22.17 //
In that egg, <s>Brahmā</s> was situated and commenced his sleep;
having slept for a period of a thousand <s>yugas</s>, he awoke. // VamPSm_22.18 //
Having risen from sleep, <s>Brahmā</s> then beheld the world as empty.

children.text: sṛṣṭiṃ cintayatastasya rajasā mohitasya ca // VamPSm_22.19 //
children.translated_text: As he was contemplating creation, impelled by <s>rajas</s> (passion) — // VamPSm_22.19 //

children.text: rajaḥ sṛṣṭiguṇaṃ proktaṃ sattvaṃ sthitiguṇaṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rajas</s> is declared to be the quality of creation; <s>sattva</s> (goodness) is known as the quality of maintenance;
and at the time of dissolution, the quality of <s>tamas</s> (darkness) prevails. // VamPSm_22.20 //

children.text: guṇātītaḥ sa bhagavān vyāpakaḥ puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: That Lord who transcends the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), who is all-pervading, is known as <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Supreme Person);
by Him this entire (universe) is pervaded — whatever is designated as a living being. // VamPSm_22.21 //

children.text: sa brahma sa ca govinda īśvaraḥ sa sanātanaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is <s>Brahman</s>, He is <s>Govinda</s>, He is <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), He is the eternal one.

children.text: yastaṃ veda mahātmānaṃ sa sarvaṃ veda mokṣavit // VamPSm_22.22 //
children.translated_text: He who knows that great-souled one — he knows everything, he is a knower of liberation. // VamPSm_22.22 //
What need have they of all <s>tīrthas</s> or hermitages —
those whose minds, directed toward the infinite, are established in the <s>ātman</s> (self) alone? // VamPSm_22.23 //
The <s>ātman</s> is the river, with self-restraint as its sacred ford, truth as its water, endowed with good conduct and wisdom;

children.text: tasyāṃ snātaḥ puṇyakarmā punāti na viriṇā suddhyati cāntarātmā // VamPSm_22.24 //
children.translated_text: one who bathes in that (river), one of meritorious deeds, is purified — but the inner self is not purified by (mere) water. // VamPSm_22.24 //
This is the chief action of a person: that which has entered the bliss of self-realization;

children.text: jñeyaṃ tadeva pravadanti santastatprāpya dehī vijahāti kāmān // VamPSm_22.25 //
children.translated_text: the saints declare that alone is to be known — having attained it, the embodied being abandons desires. // VamPSm_22.25 //

children.text: naitādṛsaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsti vittaṃ yathaikatā samatā satyatā ca /
children.translated_text: There is no wealth of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> equal to unity, equanimity, and truthfulness,
steadfastness in good conduct, the avoidance of punishment-dealing, freedom from anger, and cessation from (selfish) actions. // VamPSm_22.26 //

children.text: etad brahma samāsena mayoktaṃ te dvijottama /
children.translated_text: This <s>Brahman</s> has been briefly told to you by me, O best of the twice-born;

children.text: yajjñātvā brahma paramaṃ prāpsyasi tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ // VamPSm_22.27 //
children.translated_text: knowing which, you shall attain the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — there is no doubt. // VamPSm_22.27 //
Now hear also the origin of <s>Brahmā</s>, the Supreme Self;

children.text: imaṃ codāharantyeva ślokaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prati // VamPSm_22.28 //
children.translated_text: and they cite this very verse regarding <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>: // VamPSm_22.28 //

children.text: āpo nārā vai tanava ityevaṃ nāma śuśrumaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The waters are called <s>Nāra</s>, for they are indeed his offspring' — thus we have heard the name;

children.text: tāsu śete sa yasmācca tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // VamPSm_22.29 //
children.translated_text: since he rests (<s>śete</s>) in them, he is therefore called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // VamPSm_22.29 //
Having awakened in that water, and perceiving the universe contained within (the egg),
the Lord split open the egg — from that, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> was born. // VamPSm_22.30 //

children.text: tato bhūrabhavat tasmād bhuva ityaparaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then from that arose <s>Bhūḥ</s> (earth); the second (world) is known as <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>;

children.text: svaḥ śabdaśca tṛtīyo 'bhad bhūrbhuvaḥ sveti saṃjñitaḥ // VamPSm_22.31 //
children.translated_text: and the third was <s>Svaḥ</s> (heaven) — (together) designated as <s>Bhūrbhuvaḥsvaḥ</s>. // VamPSm_22.31 //
From that arose the radiance — that which is the excellent (light) of <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun);
and that radiance, having emerged from the egg, dried up the water. // VamPSm_22.32 //
What remained after being dried by the radiance became a viscous mass (<s>kalala</s>);

children.text: kalalād budbudaṃ jñeyaṃ tataḥ kāṭhinyatāṃ gatam // VamPSm_22.33 //
children.translated_text: from the viscous mass arose a bubble, and then it attained hardness. // VamPSm_22.33 //

children.text: kāṭhinyād dharaṇī jñeya bhūtānāṃ dhāriṇī iha sā /
children.translated_text: From that hardness is to be known the earth (<s>dharaṇī</s>), the supporter of all beings here.

children.text: yasmin stānesthitaṃ hyaṇḍaṃ tasmin saṃnihitaṃsaraḥ // VamPSm_22.34 //
children.translated_text: In the very place where the egg was situated — there is the <s>Sānnihita</s> lake. // VamPSm_22.34 //
The radiance that first emerged from it — from that, it is called <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun).
In the middle of the egg was born <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the world. // VamPSm_22.35 //
The embryonic membrane (<s>ulba</s>) became <s>Meru</s> (the cosmic mountain); the afterbirth (<s>jarāyu</s>) is known as the (other) mountains;

children.text: garbhodakaṃ samudrāśca tathā nadyaḥ sahasraśaḥ // VamPSm_22.36 //
children.translated_text: the embryonic fluid became the oceans, and the rivers by the thousands. // VamPSm_22.36 //
The pure, great water at the navel of <s>Brahmā</s> —
the great lake was filled with that pure, excellent water. // VamPSm_22.37 //
In its center, a banyan tree in the form of <s>Sthāṇu</s> (Śiva), the great-minded one;

children.text: tasmād vinirgatā varṇā brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā viśaḥ // VamPSm_22.38 //
children.translated_text: from that emerged the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) — <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>; // VamPSm_22.38 //
and from that the <s>Śūdras</s> were born, for the purpose of serving the twice-born.
Then, as <s>Brahmā</s>, the one born from the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), was contemplating creation,

children.text: manasā mānasā jātāḥ sanakādyā maharṣayaḥ // VamPSm_22.39 //
children.translated_text: from his mind were born the mind-born ones — <s>Sanaka</s> and the other great sages. // VamPSm_22.39 //
And as the wise one again contemplated, desiring progeny,

children.text: utpannā ṛṣayaḥ sapta te prajāpatayo 'bhavan // VamPSm_22.40 //
children.translated_text: the seven sages were born — they became the <s>Prajāpatis</s> (lords of creatures). // VamPSm_22.40 //
And as he again contemplated, impelled by <s>rajas</s> (passion),
the <s>Bālakhilyas</s> were born, devoted to austerities and self-study. // VamPSm_22.41 //
They, always devoted to bathing, intent on worshipping the gods,
emaciate their bodies through fasts and severe vows. // VamPSm_22.42 //
Following the discipline of forest-dwellers (<s>vānaprastha</s>), accompanied by the <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-sacrifice),
they emaciate their bodies through supreme austerities here. // VamPSm_22.43 //
For a divine thousand years, emaciated and with sinews protruding,

children.text: ārādhayanti deveśaṃ na ca tuṣyati śaṅkaraḥ // VamPSm_22.44 //
children.translated_text: they worshipped the Lord of gods — yet <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) was not pleased. // VamPSm_22.44 //

children.text: tataḥ kālena mahatā umayā saha śaṅkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, after a great length of time, <s>Śaṅkara</s> together with <s>Umā</s>,

children.text: ākāśamārgeṇa tadā dṛṣṭvā devī suduḥkhitāḥ // VamPSm_22.45 //
children.translated_text: (traveling) through the sky-path, the Goddess saw them in great distress. // VamPSm_22.45 //
Having propitiated the Lord of the lords of gods, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the one of excellent vows spoke:
"These hosts of sages who dwell in the <s>Devadāru</s> (deodar) forest are suffering. // VamPSm_22.46 //

children.text: teṣāṃ kleśakṣayaṃ deva vidhehi kuru me dayām /
children.translated_text: O god, bring an end to their suffering; show me compassion.
What (sin) have these people, who are devoted to the duties of the <s>Vedas</s>, the limitless, O god, committed, // VamPSm_22.47 //
that they still are not purified, though dried to mere sinews and bones?"
Having heard the words of the Goddess, the wielder of the <s>Pināka</s> bow, the slayer of <s>Andhaka</s>,
spoke, laughing, his head adorned with the beautiful rays of the moon: // VamPSm_22.48 //
The glorious <s>Mahādeva</s> said:

children.text: na vetsi devi tattvena dharmasya gahanā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: "You do not know the truth, O Goddess — the ways of <s>dharma</s> are inscrutable.

children.text: naite dharmaṃ vijānanti na ca kāmavivarjitāḥ // VamPSm_22.49 //
children.translated_text: They do not know <s>dharma</s>, nor are they free from desire. // VamPSm_22.49 //

children.text: na ca krodhena nirmuktāḥ kevalaṃ mūḍhabuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor are they released from anger — they are merely of deluded understanding."

children.text: etacchrutvābravīd devī mā maivaṃ śaṃsitavratān // VamPSm_22.50 //
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the Goddess said: "Do not speak thus of these whose vows are well-praised. // VamPSm_22.50 //

children.text: deva pradarśayātmānaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me /
children.translated_text: O god, reveal yourself — I have great curiosity about this."

children.text: sa ityukta uvācedaṃ devīṃ devaḥ smitānanāḥ // VamPSm_22.51 //
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the god spoke this to the Goddess, with a smiling face: // VamPSm_22.51 //
"You stay here; I shall go where these chief among sages

children.text: sādhayanti tapo ghoraṃ darśayiṣyāmi ceṣṭitam // VamPSm_22.52 //
children.translated_text: are performing terrible austerities — I shall show you my conduct." // VamPSm_22.52 //

children.text: ityuktā tu tato devī śaṅkareṇa mahātmanā /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the great-souled <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the Goddess,
delighted, said to her husband, the Lord of the worlds: "Go!" // VamPSm_22.53 //

children.text: yatra te munayaḥ sarve kāṣṭhaleṣṭasamāḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: where all those sages stood, motionless as logs and stones,
reciting [the Vedas], most blessed, having performed the rites of fire-tending; // VamPSm 22.54 //

children.text: tān vilokya tato devo nagnaḥ sarvāṅgasundaraḥ /
children.translated_text: seeing them, the god [appeared] — naked, beautiful in every limb,
wearing a garland of forest flowers as his crown-ornament, youthful, bearing a begging bowl and skull; // VamPSm 22.55 //

children.text: āśrame paryaṭan bhikṣāṃ munīnāṃ darśanaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: wandering through the hermitage begging alms, approaching the sages for a viewing,

children.text: dehi bhikṣāṃ tataścoktvā hyāśramādāśramaṃ yayau // VamPSm_22.56 //
children.translated_text: having said 'Give me alms,' he went from one hermitage to another. // VamPSm 22.56 //
Seeing him arrived at the hermitage, the wives of the <s>Brahman</s>-speaking [sages],
enchanted by his form, with a nature full of curiosity — // VamPSm 22.57 //

children.text: procuḥ parasparaṃ nārya ehi paśyāma bhiśrukam /
children.translated_text: the women said to one another: 'Come, let us behold this mendicant!'

children.text: parasparamiti coktvā gṛhya mūlaphalaṃ bahu // VamPSm_22.58 //
children.translated_text: Having said this to one another, they took up many roots and fruits, // VamPSm 22.58 //
'Accept alms!' said those wives of the sages to that god;

children.text: sa tu bhikṣākapālaṃ taṃ prasārya bahu sādaram // VamPSm_22.59 //
children.translated_text: and he, extending that begging bowl, [said] with great respect: // VamPSm 22.59 //
'Give, give! May there be auspiciousness for you ladies in this penance grove!'
The god, laughing, was beheld there by the goddess [from afar];

children.text: tasmai dattvaiva tāṃ bhikṣāṃ papracchustaṃ smarāturāḥ // VamPSm_22.60 //
children.translated_text: having given him those alms, afflicted with desire, they questioned him: // VamPSm 22.60 //
The women said:
'What is your name? What vow and observance do you, O ascetic, practice,
in which, with naked body, adorned with a garland of forest flowers,

children.text: bhavān vai tāpaso hṛdyo hṛdyāḥ smo yadi manyase // VamPSm_22.61 //
children.translated_text: you are indeed a charming ascetic? We too are charming — if you so consider.' // VamPSm 22.61 //
Thus addressed by the ascetic women, he spoke with a smiling face:

children.text: idamīdṛg vrataṃ kiñcinna rahasyaṃ prakāśyate // VamPSm_22.62 //
children.translated_text: 'This vow is of such a nature — its secret is not to be disclosed. // VamPSm 22.62 //

children.text: śṛṇvanti bahavo yatra tatra vyākhyā na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Where many listen, there no explanation is given;

children.text: asya vratasya subhagā iti matvā gamiṣyatha // VamPSm_22.63 //
children.translated_text: O beautiful ones, thinking thus [about] this vow, you will go [your way].' // VamPSm 22.63 //
Thus addressed by him, those [women] then replied to the sage:

children.text: rahasye hi gamiṣyāmo mune naḥ kaitukaṃ mahat // VamPSm_22.64 //
children.translated_text: 'We shall indeed go in private — O sage, our curiosity is great!' // VamPSm 22.64 //

children.text: ityuktvā tāstadā taṃ vai jagṛhuḥ pāṇipallavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having said this, they then seized him with their tender hands;
one [embraced him] by the neck with passion, another with her arms; // VamPSm 22.65 //
other women [grasped him] by the knees, others playfully by the hair,
others at the region of the waist, and others at the feet. // VamPSm 22.66 //
Seeing the agitation of their own wives in the hermitages, the sages,
crying 'Let him be slain!' with sticks and stones in hand, // VamPSm 22.67 //
cut off and cast down the god's terrible <s>liṅga</s> (phallus).
When the <s>liṅga</s> had been cut down, the Lord disappeared;

children.text: 22.68 devyā sa bhagavān rudraḥ kailāsaṃ nagamāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, together with the goddess, took refuge on Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>.

children.text: patite devadevasya liṅge naṣṭe carācare // VamPSm_22.69 //
children.translated_text: When the <s>liṅga</s> of the god of gods had fallen, in all that moves and does not move, // VamPSm 22.69 //
a great disturbance arose among the self-realized sages.

children.text: evaṃ deve tadā tatra vartati vyākulīkṛte // VamPSm_22.70 //
children.translated_text: While the god was thus made to be in such a state of confusion there, // VamPSm 22.70 //
one chief among sages, the best of the wise, said:

children.text: na vayaṃ vidmaḥ sadbhāvaṃ tāpasasya mahātmanaḥ // VamPSm_22.71 //
children.translated_text: 'We do not know the true nature of that great-souled ascetic. // VamPSm 22.71 //

children.text: viriñciṃ śaraṇaṃ yāmaḥ sa hi jñāsyati ceṣṭitam /
children.translated_text: Let us go to <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) for refuge — he will know [the ascetic's] conduct.'

children.text: evamuktāḥ sarva eva ṛṣayo lañjitā bhṛśam // VamPSm_22.72 //
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, all the sages, greatly ashamed, // VamPSm 22.72 //

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ jagmur devaiḥ saha niṣevitam /
children.translated_text: went to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, attended by the gods.
Having prostrated before the lord of the gods, they stood with faces downcast in shame. // VamPSm 22.73 //

children.text: atha tān duḥkhitān dṛṣṭvā brahma vacanamabravīt /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing them distressed, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke these words:

children.text: aho mugdhā yadā yūyaṃ krodhena kaluṣīkṛtāḥ // VamPSm_22.74 //
children.translated_text: 'Alas, deluded ones! You have been polluted by anger! // VamPSm 22.74 //
Not a single practice of <s>dharma</s> is understood by you, O dull-witted ones!
Listen to the essence of <s>dharma</s>, O ascetics of cruel deeds: // VamPSm 22.75 //

children.text: viditvā yad budhaḥ kṣipraṃ dharmasya phalamāpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: knowing which, a wise person quickly obtains the fruit of <s>dharma</s> —
that [Self] which is all-pervading, eternal, and ever-established within this body, in the self, // VamPSm 22.76 //
He is beginningless, He is the great pillar (<s>Sthāṇu</s>), indicated in His separateness;
just as a jewel, though radiant in color by itself, by its setting // VamPSm 22.77 //
takes on the nature of that [setting], so too the self, fashioned by the mind,
taking on the distinctions of the mind, is augmented by actions. // VamPSm 22.78 //
Then, subject to <s>karma</s>, one experiences enjoyments — heavenly and infernal;
therefore the wise one should purify that mind by the means of <s>jñāna-yoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) and the rest. // VamPSm 22.79 //
When that [mind] is purified, the inner self, by itself, becomes free from disturbance;
not even through the afflictions of the body, which are of a burning nature, // VamPSm 22.80 //

children.text: śuddhimāpnoti puruṣaḥ saṃśuddhaṃ yasya no manaḥ /
children.translated_text: does a person attain purity if his mind is not purified.

children.text: kriyā hi niyamārthāya pātakebhyaḥ prakīrtitāḥ // VamPSm_22.81 //
children.translated_text: Ritual observances are prescribed for the purpose of discipline, [protecting] from sins. // VamPSm 22.81 //

children.text: yasmādatyāvilaṃ dehaṃ na śīghraṃ śuddhyate kila /
children.translated_text: Since the body, being exceedingly impure, is not quickly purified,

children.text: tena lokeṣu mārgo 'yaṃ satpathasya pravartitaḥ // VamPSm_22.82 //
children.translated_text: therefore this path of the true way has been established in the worlds. // VamPSm 22.82 //
This division of <s>varṇas</s> (classes) and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) by some overseer of the world
was created — the mark of the greatness of delusion and of those of highest destiny. // VamPSm 22.83 //
You, dwelling in hermitages, are overcome by anger and desire;
