the hermitage is the dwelling of the wise; for the <s>yogins</s>, there is no hermitage [in the conventional sense]. // VamPSm 22.84 //

children.text: kva ca nyastasamastecchā kva ca nārīmayo bhramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where is [your state of] having renounced all desires? And where is this delusion caused by women?

children.text: kva krodhamīdṛśaṃ ghoraṃ yenātmānaṃ na jāyatha // VamPSm_22.85 //
children.translated_text: Where is this terrible anger, by which you do not recognize your own self? // VamPSm 22.85 //

children.text: yatkrodhano yajati yad dadāti yad vā tapastapatila yajjuhoti /
children.translated_text: Whatever an angry man sacrifices, whatever he gives, whatever austerity he performs, whatever he offers [in the fire] —

children.text: na tasya prāpnoti phalaṃ hi loke moghaṃ phalaṃ tasya hi krodhanasya // VamPSm_22.86 //
children.translated_text: the fruit of that does not come to him in this world; futile is the fruit of that angry one.' // VamPSm 22.86 //
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the glorious <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Brahmā</s>, all those sages
asked once again about the cause of the welfare of the world. // VamPSm 23.1 //
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
'Let us go for refuge to the god who holds the trident, the three-eyed one;

children.text: prasādād devadevasya bhaviṣyatha yathā purā // VamPSm_23.2 //
children.translated_text: by the grace of the god of gods, you will become as [you were] before.' // VamPSm 23.2 //
Thus told, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, [they went to] <s>Kailāsa</s>, the supreme mountain;
they beheld <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) seated together with <s>Umā</s>. // VamPSm 23.3 //
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the world, began to praise

children.text: devādhidevaṃ varadaṃ trailokyasya prabhuṃ śivam // VamPSm_23.4 //
children.translated_text: the god of gods, the boon-granter, the lord of the three worlds, <s>Śiva</s>. // VamPSm 23.4 //
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
'Salutations to the infinite one, to the boon-granter, to the wielder of the <s>Pināka</s> bow,
to <s>Mahādeva</s>, to the god, to <s>Sthāṇu</s> (the immovable pillar), to the Supreme Self! // VamPSm 23.5 //
Salutations to you always, O lord of the worlds, O deliverer;
you alone are the god who bestows knowledge, the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>. // VamPSm 23.6 //
Salutations to you, O lotus-wombed one! Salutations again and again to the lord of the lotus!
To the one whose form is both terrible and peaceful, to <s>Caṇḍa</s> of fierce wrath, salutations! // VamPSm 23.7 //
Salutations to you, O god, O lord of the universe! Salutations to you, O leader of the gods!
O trident-wielder, salutations to you! Salutations to you, O creator of the universe!' // VamPSm 23.8 //
Thus praised by <s>Brahmā</s> and the sages, <s>Mahādeva</s>

children.text: uvāca mā bhairvrajata liṅgaṃ vo bhavitā punaḥ // VamPSm_23.9 //
children.translated_text: said: 'Fear not! Go — the <s>liṅga</s> will be yours again. // VamPSm 23.9 //

children.text: kriyatāṃ madvayaḥ śīghraṃ yena me prītiruttamā /
children.translated_text: Let my decree be carried out quickly, by which my supreme satisfaction

children.text: bhaviṣyati pratiṣṭhāyāṃ liṅgasyātra na saṃśayaḥ // VamPSm_23.10 //
children.translated_text: will come about through the installation of the <s>liṅga</s> — of this there is no doubt. // VamPSm 23.10 //
Those who worship my <s>liṅga</s> with devotion —

children.text: na teṣāṃ durlabhaṃ kicid bhaviṣyati kadācana // VamPSm_23.11 //
children.translated_text: for them, nothing will ever be unattainable. // VamPSm 23.11 //
Even all sins committed knowingly

children.text: śuddhyate liṅgapūjāyāṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // VamPSm_23.12 //
children.translated_text: are purified through the worship of the <s>liṅga</s> — no deliberation is needed in this matter.' // VamPSm 23.12 //
'The <s>liṅga</s> cast down by you — carry it from the great lake',

children.text: sāṃnihatyaṃ tu vikhyātaṃ tasmiñśīghraṃ pratiṣṭhitam // VamPSm_23.13 //
children.translated_text: 'the famous <s>Sāṃnidhya</s> — and install it there swiftly.' // VamPSm 23.13 //
'Then you shall obtain whatever desired wish, O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;

children.text: sthāṇurnāmnā hi lokeṣu pūjanīyo divaukasām // VamPSm_23.14 //
children.translated_text: by the name <s>Sthāṇu</s>, it is to be worshipped in the worlds by the celestials.' // VamPSm 23.14 //
'Since it stands established at <s>Sthāṇvīśvara</s>, it is therefore known as <s>Sthāṇvīśvara</s>;

children.text: ye smaranti sadā sthāṇuṃ te muktāḥ sarvakilbiṣaiḥ // VamPSm_23.15 //
children.translated_text: those who always remember <s>Sthāṇu</s> are freed from all sins. // VamPSm 23.15 //
They will become pure in body and, through its sight, will attain liberation.'

children.text: ityevamuktā devena ṛṣayo brahmaṇā saha // VamPSm_23.16 //
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the god, the sages together with <s>Brahmā</s> // VamPSm 23.16 //
then set about to carry the <s>liṅga</s> from that <s>Dāruvana</s> (pine forest).

children.text: na taṃ cālayituṃ śaktāste devā ṛṣibhiḥ saha // VamPSm_23.17 //
children.translated_text: But the gods together with the sages were unable to move it. // VamPSm 23.17 //

children.text: śrameṇa mahatā yuktā brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ /
children.translated_text: Afflicted by great exertion, they went to <s>Brahmā</s> for refuge;
to those tormented by effort, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke these words: // VamPSm 23.18 //

children.text: kiṃ vā śrameṇa mahatā na yūyaṃ vahanakṣamāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What use is this great exertion? You are not capable of carrying it!

children.text: svecchayā pātitaṃ liṅgaṃ devadevena śūlinā // VamPSm_23.19 //
children.translated_text: The <s>liṅga</s> was dropped by the god of gods, the trident-wielder, of His own will. // VamPSm 23.19 //

children.text: tasmāt tameva śaraṇaṃ yāsyāmaḥ sahitāḥ surāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, let us all, together with the gods, go to Him alone for refuge;
being pleased, <s>Mahādeva</s> Himself will carry it.' // VamPSm 23.20 //
Thus addressed, the sages and gods, together with <s>Brahmā</s>,
approached Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>, desirous of seeing <s>Rudra</s>. // VamPSm 23.21 //

children.text: na ca paśyanti taṃ devaṃ tataścintāsamanvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: But they did not see that god; then, filled with anxiety,

children.text: brahmāṇamūcurmunayaḥ kva sa devo maheśvaraḥ // VamPSm_23.22 //
children.translated_text: the sages said to <s>Brahmā</s>: 'Where is the god <s>Maheśvara</s>?' // VamPSm 23.22 //

children.text: tato brahma ciraṃ dhyātvā jñātvā devaṃ maheśvaram /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, meditating for a long time, knowing the god <s>Maheśvara</s>
[to be] standing in the form of an elephant, praised by the sages mentally — // VamPSm 23.23 //

children.text: atha te ṛṣayaḥ sarve devāśca brahmaṇā saha /
children.translated_text: then all those sages and gods, together with <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: gatā mahatsaraḥ puṇyaṃ yatra devaḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ // VamPSm_23.24 //
children.translated_text: went to the sacred great lake where the god Himself stood. // VamPSm 23.24 //
But they did not see that god, searching here and there;

children.text: tataścintānvitā devā brahmaṇā sahitā sthitāḥ // VamPSm_23.25 //
children.translated_text: then the gods, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, stood filled with anxiety. // VamPSm 23.25 //
They beheld the goddess, well-pleased, adorned with a water-pot;

children.text: prīyamāṇā tadā devī idaṃ vacanamabravīt // VamPSm_23.26 //
children.translated_text: the goddess, being gracious, then spoke these words: // VamPSm 23.26 //
'Afflicted by great exertion, searching for <s>Maheśvara</s> —
drink this nectar, O gods, and then you shall know <s>Śaṅkara</s>.'

children.text: etacchratvā tu vacanaṃ bhavānyā samudāhṛtam // VamPSm_23.27 //
children.translated_text: Hearing these words uttered by <s>Bhavānī</s>, // VamPSm 23.27 //
the gods, comfortably seated, drank that pure nectar.
Then, seated at ease, they asked the supreme goddess: // VamPSm 23.28 //

children.text: kva sa deva ihāyāto hastirūpadharaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where is that god who came here, standing in elephant form?'

children.text: darśitaśca tadā devyā saromadhye vyavasthitaḥ // VamPSm_23.29 //
children.translated_text: He was then shown by the goddess, stationed in the middle of the lake. // VamPSm 23.29 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā devaṃ harṣayuktāḥ sarve devāḥ saharṣibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the god, all the gods and sages, filled with joy,
placing <s>Brahmā</s> at the forefront, spoke these words: // VamPSm 23.30 //
'O <s>Mahādeva</s>, the <s>liṅga</s>, worshiped by the three worlds, was abandoned by you;

children.text: tasya cānayane nānyaḥ samarthaḥ syānmaheśvara // VamPSm_23.31 //
children.translated_text: and for bringing it, no one else is capable, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.' // VamPSm 23.31 //
Thus addressed by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, the blessed lord <s>Hara</s>
went together with the sages to the hermitage in the <s>Devadāru</s> (deodar) forest. // VamPSm 23.32 //
Having gone there, <s>Mahādeva</s> <s>Hara</s>, bearing the form of an elephant,

children.text: kareṇa jagrāha tato līlayā parameśvaraḥ // VamPSm_23.33 //
children.translated_text: grasped [the liṅga] with his trunk — the supreme lord, playfully. // VamPSm 23.33 //
Carrying that, <s>Mahādeva</s>, being praised by the great sages,

children.text: niveśayāmāsa tadā saraḥpārśve tu paścime // VamPSm_23.34 //
children.translated_text: installed it then on the western side of the lake. // VamPSm 23.34 //

children.text: tato devāḥ sarva eva ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all the gods and the sages, rich in austerity,

children.text: ātmānaṃ saphalaṃ daṣṭvā stavaṃ cakrurmaheśvare // VamPSm_23.35 //
children.translated_text: seeing themselves fulfilled, composed a hymn of praise to <s>Maheśvara</s>. // VamPSm 23.35 //

children.text: namaste paramātman anantayone lokasākṣin parameṣṭhin bhagavan mahāviriñca mahāvibhūte mahākṣetrajña mahāpuruṣa sarvabhūtāvāsa manonivāsa ādideva mahādeva sadāśiva (5) īśāna durvijñeya durārādhya mahābhūteścara parameśvara mahāyogeśvara tryambaka mahāyogin parabrahman paramajyotiḥ brahmaviduttama oṅkāra vaṣaṭkāra svāhākāra svadhākāra paramakāraṇa sarvagata sarvadarśin sarvaśakte sarvadeva aja (10) sahasrārciḥ pṛṣārciḥ sudhāman haradhāma anantadhāma saṃvarta saṃkarṣaṇa vaḍavānala agnīṣomātmaka pavitra mahāpavitra mahāmegha mahāmāyādhara mahākāma kāmahan haṃsa paramahaṃsa mahārājika maheśvara mahākāmuka mahāhaṃsa bhavakṣayakara surasiddhārcita (15) hiraṇyavāha hiraṇyaretaḥ hiraṇyanābha hiraṇyāgrakeśa
children.translated_text: Salutations to you, O <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), O infinite source, witness of the worlds, <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, great <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), of great splendor, great <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), great <s>Puruṣa</s>, abode of all beings, dwelling place of the mind, primordial god, great god, ever-auspicious (<s>Sadāśiva</s>), (5) <s>Īśāna</s>, difficult to know, difficult to worship, one who moves among the great elements, supreme lord, great lord of <s>Yoga</s>, three-eyed (<s>Tryambaka</s>), great yogin, supreme <s>Brahman</s>, supreme light, the best among knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Oṃkāra</s>, <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>, <s>Svāhākāra</s>, <s>Svadhākāra</s>, supreme cause, all-pervading, all-seeing, all-powerful, all-god, unborn, (10) of a thousand rays, of bristling rays, of beautiful abode, the abode of <s>Hara</s>, of infinite abode, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, the submarine fire (<s>Vaḍavānala</s>), having <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> as essence, purifier, the great purifier, the great cloud, bearer of the great <s>Māyā</s>, the great desire, destroyer of desire (<s>Kāmahan</s>), <s>Haṃsa</s> (swan), supreme <s>Haṃsa</s>, the great sovereign, great lord, the great lover, the great swan, destroyer of worldly existence, worshipped by gods and <s>Siddhas</s>, (15) of golden vehicle, of golden seed, of golden navel, of golden-tipped hair,

children.text: muñjakeśin sarvalokavaraprada sarvānugrahakara kamaleśaya kuśeśaya hṛdayeśaya jñānodadhe śaṃbho vibho mahāyajña mahāyājñi ka sarvayajñamaya sarvaya5hṛdaya sarvayajñasaṃstuta nirāśraya (20) samudreśaya atrisaṃbhava bhaktānukampin abhagnayoga yogadhara vāsukimahāmaṇi- vidyotitavigraha haritanayana trilocana jaṭādhara nīlakaṇṭha candrārdhadhara umāśarīrārdhahara gajacarmadhara dustarasaṃsāramahāsaṃhārakara(25) prasīda bhaktajanavatsala evaṃ stuto devagaṇaiḥ subhaktyā sabrahāmukhyaiśca pitāmahena /
children.translated_text: matted-haired (<s>Muñjakeśin</s>), granter of boons to all worlds, bestower of grace upon all, reclining on a lotus, reclining on <s>Kuśa</s> grass, reclining in the heart, ocean of knowledge, <s>Śambhu</s>, all-pervading one, the great sacrifice, the great sacrificer, consisting of all sacrifices, the heart of all sacrifices, praised by all sacrifices, without support, (20) reclining on the ocean, born of <s>Atri</s>, compassionate to devotees, of unbroken <s>Yoga</s>, bearer of <s>Yoga</s>, one whose form is illuminated by the great gem of <s>Vāsuki</s>, green-eyed, three-eyed, matted-haired (<s>Jaṭādhara</s>), blue-throated (<s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>), bearing the half-moon, having half the body of <s>Umā</s>, wearing an elephant skin, the great destroyer of the impassable <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth), (25) be gracious, O one who is tender toward devotees!' Thus praised by the hosts of gods with great devotion, headed by <s>Brahmā</s>, and by the Grandfather himself,

children.text: tyaktvā tadā hastirūpaṃ mahātmā liṅge tadā saṃnidhānaṃ cakāra // VamPSm_23.36 //
children.translated_text: the great-souled one, abandoning then the elephant form, manifested his presence in the <s>liṅga</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 23.36 //
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then <s>Mahādeva</s> (the great god) spoke to the gods headed by <s>Brahmā</s>,
in the very presence of the sages, the supreme glory of the <s>tīrtha</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.1 //

children.text: etat sāṃnihitaṃ proktaṃ saraḥ puṇyatamaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: This is declared to be the <s>Sānnihita</s> lake, the most sacred and great;
since it is attended upon by me, therefore it grants liberation. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.2 //

children.text: iha ye puruṣāḥ kecid brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā viśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever people here — <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, or <s>Vaiśyas</s> —

children.text: liṅgasya darśanādeva paśyanti paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_24.3 //
children.translated_text: merely by seeing the <s>liṅga</s>, they behold the supreme state. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.3 //
Day after day, all the <s>tīrthas</s>, as far as the oceans and lakes,

children.text: sthāṇutīrthaṃ sameṣyanti madhyaṃ prāpte divākare // VamPSm_24.4 //
children.translated_text: shall assemble at <s>Sthāṇutīrtha</s> when the sun reaches its zenith. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.4 //

children.text: stotreṇānena ca naro yo māṃ stoṣyati bhaktitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the person who shall praise me with this hymn with devotion —

children.text: tasyāhaṃ sulabho nityaṃ bhaviṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ // VamPSm_24.5 //
children.translated_text: I shall always be easily accessible to him — there is no doubt. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.5 //

children.text: ityuktvā bhagavān rudro hyantardhānaṃ gataḥ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the lord <s>Bhagavān Rudra</s> vanished from sight,

children.text: devāśca ṛṣayaḥ sarve svāni sthānāni bhehire // VamPSm_24.6 //
children.translated_text: and all the gods and sages returned to their own abodes. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.6 //
Then heaven was made continuous, mingled with humans;
by the glory of the <s>Sthāṇu-liṅga</s>, one attains heaven merely by seeing it. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.7 //

children.text: tato devāḥ sarva eva brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all the gods sought refuge in <s>Brahmā</s>;

children.text: tānuvāca tadā brahmā kimarthamiha cāgatāḥ // VamPSm_24.8 //
children.translated_text: then <s>Brahmā</s> said to them: 'For what purpose have you come here?' // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.8 //

children.text: tato devāḥ sarva eva idaṃ vacanamabruvan /
children.translated_text: Then all the gods spoke these words:

children.text: mānuṣebhyo bhayaṃ tīvraṃ rakṣāsmākaṃ pitāmaha // VamPSm_24.9 //
children.translated_text: 'There is terrible fear from humans — protect us, O Grandfather!' // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.9 //
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of the thirty [gods], said to the gods:

children.text: pāṃśunā pūryatāṃ śīghraṃ saraḥ śakre hitaṃ kuru // VamPSm_24.10 //
children.translated_text: 'Let [the lake] be quickly filled with dust; O <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), do what is beneficial.' // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.10 //
Then <s>Bhagavān Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) rained down dust,

children.text: saptāhaṃ pūrayāmāsa saro devaistadā vṛtaḥ // VamPSm_24.11 //
children.translated_text: and for seven days he filled the lake, surrounded by the gods. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.11 //

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṃśuvarṣaṃ ca devadevo maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing that rain of dust, <s>Maheśvara</s>, the god of gods,

children.text: kareṇa dhārayāmāsa liṅgaṃ tīrthavaṭaṃ tadā // VamPSm_24.12 //
children.translated_text: held with his hand the <s>liṅga</s> and the sacred fig tree of the <s>tīrtha</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.12 //
Therefore the most sacred <s>tīrtha</s> is the first one where the water remains;

children.text: tasmin snātaḥ sarvatīrthaiḥ snāto bhavati mānavaḥ // VamPSm_24.13 //
children.translated_text: a person who bathes there is [considered as] having bathed in all <s>tīrthas</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.13 //
One who performs <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) there, between the fig tree and the <s>liṅga</s> —

children.text: tasya prītāśca pitaro dāsyanti bhuvi durlabham // VamPSm_24.14 //
children.translated_text: his ancestors, pleased, will grant what is rare on earth. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.14 //

children.text: pūritaṃ ta caco dṛṣṭvā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing [the lake] filled, all those sages

children.text: pāṃśunā sarvagātrāṇi spṛśanti śraddhayā yutāḥ // VamPSm_24.15 //
children.translated_text: touched all their limbs with the dust, endowed with faith. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.15 //
Those sages too, with their sins cleansed by the dust, departed,

children.text: pūjyamānāḥ suragaṇaiḥ prayātā brahmaṇaḥ padam // VamPSm_24.16 //
children.translated_text: honored by the hosts of gods, and went to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.16 //

children.text: ye tu siddhā mahātmānaste liṅgaṃ pūjayanti ca /
children.translated_text: And those great-souled <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings) who worship the <s>liṅga</s>,
they attain the supreme perfection, from which return is impossible. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.17 //

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā tadā brahmā liṅgaṃ śailamayaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: Having understood this, <s>Brahmā</s> then installed a stone <s>liṅga</s>,

children.text: ādyaliṅgaṃ tadā sthāpya tasyopari dadhāra tat // VamPSm_24.18 //
children.translated_text: establishing the first <s>liṅga</s> and placing that above it. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.18 //

children.text: tataḥ kālena mahatā tejasā tasya rañjitam /
children.translated_text: Then, after a great [passage of] time, it was imbued with its radiance;

children.text: tasyāpi sparśanāt siddhaḥ paraṃ padamavāpnuyāt // VamPSm_24.19 //
children.translated_text: by merely touching it, one becomes perfected and attains the supreme state. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.19 //
Then <s>Brahmā</s> was again entreated by the gods, O best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>:

children.text: ete yānti parāṃ siddhiṃ liṅgasya darśanānnarāḥ // VamPSm_24.20 //
children.translated_text: 'These men attain supreme perfection merely by seeing the <s>liṅga</s>!' // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.20 //
Hearing that, <s>Bhagavān Brahmā</s>, desiring the welfare of the gods,

children.text: uparyupari liṅgāni sapta tatra cakāra ha // VamPSm_24.21 //
children.translated_text: placed seven <s>liṅgas</s> one upon another there. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.21 //
Then those who desired liberation, <s>Siddhas</s> devoted to tranquility,

children.text: sevya pāṃśuṃ prayatnena prayātāḥ paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_24.22 //
children.translated_text: having carefully worshipped the dust, went to the supreme state. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.22 //
Even the dust particles of <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, stirred up by the wind,
lead to the supreme state even one who has committed great misdeeds. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.23 //

children.text: ajñānājjñānato vāpi striyo vā puruṣasya vā /
children.translated_text: Whether unknowingly or knowingly, whether for women or men,
all misdeeds are destroyed by the power of <s>Sthāṇutīrtha</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.24 //
Liberation comes from seeing the <s>liṅga</s>, and from touching the fig tree;

children.text: tatsaṃnidhau jale snātvā prāpnotyabhimataṃ phalam // VamPSm_24.25 //
children.translated_text: and having bathed in the water near it, one obtains the desired fruit. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.25 //

children.text: pitṛṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ yastu jale tasmin kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: One who shall perform the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) for the ancestors in that water —

children.text: bindo bindau tu toyasya anantaphalabhāgbhavet // VamPSm_24.26 //
children.translated_text: with every single drop of water, he shall become a partaker of infinite fruit. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.26 //

children.text: yastu kṛṣṇatilaiḥ sārddha liṅgasya paścime sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who, standing to the west of the <s>liṅga</s> together with black sesame seeds,

children.text: tarpayecchraddhayā yuktaḥ sa prīṇāti yugatrayam // VamPSm_24.27 //
children.translated_text: offers <s>tarpaṇa</s> endowed with faith — he gratifies [the ancestors for] three <s>yugas</s> (ages). // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.27 //
As long as the <s>Manvantara</s> (cosmic era) is declared, as long as the <s>liṅga</s> endures,
so long the gratified ancestors drink the excellent water. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.28 //
In the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>, [the tīrtha is] <s>Sānnihitya</s>; in the <s>Tretā</s>, it is called <s>Vāyu</s>;
in the <s>Dvāpara</s> and <s>Kali</s> [ages], it is known as a well [and] <s>Rudrahrada</s> (pool of <s>Rudra</s>). // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.29 //
On the fourteenth of the dark half of <s>Caitra</s>, the best of men,

children.text: snātvā rudrahrade tīrthe paraṃ padamavāpnuyāt // VamPSm_24.30 //
children.translated_text: having bathed at the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Rudrahrada</s>, attains the supreme state. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.30 //

children.text: yastu vaṭe sthito rātriṃ dhyāyate parameśvaram /
children.translated_text: One who stays the night at the fig tree meditating on the supreme lord,
by the grace of the fig tree of <s>Sthāṇu</s>, [obtains] the fruit conceived in the mind. // <s>VamPSm</s> 24.31 //
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
To the north of <s>Sthāṇu-vaṭa</s> is proclaimed the <s>Sukra-tīrtha</s>;
to the east of <s>Sthāṇu-vaṭa</s> is <s>Soma-tīrtha</s>, O best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.1 //
To the south of <s>Sthāṇu-vaṭa</s> is declared <s>Dakṣa-tīrtha</s>;
to the west of <s>Sthāṇu-vaṭa</s> is established <s>Skanda-tīrtha</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.2 //
These are the holy <s>tīrthas</s>, with <s>Sthāṇu</s> in the middle — so it is recorded;

children.text: tasya darśanamātreṇa prāpnoti paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_25.3 //
children.translated_text: merely by seeing it, one attains the supreme state. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.3 //
On the eighth and fourteenth [of the lunar fortnight], one who circumambulates these —

children.text: pade pade yajñaphalaṃ sa prāpnoti na śaṃśayaḥ // VamPSm_25.4 //
children.translated_text: at every step he obtains the fruit of sacrifice — there is no doubt. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.4 //
These [tīrthas] were attended with effort by sages, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>,
<s>Maruts</s> (wind gods), and <s>Agnis</s> (fire gods). // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.5 //

children.text: anye ye prāṇinaḥ kecit praviṣṭāḥ sthāṇumuttamam /
children.translated_text: Whatever other living beings have entered the supreme <s>Sthāṇu</s>,
freed from all sins, they go to the supreme destination. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.6 //
Near it is the <s>liṅga</s> of the trident-bearing god of gods;

children.text: umā ca liṅgarūpeṇa harapārśvaṃ na muñcati // VamPSm_25.7 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Umā</s>, in the form of a <s>liṅga</s>, does not leave <s>Hara</s>'s side. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.7 //
Merely by seeing it, a person attains perfection.

children.text: vaṭasya uttare pārśve takṣakeṇa mahātmanā // VamPSm_25.8 //
children.translated_text: On the northern side of the fig tree, by the great-souled <s>Takṣaka</s>, // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.8 //
a great <s>liṅga</s> was installed that grants all desires.
On the eastern side of the fig tree, a great one was made by <s>Viśvakarman</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.9 //
Having seen the westward-facing <s>liṅga</s>, a person attains perfection.

children.text: tatraiva liṅgarūpeṇa sthitā devī sarasvatī // VamPSm_25.10 //
children.translated_text: There also, <s>Devī Sarasvatī</s> stands in the form of a <s>liṅga</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.10 //

children.text: praṇamya tāṃ prayatnena buddhiṃ medhāṃ ca vindati /
children.translated_text: By bowing to her with effort, one obtains intelligence and wisdom.

children.text: vaṭapārśve sthitaṃ liṅgaṃ brahmaṇā tat pratiṣṭhitam // VamPSm_25.11 //
children.translated_text: At the side of the fig tree stands a <s>liṅga</s> installed by <s>Brahmā</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.11 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vaṭeśvaraṃ devaṃ prayāti paramaṃ padam /
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Vaṭeśvara</s> (the lord of the fig tree), one goes to the supreme state.

children.text: tataḥ sthāṇuvaṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam // VamPSm_25.12 //
children.translated_text: Then, having seen <s>Sthāṇu-vaṭa</s> and having performed circumambulation, // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.12 //
by him the seven-continented earth has been circumambulated.

children.text: sthāṇoḥ paścimadigbāge nakulīśo gaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // VamPSm_25.13 //
children.translated_text: On the western side of <s>Sthāṇu</s> is the <s>gaṇa</s> (attendant) known as <s>Nakulīśa</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.13 //
By worshipping him with effort, one is freed from all sins.

children.text: tasya dakṣiṇadigbhāge tīrthaṃ rudrakaraṃ smṛtam // VamPSm_25.14 //
children.translated_text: On its southern side is the <s>tīrtha</s> known as <s>Rudrakara</s>. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.14 //

children.text: tasmin snātaḥ sarvatīrthe snāto bhavati mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: A person who bathes there is [considered as] having bathed in all <s>tīrthas</s>.
On its northern side, by the great-souled <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.15 //
a great <s>liṅga</s> was installed, called <s>Gokarṇa</s> by name.
In the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, on the fourteenth of the dark half,

children.text: tasyāṃ yor'cati gokarṇaṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu // VamPSm_25.16 //
children.translated_text: one who worships <s>Gokarṇa</s> on that day — hear of its meritorious fruit: // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.16 //

children.text: kāmato 'kāmato vāpi yat pāpaṃ tena saṃcitam /
children.translated_text: whatever sin has been accumulated by him, intentionally or unintentionally —

children.text: tasmād vimucyate pāpāt pūjayitvā haraṃ śuciḥ // VamPSm_25.17 //
children.translated_text: from that sin he is freed, having worshipped <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) in purity. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.17 //
The merit obtained by men through lifelong <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) from youth —

children.text: tatpuṇyaṃ sakalaṃ tasya aṣṭamyāṃ yor'cayecchivam // VamPSm_25.18 //
children.translated_text: all that merit belongs to one who worships <s>Śiva</s> on the eighth [lunar day]. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.18 //
If one desires supreme beauty, good fortune, and abundance of wealth —
by the glory of <s>Kumāreśvara</s>, it is accomplished — there is no doubt.
25.19 On its northern side, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> worshipped a <s>liṅga</s>,
and became ageless and immortal. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.20 //

children.text: āṣāḍhasya tu māsasya śuklā yā cāṣṭamī bhavet /
children.translated_text: On the eighth of the bright half of the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>,
one who worships it with fasting attains immortality. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.21 //

children.text: khareṇa pūjitaṃ liṅgaṃ tasmin sthāne dvijottama /
children.translated_text: A <s>liṅga</s> was worshipped by <s>Khara</s> at that place, O best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;
by worshipping it with effort, one obtains all desires. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.22 //
<s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Triśiras</s> also, having worshipped <s>Maheśvara</s> there,
obtained their desired wishes and were filled with joy. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.23 //

children.text: caitramāse site pakṣe yo narastatra pūjayet /
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Caitra</s>, in the bright half, one who worships there —

children.text: tasya tau varadau devau prayacchete 'bhivāñchitam // VamPSm_25.24 //
children.translated_text: those two benevolent gods grant him what is desired. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.24 //
To the east of <s>Sthāṇu-vaṭa</s> is <s>Hastipādeśvara Śiva</s>;

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mucyate pāpairanyajanmani saṃbhavaiḥ // VamPSm_25.25 //
children.translated_text: by seeing him, one is freed from sins arising in other births. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.25 //

children.text: tasya dakṣiṇato liṅgaṃ hārītasya ṛṣeḥ sthitam /
children.translated_text: To its south stands the <s>liṅga</s> of the sage <s>Hārīta</s>;

children.text: yat praṇaṇya prayatnena siddhiṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ // VamPSm_25.26 //
children.translated_text: by bowing to it with effort, a person attains perfection. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.26 //
On its southern side, [there is the liṅga] of the great-souled <s>Vāpīta</s>,
a <s>liṅga</s> renowned in the three worlds, auspicious, that removes all sins. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.27 //
And by <s>Rudra</s> of great soul in the form of a skeleton (<s>Kaṅkāla</s>),
a great <s>liṅga</s> was installed that destroys all sins. // <s>VamPSm</s> 25.28 //
It is declared to grant both enjoyment and liberation, and to destroy all offenses.
and from beholding the <s>liṅga</s>, one obtains the fruit of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> (fire-sacrifice). // VamPSm 25.29 //
On its western side, a <s>liṅga</s> installed by <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings),
known as <s>Siddheśvara</s>, the bestower of all perfections. // VamPSm 25.30 //
On its southern side, by the great-souled <s>Mṛkaṇḍa</s>,

children.text: tatra pratiṣṭhitaṃ liṅgaṃ darśanāt siddhidāyakam // VamPSm_25.31 //
children.translated_text: a <s>liṅga</s> was installed there, which grants perfection by its mere sight. // VamPSm 25.31 //

children.text: tasya pūrve ca digbhāge ādityena mahātmanā /
children.translated_text: On its eastern side, by the great-souled <s>Āditya</s> (Sun),
an excellent <s>liṅga</s> was installed, which destroys all sins. // VamPSm 25.32 //
<s>Citrāṅgada</s> the <s>Gandharva</s>, and <s>Rambhā</s>, the best of <s>Apsarases</s>,
mutually in love, desiring to behold <s>Sthāṇu</s>, // VamPSm 25.33 //
having beheld <s>Sthāṇu</s> and worshipped him, mutually in love,

children.text: ārādhya varadaṃ devaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya maheśvaram // VamPSm_25.34 //
children.translated_text: having propitiated the boon-granting god and installed <s>Maheśvara</s> — // VamPSm 25.34 //
having beheld <s>Citrāṅgadeśvara</s> and likewise <s>Rambheśvara</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: subhago darśanīyaśca kule janma samāpnuyāt // VamPSm_25.35 //
children.translated_text: one becomes fortunate, handsome, and obtains birth in a noble family. // VamPSm 25.35 //

children.text: tasya dabhiṇato liṅgaṃ vajriṇā sthāpitaṃ purā /
children.translated_text: To its south, a <s>liṅga</s> was established formerly by <s>Vajrin</s> (<s>Indra</s>).

children.text: tasya prasādāt prāpnoti manasā cintitaṃ phalam // VamPSm_25.36 //
children.translated_text: By his grace, one obtains the fruit desired in mind. // VamPSm 25.36 //
By the sage <s>Parāśara</s>, having worshipped <s>Śaṅkara</s> there,

children.text: prāptaṃ kavitvaṃ paramaṃ darśanācchaṅkarasya ca // VamPSm_25.37 //
children.translated_text: supreme poetic power was obtained through beholding <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // VamPSm 25.37 //
By the sage <s>Vedavyāsa</s>, having worshipped <s>Parameśvara</s>,
omniscience and knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> were obtained by the grace of the god. // VamPSm 25.38 //
On the western side of <s>Sthāṇu</s>, by <s>Vāyu</s>, the life of the world,
a great <s>liṅga</s> was installed, which destroys sin by its mere sight. // VamPSm 25.39 //
And on its southern side, the <s>liṅga</s> of <s>Himavateśvara</s>,
installed by the meritorious, which grants perfection by its sight. // VamPSm 25.40 //
And on its western side, installed by <s>Kārtavīrya</s>,

children.text: liṅgaṃ pāpaharaṃ sadyo kārtanāt puṇyamāpnuyāt // VamPSm_25.41 //
children.translated_text: a <s>liṅga</s> that removes sin — by its recitation one instantly obtains merit. // VamPSm 25.41 //
And on its northern side, at <s>Supārśva</s>, it was installed again.
<s>Hanumān</s> too, having worshipped (there), obtained perfection by the grace of the god. // VamPSm 25.42 //
On its eastern side, by the mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: ārādhya varadaṃ devaṃ cakraṃ labdhaṃ sudarśanam // VamPSm_25.43 //
children.translated_text: having worshipped the boon-granting god, the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus was obtained. // VamPSm 25.43 //
And on its eastern side, by <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>,
two excellent <s>liṅgas</s> were installed, bestowing all desires. // VamPSm 25.44 //
These (liṅgas) were reverenced with effort by sages, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, and <s>Vasus</s>,
and they indeed remove all sins. // VamPSm 25.45 //
Behind the <s>Kharṇa-liṅga</s>, by the sages who perceive the truth,

children.text: pratiṣṭhitāni liṅgāni yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate // VamPSm_25.46 //
children.translated_text: <s>liṅgas</s> were installed whose number is beyond count. // VamPSm 25.46 //
And likewise to its north, as far as the river <s>Oghavatī</s>,
one thousand <s>liṅgas</s> stand to the west of the god. // VamPSm 25.47 //
And on its eastern side, by the great-souled <s>Bālakhilyas</s>,
a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) of <s>Rudras</s> were installed, extending as far as Lake <s>Saṃnihita</s>. // VamPSm 25.48 //
And to the south of the god, by <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>,

children.text: pratiṣṭhitāni liṅgāni yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate // VamPSm_25.49 //
children.translated_text: <s>liṅgas</s> were installed whose number is beyond count. // VamPSm 25.49 //
<s>Vāyu</s> declared: three and a half <s>koṭis</s> (thirty-five million) of <s>liṅgas</s>,

children.text: asaṃkhyātāḥ sahasrāṇi ye rudrāḥ sthāṇumāśritāḥ // VamPSm_25.50 //
children.translated_text: and innumerable thousands of <s>Rudras</s> who have taken refuge in <s>Sthāṇu</s>. // VamPSm 25.50 //
Knowing this, a faithful person should take refuge in the <s>Sthāṇu-liṅga</s>,

children.text: yasya prasādāt prāpnoti manasā cintitaṃ phalam // VamPSm_25.51 //
children.translated_text: by whose grace one obtains the fruit desired in mind. // VamPSm 25.51 //

children.text: akāmo vā sakāmo vā praviṣṭaḥ sthāṇumandiram /
children.translated_text: Whether without desire or with desire, one who has entered the temple of <s>Sthāṇu</s>,

children.text: vimuktaḥ pātakairghoraiḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_25.52 //
children.translated_text: freed from terrible sins, attains the supreme state. // VamPSm 25.52 //
In the month of <s>Caitra</s>, on the thirteenth, by the conjunction of divine stars,
on the most auspicious and holy day when Venus, the Sun, and the Moon are conjoined, // VamPSm 25.53 //
the <s>Sthāṇu-liṅga</s> was installed by <s>Brahmā</s>, the sustainer of the worlds,
and has been worshipped by sages and hosts of gods for eternal years. // VamPSm 25.54 //
At that time, those persons who, fasting and endowed with faith,

children.text: pūjayanti śivaṃ ye vai te yānti paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_25.55 //
children.translated_text: worship <s>Śiva</s>, they indeed go to the supreme state. // VamPSm 25.55 //
Knowing this, those who perform circumambulation of that (sacred complex) —
by them the earth with its seven continents has been circumambulated. // VamPSm 25.56 //
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
I wish to hear the glory of <s>Sthāṇutīrtha</s>, O sage —
by whom was perfection attained, which dispels the fear of all sins? // VamPSm 26.1 //
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Hear in full the supreme glory of <s>Sthāṇu</s>,

children.text: yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mukto bhavati mānavaḥ // VamPSm_26.2 //
children.translated_text: hearing which, a person becomes freed from all sins. // VamPSm 26.2 //
When this world was a single ocean, when all moving and stationary beings had perished,
from the navel of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the unmanifest-born, a lotus arose;
in that (lotus), <s>Brahmā</s> was born, the grandfather of all worlds. // VamPSm 26.3 //
From him <s>Marīci</s> was born; from <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s> was the son.
From <s>Kaśyapa</s> was born <s>Bhāsvān</s> (the Sun); from him, <s>Manu</s> was born. // VamPSm 26.4 //
And from <s>Manu</s>, when he sneezed, a son was born from his mouth.
On the earth bounded by four (oceans), he was a king, a protector of <s>dharma</s>. // VamPSm 26.5 //

children.text: tasya patnī babhūvātha bhayā nāma bhayāvahā /
children.translated_text: His wife was named <s>Bhayā</s>, who was fearsome —

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sakāśādutpannā kālasya duhitā tadā // VamPSm_26.6 //
children.translated_text: she was born from <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), the daughter of <s>Kāla</s> (Time). // VamPSm 26.6 //
From her was born <s>Vena</s>, wicked-souled, a reviler of the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā putravadanaṃ kruddho rājā vanaṃ yayau // VamPSm_26.7 //
children.translated_text: Seeing the face of his son, the king, enraged, went to the forest. // VamPSm 26.7 //

children.text: tatra kṛtvā tapo ghoraṃ dharmeṇāvṛtya rodasī /
children.translated_text: There, having performed terrible austerity, having enveloped heaven and earth with <s>dharma</s>,
he attained the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, from which return is difficult. // VamPSm 26.8 //
<s>Vena</s> became king over the entire surface of the earth.
Due to the fault of his maternal grandfather — for he was the grandson of <s>Kāla</s> (Time) — // VamPSm 26.9 //
the wicked-souled reviler of the <s>Vedas</s> proclaimed in the city:

children.text: na dātavyaṃ na yaṣṭavyaṃ na hotavyaṃ kadācana // VamPSm_26.10 //
children.translated_text: 'Nothing is to be given, nothing is to be sacrificed, nothing is to be offered — ever! // VamPSm 26.10 //

children.text: ahameko 'tra vai vandyaḥ pūjyo 'haṃ bhavatāṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: I alone am to be revered here; I am always to be worshipped by you.

children.text: mayā hi pālitā yūyaṃ nivasadhvaṃ yathāsukham // VamPSm_26.11 //
children.translated_text: You are protected by me; dwell in comfort as you please. // VamPSm 26.11 //

children.text: tanmatto 'nyo na devo 'sti yuṣmākaṃ yaḥ parāyaṇam /
children.translated_text: Besides me, there is no other god who is your refuge.'

children.text: etacchratvā tu vacanamṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te // VamPSm_26.12 //
children.translated_text: Having heard these words, all those sages, // VamPSm 26.12 //
assembled together and spoke to the king:

children.text: śrutiḥ pramāṇaṃ dharmasya tato yajñaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ // VamPSm_26.13 //
children.translated_text: 'Scripture (<s>śruti</s>) is the authority for <s>dharma</s>; from it, sacrifice is established. // VamPSm 26.13 //
Without sacrifices, the gods dwelling in heaven are not pleased,

children.text: aprītā na prayacchanti vṛṣṭiṃ sasyasya vṛddhaye // VamPSm_26.14 //
children.translated_text: and when not pleased, they do not grant rain for the growth of crops. // VamPSm 26.14 //
Therefore, by sacrifices and gods, the world with its moving and stationary beings is sustained.'

children.text: etacchrutvā krodhadṛṣṭirvenaḥ prāha punaḥ punaḥ // VamPSm_26.15 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Vena</s>, with wrathful eyes, said again and again: // VamPSm 26.15 //
'Nothing is to be sacrificed, nothing is to be given!' — thus he spoke, overcome by anger.

children.text: tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te // VamPSm_26.16 //
children.translated_text: Then those sages, all of them, possessed by anger, // VamPSm 26.16 //
struck him down with <s>kuśa</s> grass, sanctified by <s>mantras</s>, (sharp) as thunderbolts.

children.text: tatastvarājake loke tamasā saṃvṛte tadā // VamPSm_26.17 //
children.translated_text: Then, in that kingless world, enveloped by darkness, // VamPSm 26.17 //
those (people), being oppressed by robbers, sought refuge with the sages.

children.text: tataste ṛṣayaḥ sarve mamanthustasya vai karam // VamPSm_26.18 //
children.translated_text: Then all those sages churned his hand — // VamPSm 26.18 //
the left one; from it arose a man of short stature.
All the sages said to him: 'Sit down!' // VamPSm 26.19 //
From him the <s>Niṣādas</s> were born, arising from the impurity of <s>Vena</s>.

children.text: tataste ṛṣayaḥ sarve manmathurdakṣiṇaṃ karam // VamPSm_26.20 //
children.translated_text: Then all those sages churned the right hand. // VamPSm 26.20 //
As that hand was being churned, another man was born —
resembling a great <s>Sāla</s> tree, marked with divine auspicious signs, // VamPSm 26.21 //
bearing a bow and arrows in his hands, and accompanied by a discus and standard.

children.text: tamutpannaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ // VamPSm_26.22 //
children.translated_text: Seeing him born, all the gods together with <s>Indra</s> // VamPSm 26.22 //
consecrated him as king on the earth, a protector of the land.

children.text: tataḥ sa rañjayāmāsa dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ tadā // VamPSm_26.23 //
children.translated_text: Then he delighted the earth with <s>dharma</s>, // VamPSm 26.23 //
(the earth) which had not been delighted by his father — he protected it.
There the word 'king' (<s>rājan</s>) arose for him, from delighting (<s>rañjana</s>) the earth. // VamPSm 26.24 //

children.text: sa rājyaṃ pāpya tebhyastu cintayāmāsa pārthivaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having received the kingdom from them, that sovereign pondered:
'My father was unrighteous, one who disrupted sacrifices. // VamPSm 26.25 //
How can the rites be performed for him that would bring happiness in the other world?'
As he was pondering thus, <s>Nārada</s> arrived. // VamPSm 26.26 //

children.text: tasmai sa cāsanaṃ dattvā praṇipatya ca pṛṣṭavān /
children.translated_text: Having offered him a seat and bowing down, he asked:

children.text: bhagavan sarvalokasya jānāsi tvaṃ śubhāśubham // VamPSm_26.27 //
children.translated_text: 'O lord, you know the good and evil of all the worlds. // VamPSm 26.27 //
My father was of evil conduct, a reviler of gods and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
devoid of his own <s>karmas</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — he has gone to the other world. // VamPSm 26.28 //
Then <s>Nārada</s> spoke to him, having seen with his divine eye
(that Vena had been) born among the <s>Mlecchas</s> (barbarians), afflicted with consumption and leprosy. // VamPSm 26.29 //
Having heard the words of the great-souled <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: cintayāmāsa dukhārtaḥ kathaṃ kāryaṃ mayā bhavet // VamPSm_26.30 //
children.translated_text: he pondered, afflicted by grief: 'What should I do?' // VamPSm 26.30 //
As that great-souled one was pondering, this thought arose in him:

children.text: putraḥ sa kathyate loke yaḥ pitṝṃstrāyate bhayāt // VamPSm_26.31 //
children.translated_text: 'He is called a son (<s>putra</s>) in the world who saves (<s>trāyate</s>) his ancestors from fear.' // VamPSm 26.31 //

children.text: evaṃ saṃcintya sa tadā nāradaṃ pṛṣṭavān munim /
children.translated_text: Having thus reflected, he then asked the sage <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: tāraṇaṃ matpitustasya mayā kāryaṃ kathaṃ mune // VamPSm_26.32 //
children.translated_text: 'How should I effect the deliverance of my father, O sage?' // VamPSm 26.32 //
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: gaccha tvaṃ tasya taṃ dehaṃ tīrtheṣu kuru nirmalam /
children.translated_text: 'Go and bring that body of his; purify it at the <s>tīrthas</s>,

children.text: yatra sthāṇormahattīrthaṃ saraḥ saṃnihitaṃ prati // VamPSm_26.33 //
children.translated_text: where the great <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Sthāṇu</s> is, near lake <s>Saṃnihita</s>.' // VamPSm 26.33 //
Having heard the words of the great-souled <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: sacive rājyamādhāya rājā sa tu jagāma ha // VamPSm_26.34 //
children.translated_text: entrusting the kingdom to his minister, the king departed. // VamPSm 26.34 //

children.text: sa gatvā cottarāṃ bhūmiṃ mlecchamadhye dadarśa ha /
children.translated_text: Having gone to the northern land, he found (his father) among the <s>Mlecchas</s>,

children.text: kuṣṭharogeṇa mahātā kṣayeṇa ca samanvitam // VamPSm_26.35 //
children.translated_text: afflicted with great leprosy and consumption. // VamPSm 26.35 //
Then, tormented by great grief, he spoke these words:

children.text: ha mlecchā naumi puruṣaṃ svagṛhaṃ ca nayāmyaham // VamPSm_26.36 //
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Mlecchas</s>, I bow to you; I shall take this man to my home. // VamPSm 26.36 //
There I shall make him free from disease, if you agree.'

children.text: tatheti sarve te mlecchāḥ puruṣaṃ taṃ dayāparam // VamPSm_26.37 //
children.translated_text: All those <s>Mlecchas</s>, compassionate toward that man, // VamPSm 26.37 //
said with all their limbs bowed in reverence: 'Do as you know (best).'
Then, having brought men accustomed to carrying a palanquin, // VamPSm 26.38 //

children.text: dattvā śulkaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ sukhena nayata dvijam /
children.translated_text: and having given double payment: 'Carry this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> comfortably.'

children.text: tataḥ śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya rājño dayāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having heard the words of that compassionate king,

children.text: 26.39 gṛhītvā śivikāṃ kṣipraṃ kurukṣetreṇa yānti te /
children.translated_text: taking the palanquin quickly, they went by way of <s>Kurukṣetra</s>. // VamPSm 26.39 //

children.text: tatra nītvā sthāṇutīrthe avatārya ca te gatāḥ // VamPSm_26.40 //
children.translated_text: Having brought him there to <s>Sthāṇutīrtha</s> and having set him down, they departed. // VamPSm 26.40 //

children.text: tataḥ sa rājā madhyāhne taṃ snāpayati vai tadā /
children.translated_text: Then at midday, the king bathed him.
Then <s>Vāyu</s> (the Wind god) spoke these words from the sky: // VamPSm 26.41 //

children.text: mā tāta sāhasaṃ kārṣistīrtha rakṣa prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Do not act rashly, my son! Protect the <s>tīrtha</s> with care!

children.text: ayaṃ pāpena ghorema atīva pariveṣṭitaḥ // VamPSm_26.42 //
children.translated_text: This one is excessively enveloped by terrible sin. // VamPSm 26.42 //
The reviling of the <s>Vedas</s> is a great sin whose end cannot be found.
This person, by bathing, will destroy this great <s>tīrtha</s> instantly.' // VamPSm 26.43 //
Having heard these words of <s>Vāyu</s>, overcome by great grief,
he spoke, tormented by sorrow, grieving for his (father's) suffering:

children.text: eṣa ghoreṇa pāpena atīva pariveṣṭitaḥ // VamPSm_26.44 //
children.translated_text: 'This one is excessively enveloped by terrible sin.' // VamPSm 26.44 //
I shall perform the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) that the gods shall prescribe.'

children.text: tatastā devatāḥ sarvā idaṃ vacanamabruvan // VamPSm_26.45 //
children.translated_text: Then all those gods spoke this word:

children.text: snātvā snātvā ca tīrtheṣu abhiṣiñcasva vāriṇā /
children.translated_text: 'Having bathed repeatedly at the <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords), sprinkle yourself with water;

children.text: ojasā culukaṃ yāvat pratikūle sarasvatīm // VamPSm_26.46 //
children.translated_text: with vigor, [offer] a handful of water upstream in the <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
One who bathes [there] with faith attains liberation.'
'This one, intent on self-nourishment and devoted to the defilement of gods,
abandoned by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, can never be purified.

children.text: tasmādenaṃ samuddiśya snātvā tīrtheṣu bhaktitaḥ // VamPSm_26.48 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, directing [the merit] toward him, having bathed at the <s>tīrthas</s> with devotion,
sprinkle [him] with water — then he shall become purified.'

children.text: ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā kṛtvā tasyāśramaṃ tataḥ // VamPSm_26.49 //
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction and having established his <s>āśrama</s> (hermitage) there,

children.text: tīrthayātrāṃ yayau rājā uddiśya janakaṃ svakam /
children.translated_text: the king went on a <s>tīrthayātrā</s> (pilgrimage), directing [the merit] toward his own father.

children.text: sa teṣu plāvanaṃ kurvastīrtheṣu ca dine dine // VamPSm_26.50 //
children.translated_text: Performing ablutions at those <s>tīrthas</s> day after day,
he constantly sprinkled his father with the water of the <s>tīrthas</s>.

children.text: etasminneva kāle tu sārameyo jagāma ha // VamPSm_26.51 //
children.translated_text: At this very time, a dog went forth —
a <s>kaulapati</s> (head of the household) at the <s>maṭha</s> (monastery) of <s>Sthāṇu</s>, a guardian of divine property,
always a protector of the accumulated possessions,
dear to all assemblies and devoted to divine duties.

children.text: tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya dharmamārge sthitasya ca // VamPSm_26.53 //
children.translated_text: While he was thus living, established on the path of <s>dharma</s>,
in time his mind was led astray toward the destruction of divine property.
Due to that <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), when he passed to the other world,

children.text: 26.54 dṛṣṭvā yamo 'bravīd vākyaṃ śvayoniṃ va3ja mā ciram /
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> (god of death), seeing him, spoke: 'Go to a dog's womb without delay!'

children.text: tadvākyānantaraṃ jātaḥ śva vai saugandhike vane // VamPSm_26.55 //
children.translated_text: Immediately after that pronouncement, he was born as a dog in the <s>Saugandhika</s> forest.
Then, after a long time, surrounded by a pack of dogs,

children.text: paribhūtaḥ saramayā duḥkhena mahatā vṛtaḥ // VamPSm_26.56 //
children.translated_text: tormented by <s>Saramā</s> (the divine dog), he was engulfed in great suffering.

children.text: tyaktvā dvaitavanaṃ puṇyaṃ sānnihatyaṃ yayau saraḥ /
children.translated_text: Leaving the sacred <s>Dvaitavana</s> (forest), he went to the <s>Sānnihitya</s> lake.
The moment he entered there, by the grace of <s>Sthāṇu</s> (Śiva),

children.text: atīva tṛṣayā yuktaḥ sarasvatyāṃ mamañja ha /
children.translated_text: overcome with extreme thirst, he plunged into the <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
There, with his body immersed, he was freed from all sins.
Then, out of hunger, he entered a hut.

children.text: praviśantaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā śvānaṃ bhayasamanvitaḥ // VamPSm_26.59 //
children.translated_text: Seeing the dog entering, [the king], filled with fear,

children.text: sa taṃ pasparśa śanakaiḥ sthāṇutīrthe mamañja ha /
children.translated_text: gently touched him — [the dog] had bathed at the <s>Sthāṇu</s> <s>tīrtha</s>.
As [the dog] had bathed at the earlier <s>tīrthas</s>, the drops that sprinkled [from him],
the water drops born from the body of that dog — by those he [the king's father] was sprinkled.

children.text: viraktadṛṣṭiśca śunaḥ kṣepeṇa ca tataḥ param // VamPSm_26.61 //
children.translated_text: Through the detached gaze of the dog and through his shaking [off water],

children.text: sthāṇutīrthasya māhātmyāt sa putreṇa ca tāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: by the greatness of the <s>Sthāṇu</s> <s>tīrtha</s>, he [Vena] was delivered along with his son.
Immediately at that moment, [Vena] was reborn and began to recite a hymn of praise.
<s>Vena</s> said:
I take refuge in the Lord <s>Īśāna</s>, in you, the unborn one, adorned with the moon,

children.text: mahādevaṃ mahātmānaṃ viśvasya jagataḥ patim // VamPSm_26.63 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s>, the great-souled, the lord of the entire universe.
Salutations to you, O lord of the gods of gods, O destroyer of all enemies,
O lord of the gods, subduer of <s>Bali</s>, worshipped by both gods and <s>Daityas</s> (demons).
O <s>Virūpākṣa</s> (odd-eyed one), O thousand-eyed one, O three-eyed one, O one dear to <s>Yakṣeśvara</s> (lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>),
having hands and feet everywhere, having eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,
having ears everywhere in the world — you pervade and abide in everything.
O <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> (spike-eared one), O doer of great deeds, O <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> (pot-eared one), O one whose abode is the ocean,
O <s>Gajendrakarṇa</s> (elephant-eared one), O <s>Gokarṇa</s> (cow-eared one), O <s>Pāṇikarṇa</s> (hand-eared one), salutations to you!
O hundred-tongued one, O hundred-whirled one, O hundred-bellied one, O hundred-faced one,
those who know the <s>Gāyatrī</s> sing of you; those who worship the sun venerate you.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ tvā śatakrato udvaṃśamiva menire // VamPSm_26.68 //
children.translated_text: They regard you as <s>Brahmā</s>, O <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra), like a lofty ridgepole.
In your form, O great-formed one, are the oceans and clouds,

children.text: devatāḥ sarva evātra goṣṭhe gāva ivāsate // VamPSm_26.69 //
children.translated_text: and all the deities abide therein, like cows in a pen.
In your body I see <s>Soma</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Jaleśvara</s> (lord of waters),

children.text: nārāyaṇaṃ tathā sūryaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca bṛhaspatim // VamPSm_26.70 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and also <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
O Blessed One, you are the cause and the effect, the action and the instrument of action;
you are the origin and the dissolution, both the existent and the non-existent, O deity.
Salutations to <s>Bhava</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to the boon-granter, to the one of fierce form,

children.text: andhakāsurahantre ca paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ // VamPSm_26.72 //
children.translated_text: to the slayer of the demon <s>Andhaka</s>, and salutations to <s>Paśupati</s> (lord of beings).
To the one with three matted locks, to the three-headed one, to the one holding the trident and skull-cup in hand,

children.text: tryambakāya trinetrāya tripuraghra namo 'stu te // VamPSm_26.73 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Tryambaka</s> (three-eyed one), to the three-eyed one, to the destroyer of the three cities — salutations to you!
Salutations to the shaven-headed one, to the fierce one, to the cosmic egg, to the cause of creation,
to the one with <s>ḍiṇḍima</s> (drum) attached to his hand, to <s>Ḍiṇḍimuṇḍa</s> — salutations to you!
Salutations to the one with upward-standing hair and fangs, to the emaciated one, to the deformed one,
to the one who is smoke-colored, red, and dark — salutations to you, O <s>Nīlagrīva</s> (blue-throated one)!
Salutations to the one without equal form, to the one of strange form, to <s>Śiva</s>,
to the one garlanded with suns, to the sun [itself], to the one bearing a banner of his own form.
Salutations to the one of pride and exceeding pride, salutations to you, the most acute,
salutations to the lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, to the one with a bull's shoulders, to the archer.
To the battle-crier, to the fierce one, to the one whose bowstring is of leaves,
salutations to the one of golden color, salutations to the one of golden radiance.

children.text: namaḥ stutāya stutyāya stutisthāya namo 'stu te /
children.translated_text: Salutations to the praised one, to the praiseworthy one, to the one established in praise — salutations to you!
To the all-pervading one, to the all-consuming one, to the one embodied in all beings,

children.text: namo hotre ca hantre ca sitodagrapatākine /
children.translated_text: salutations to the invoker and the destroyer, to the one with white, upraised banners,

children.text: namo namyāya namrāya namaḥ kaṭakaṭāya ca // VamPSm_26.80 //
children.translated_text: salutations to the one who should be bowed to, to the one who is bowed, and salutations to the clattering one.
Salutations to the destroyer of the lean, to the one lying down and the one risen up,

children.text: sthitāya dhāvamānāya muṇḍāya kuṭilāya ca // VamPSm_26.81 //
children.translated_text: to the one standing, to the one running, to the shaven-headed one, and to the crooked one.
Salutations to the one fond of dancing, adorned with rhythm and instruments,
to the one delighting in dramatic offerings, adorned with vocal music.
Salutations to the eldest, to the most excellent, to the destroyer of the strong by strength,
to the destroyer of Time, to Time itself, to the one whose form is the dissolution of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
O beloved of the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, salutations to <s>Bhairava</s>!

children.text: ugrāya ca namo nityaṃ namo 'stu daśabāhave // VamPSm_26.84 //
children.translated_text: Salutations eternally to the fierce one, salutations to the ten-armed one!
To the one who is fond of cremation-ground ashes, to the one with a skull-cup attached to his hand,
to the terrifying one, to the dreadful one, and to the one who observes fearsome vows,
salutations to the one with a distorted face, salutations to the one with a pure yet fierce gaze,
to the one fond of cooked and raw flesh, and to the one who delights in the <s>tāmbī-vīṇā</s> (stringed instrument).
Salutations to the one whose banner and tree bear the bull, salutations to the one celebrated by cows and bulls!

children.text: kaṭaṅkaṭāya bhīmāya namaḥ paraparāya ca // VamPSm_26.87 //
children.translated_text: Salutations to the clattering one, to the terrifying one, and salutations to the one beyond the highest.
Salutations to the most excellent of all, to the excellent one, to the boon-giver,
salutations to the one both detached and attached, to the one of contemplation, to the one wearing a rosary of <s>akṣa</s> (Rudrākṣa) beads.
To the one who is distinction, division, and the divided, to shadow and to the scorcher,
to the one whose form is both non-terrible and terrible, and to the one more terrible than the terrible.

children.text: namaḥ śivāya śāntāya namaḥ śāntatamāya ca /
children.translated_text: Salutations to <s>Śiva</s>, to the tranquil one, salutations to the most tranquil one,
to the one with many eyes and skulls, to the one of single form — salutations to you!
Salutations to the small one, to the greedy one, to the one fond of sacrificial portions,
to <s>Pañcāla</s>, to the white-limbed one, salutations to the one who controls by <s>Yama</s> and <s>Niyama</s> (restraint and observance).
Salutations to the one with wondrous and tinkling bells, to the one with bells upon bells,
to the one with hundreds and thousands of bells, to the one adorned with garlands of bells.
To the one proud of the clash of breaths, salutations to the one fond of the <s>kilikilikāra</s> (war-cry),
to the one who utters <s>huṃhuṃkāra</s>, to the transcendent one, to the one fond of the <s>huṃhuṃkāra</s> sound.
Salutations always to the one who is both even and equal, dwelling in homes and trees,
to the one [worshipped] with womb-flesh by jackals, to the deliverer, to the one who carries across.

children.text: namo yajñāya yajine hutāya prahutāya ca /
children.translated_text: Salutations to <s>Yajña</s> (sacrifice), to the sacrificer, to the oblation, and to the secondary oblation,

children.text: yajñavāhāya havyāya tapyāya tapanāya ca // VamPSm_26.95 //
children.translated_text: to the bearer of sacrifice, to the offering, to the one who should be worshipped through austerity, and to the scorcher.

children.text: namastu payase tubhyaṃ tuṇḍānāṃ pataye namaḥ /
children.translated_text: Salutations to you who are milk, salutations to the lord of beaks,
to the giver of food, to the lord of food, salutations to the one who eats various foods.
Salutations to the one with a thousand heads, and to the one with a thousand feet,
to the one with a thousand raised tridents, and to the one with a thousand ornaments.
To the protector who accompanies the young, to the one who sports in child's play,

children.text: namo bālāya vṛddhāya kṣubdhāya kṣobhaṇāya ca // VamPSm_26.98 //
children.translated_text: salutations to the young one and the old one, to the agitated one and to the agitator.
Salutations to the one whose hair is adorned by the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, to the one with <s>muñja</s>-grass hair,
salutations to the one pleased by the six rites, and to the one devoted to the three rites.
To the naked one of fierce spirit, to the fierce one, to the emaciated one, and to the one who causes bursting forth,
to the one who tells and narrates <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, and <s>Mokṣa</s>,
to <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, to the foremost in <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, to the one whose face is <s>Sāṅkhya-Yoga</s>,
salutations to the one who is both without a chariot path and at the four crossroads.
To the one whose upper garment is a black antelope skin, to the one whose sacred thread is a serpent,
to the one whose hair is arranged at the mouth, O <s>Harikeśa</s> (tawny-haired one), salutations to you!
To the lord of <s>Tryambikā</s> and <s>Ambikā</s>, to the one both manifest and unmanifest, to the creator,
O destroyer of desire, O granter of desire, O slayer of desire — to the one who deliberates between the satisfied and the unsatisfied,
salutations, O ever-present destroyer of sin, to the one who reckons the cycles of the <s>kalpas</s>.
O one of great being, O great-armed one, O great-strengthened one, salutations to you!
O great cloud, O one brilliant like a great [luminary], O <s>Mahākāla</s>, O one of great splendor,
O whirlpool of clouds, O cycle of ages, salutations to the lord of the moon and the sun!
You are food, the eater of food, the eater of what is cooked, the most purifying one.
Those born from the womb, from the egg, from sweat, and from the earth —
you alone, O lord of the gods of gods, are the fourfold host of beings.

children.text: sraṣṭā carācarasyāsya pātā hantā tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: You are the creator, protector, and destroyer of this [world] of moving and unmoving [beings];

children.text: tvāmāhurbrahya vidvāṃso brahma brahmavidāṃ gatim // VamPSm_26.107 //
children.translated_text: the wise call you <s>Brahman</s>, the goal of the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>.
You are the supreme light beyond the mind, you are the wind, and the [light] of luminaries;
the expounders of <s>Brahman</s> call you the bee in the tree of the <s>haṃsa</s> (supreme soul).
They say you are made of <s>Yajus</s>, made of <s>Ṛk</s>, and likewise made of <s>Sāman</s>;
you are always recited through praises by the hosts of <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Upaniṣads</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā varṇāvarāśca ye /
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, <s>Śūdras</s>, and those of lower <s>varṇas</s> —
you alone are the masses of clouds, the lightning, the thunder.
You are the year, the seasons, the month, and the half-month,

children.text: yugā nimeṣāḥ kāṣṭhāśca nakṣatrāṇi grahāḥ kalāḥ // VamPSm_26.111 //
children.translated_text: the ages, the eye-blinks, the instants, the constellations, the planets, and the divisions of time.

children.text: vṛkṣāṇāṃ kakubho 'si tvaṃ girīṇāṃ himavān giriḥ /
children.translated_text: Among trees you are the <s>Kakubha</s> (Arjuna tree); among mountains, <s>Himavat</s>;

children.text: vyāghro mṛgāṇāṃ patatāṃ tārkṣyo 'nantaśca bhoginām // VamPSm_26.112 //
children.translated_text: the tiger among beasts, <s>Tārkṣya</s> (Garuḍa) among birds, and <s>Ananta</s> among serpents.
Among oceans you are the <s>Kṣīroda</s> (ocean of milk), among weapons the bow,

children.text: vajraṃ praharaṇānāṃ ca vratānāṃ satyameva ca // VamPSm_26.113 //
children.translated_text: the thunderbolt among striking weapons, and truth among vows.

children.text: tvameva dveṣa icchā ca rāgo mohaḥ kṣamākṣame /
children.translated_text: You alone are hatred, desire, passion, delusion, patience, and impatience,
resolve, firmness, greed, lust, anger, victory, and defeat.

children.text: tvaṃ śarī tvaṃ gadī cāpi khaṭvāṅgī ca śarāsanī /
children.translated_text: You are the arrow-bearer, the mace-bearer, the skull-staff bearer, and the bow-wielder;

children.text: chettā mettā prahartāsi mantā netā sanātanaḥ // VamPSm_26.115 //
children.translated_text: you are the cutter, the binder, the striker, the thinker, the leader — the eternal one.
Endowed with the ten characteristics, you are <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, and <s>Kāma</s>;

children.text: samudrāḥ sarito gaṅgā parvatāśca sarāṃsi ca // VamPSm_26.116 //
children.translated_text: you are the oceans, the rivers, the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the mountains, and the lakes;
the creepers, the vines, the grasses, the herbs, the cattle, the wild animals, and the birds;
the initiator of substance, action, and quality — the one who grants flowers and fruits in due season.
You are the beginning and the end of the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and the <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ);

children.text: lohito harito nīlaḥ kuṣṇaḥ pītaḥ sitastathā // VamPSm_26.118 //
children.translated_text: you are red, green, blue, black, yellow, and white,
tawny, brown, dove-colored, and dark-blue,

children.text: savarṇaścāpyavarṇāśca kartā hartā tvameva hi // VamPSm_26.119 //
children.translated_text: both of color and colorless — you are indeed the maker and the taker.
You are <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera), and <s>Anila</s> (Vāyu);
<s>Upaplava</s>, <s>Citrabhānu</s>, and <s>Svarbhānu</s> as well. // VamPSm_26.120 //
The <s>Śikṣā</s> (phonetics), the <s>Haitraṃ</s>, the <s>Trisauparṇa</s>, and the <s>Śatarudriya</s> of the <s>Yajus</s>;

children.text: pavitraṃ ca pavitrāṇāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam // VamPSm_26.121 //
children.translated_text: the purest of the pure, and the most auspicious of the auspicious. // VamPSm_26.121 //
The <s>Tinduka</s> (Diospyros) among trees, the <s>Mudga</s> (mung bean) as the sustenance of all living beings;

children.text: prāṇāḥ sattvaṃ rajaścaiva tamaśca pratipatpitiḥ // VamPSm_26.122 //
children.translated_text: the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths), <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, and the observance of proper conduct. // VamPSm_26.122 //

children.text: prāṇo 'pānaḥ masānaśca udāno vyāna eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> as well;

children.text: unmeṣaśca nimeṣaśca kṣutaṃ jṛmbhitameva ca // VamPSm_26.123 //
children.translated_text: the opening and closing of the eyes, sneezing, and yawning. // VamPSm_26.123 //
Dwelling within the blood, the sight, the great-faced one, the great-bellied one;
with pure hair, with tawny beard, with upward-rising hair, both moving and unmoving. // VamPSm_26.124 //
One who knows song, instrumental music, and dance; one who delights in song and instruments;

children.text: matsyo jālo jalaukāśca kālaḥ kelikalā kaliḥ // VamPSm_26.125 //
children.translated_text: the fish, the net, the leech, time, playfulness, the gambler, strife. // VamPSm_26.125 //

children.text: akālaśca vikālaśca duṣkālaḥ kāla eva ca /
children.translated_text: The untimely, the ill-timed, the bad time, and time itself;

children.text: mṛtyuśca mṛtyukartā ca yakṣo yakṣabhayaṅkaraḥ // VamPSm_26.126 //
children.translated_text: death and the maker of death, the <s>Yakṣa</s> and the one terrifying to <s>Yakṣas</s>. // VamPSm_26.126 //
<s>Saṃvartaka</s> (the destroyer) and <s>Antaka</s> (the ender), and the <s>Saṃvartaka</s> cloud;

children.text: ghaṇṭo ghaṇṭī māhaghaṇṭī cirī mālī ca mātaliḥ // VamPSm_26.127 //
children.translated_text: the bell, the bell-ringer, the great bell, <s>Cirī</s>, <s>Mālī</s>, and <s>Mātali</s>. // VamPSm_26.127 //
The staff-bearer of <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Kāla</s> (Time), <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Agni</s>; the tonsured one, the bearer of three skulls;
the four ages, the four <s>Vedas</s>, and the initiator of the four sacrificial fires. // VamPSm_26.128 //
The leader of the four <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), and likewise the maker of the four <s>varṇas</s> (social orders);
always fond of dice, the cunning one, the overseer of the <s>gaṇas</s> (hosts), the lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>. // VamPSm_26.129 //
Wearing red garlands and garments, the mountain-dweller, the one fond of mountains;

children.text: śilpaṃ ca śilpināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvaśilpapravartakaḥ // VamPSm_26.130 //
children.translated_text: the craft itself and the best of craftsmen, the initiator of all crafts. // VamPSm_26.130 //
The one who destroyed <s>Bhaga</s>'s eyes, the fierce one, the destroyer of <s>Pūṣan</s>'s teeth;

children.text: svāhā svadhā vaṣaṭkāro namaskāro namo namaḥ // VamPSm_26.131 //
children.translated_text: he is <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>Svadhā</s>, <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>, <s>Namaskāra</s>, salutations upon salutations. // VamPSm_26.131 //
Of hidden vows, of secret austerities, the stars, and the essence of stars;

children.text: dhātā vidhātā saṃdhātā pṛthivyā dharaṇo 'paraḥ // VamPSm_26.132 //
children.translated_text: the creator, the ordainer, the arranger, and the supporter of the earth. // VamPSm_26.132 //

children.text: brahma tapaśca satyaṃ ca vratacarya mathārjavam /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge), <s>tapas</s> (austerity), truth, observance of vows, and rectitude;
the self of all beings, the maker of beings, prosperity, the origin of past, present, and future. // VamPSm_26.133 //

children.text: bhūrbhuvaḥ svarṛtaṃ caiva dhruvo dānto maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>, and <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) as well; the fixed one, the tamed one, <s>Maheśvara</s> (the great lord);
the initiated and the uninitiated, the beloved one, the untameable one, and the one born of taming. // VamPSm_26.134 //
The whirlpool of the moon, the whirlpool of ages, the initiator of cosmic dissolution;

children.text: binduḥ kāmo hyaṇuḥ sthūlaḥ karṇikārasrajapriyaḥ // VamPSm_26.135 //
children.translated_text: the drop, desire, the minute, the gross, the one fond of <s>Karṇikāra</s> (Pterospermum) garlands. // VamPSm_26.135 //
<s>Nandīmukha</s> (joyful-faced), <s>Bhīmamukha</s> (terrible-faced), <s>Sumukha</s> (fair-faced), and <s>Durmukha</s> (ill-faced) as well;
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the golden embryo), <s>Śakuni</s>, the lord of great serpents, <s>Virāṭ</s> (the cosmic being). //
26.136 The destroyer of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), <s>Mahādeva</s> (the great god), the staff-wielder, pre-eminent among the <s>gaṇas</s>;
in <s>Gonarda</s>, the protector of cattle, the one whose vehicle is the lord of bulls. // VamPSm_26.137 //

children.text: trailokyagoptā govindo gomārgo mārga eva ca /
children.translated_text: The protector of the three worlds, <s>Govinda</s>, the path of cattle, and the path itself;

children.text: sthiraḥ śreṣṭhaśca sthāṇuśca vikrośaḥ krośa eva ca // VamPSm_26.138 //
children.translated_text: the firm one, the best, <s>Sthāṇu</s> (the pillar), the cry, and the call. // VamPSm_26.138 //
Impossible to ward off, impossible to withstand, impossible to endure, impossible to overcome;

children.text: durddharṣo duṣprakāśaśca durdurśo durjayo jayaḥ // VamPSm_26.139 //
children.translated_text: impossible to assail, impossible to illumine, impossible to behold, unconquerable, and victorious. // VamPSm_26.139 //
Having the moon, fire, cold, and heat, hunger and thirst, and free from disease;
the afflictions and the maladies, the curer of maladies, the destroyer of diseases. // VamPSm_26.140 //
The multitude and the destroyer of the multitude, the eternal god;
crested, lotus-eyed, dwelling in the lotus grove. // VamPSm_26.141 //
Three-eyed, staff-wielding, with fierce fangs, the ender of clans;
the remover of poison, the best of the gods — you are the drinker of <s>Soma</s>, O lord of the <s>Maruts</s>;
the eater of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), lord of the universe, god of gods, lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>. // VamPSm_26.142 //
You are the bee among those dripping with honey, the voice of <s>Brahman</s>, dripping with ghee;
you are the enjoyer of all worlds, the grandsire of all worlds. // VamPSm_26.143 //

children.text: hiraṇyaretāḥ puruṣastvamekaḥ tvaṃ strī pumāṃstvaṃ hi napuṃsakaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Of golden seed, you are the one <s>Puruṣa</s> (cosmic person); you are woman, man, and also neuter;

children.text: bālo yuvā sthaviro devadaṃṣṭrā tvanno girirviśvakṛd viśvahartā // VamPSm_26.144 //
children.translated_text: a child, a youth, an elder — O divine-fanged one, you are the mountain, the maker and destroyer of all. // VamPSm_26.144 //

children.text: tvaṃ vai dhātā viśvakṛtāṃ vareṇyas tvāṃ pūjayanti praṇatāḥ sadaiva /
children.translated_text: You indeed are the creator, the most excellent among all makers; the humble ones always worship you;

children.text: candrādityau cakṣuṣī te bhavān hi tvameva cāgniḥ prapitāmahaśca /
children.translated_text: the moon and the sun are your two eyes; you indeed are <s>Agni</s> (fire) and the great-grandsire;

children.text: ārādhya tvāṃ sarakhatīṃ vāglabhante ahorātre nimiṣonmeṣakartā // VamPSm_26.145 //
children.translated_text: having propitiated you, they obtain <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquent speech); you are the maker of day and night, of the closing and opening of the eyes. // VamPSm_26.145 //

children.text: na brahmā na ca govindaḥ paurāṇā ṛṣayo na te /
children.translated_text: Neither <s>Brahmā</s>, nor <s>Govinda</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), nor the ancient sages

children.text: māhātmyaṃ vedituṃ śaktā yātātathyena śaṅkara // VamPSm_26.146 //
children.translated_text: are able to know your greatness as it truly is, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // VamPSm_26.146 //
Hundreds of thousands of beings whom you encompass and sustain —

children.text: mahatastamasaḥ pāre goptā mantā bhavān sadā // VamPSm_26.147 //
children.translated_text: beyond the great darkness, you are always the protector and counsellor. // VamPSm_26.147 //
Those who are sleepless, who have conquered the breath, established in <s>sattva</s> (purity), with senses controlled —

children.text: jyotiḥ paśyanti yuñjānāstasmai yogātmane namaḥ // VamPSm_26.148 //
children.translated_text: the light they behold through <s>yoga</s> — salutations to that one whose nature is <s>Yoga</s>! // VamPSm_26.148 //

children.text: yā mūrtayaśca sūkṣmāste na śakyā yā nidarśitum /
children.translated_text: Those forms of yours that are subtle, which cannot be shown —

children.text: tābhirmāṃ satataṃ rakṣa pitā putramivaurasam // VamPSm_26.149 //
children.translated_text: by those forms, always protect me, as a father protects his own son. // VamPSm_26.149 //

children.text: rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo 'haṃ tavānagha namo 'stu te /
children.translated_text: Protect me! I am worthy of your protection, O sinless one; salutations to you!

children.text: bhaktānukampī bhagavān bhaktaścāhaṃ sadā tvayi // VamPSm_26.150 //
children.translated_text: You are compassionate to your devotees, O Blessed One, and I am always your devotee. // VamPSm_26.150 //
To the one with matted hair, to the one bearing a staff, always, to the one with a large belly;
to the one bearing a water-pot and a quiver — salutations to that <s>Rudra</s>-self! // VamPSm_26.151 //
In whose hair are the clouds, in whose limb-joints are the rivers,
in whose belly are the four oceans — salutations to that one whose nature is water! // VamPSm_26.152 //
Having devoured all beings when the end of the age has arrived,
he who sleeps resting in the midst of the waters — I take refuge in that one who reclines upon the waters. // VamPSm_26.153 //

children.text: praviśya vadanaṃ rāhoryaḥ somaṃ pibate niśi /
children.translated_text: He who enters the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s> and drinks <s>Soma</s> (the moon) at night,

children.text: grasatyarkaṃ ca kharbhānū rakṣitastava tejasā // VamPSm_26.154 //
children.translated_text: and who swallows the sun — <s>Svarbhānu</s> (Rāhu) is protected by your radiance. // VamPSm_26.154 //

children.text: ye cātra patitā garbhā rudragandhasya rakṣeṇa /
children.translated_text: And those embryos that have fallen here, through the protection of <s>Rudra</s>'s fragrance —

children.text: namaste 'stu khadhā khāhā prāpnuvanti tadadbhute // VamPSm_26.155 //
children.translated_text: salutations to you! O <s>Khadhā</s>, O <s>Khāhā</s> — they attain that wondrous [state]. // VamPSm_26.155 //
Those <s>Puruṣas</s> (beings) of thumb-measure, dwelling in the bodies of all embodied ones —

children.text: rakṣantu te hi māṃ nityaṃ te māmāpyāyayantu vai // VamPSm_26.156 //
children.translated_text: may they always protect me; may they nourish me indeed. // VamPSm_26.156 //

children.text: ye nadīṣu samudreṣu parvateṣu guhāsu ca /
children.translated_text: Those who dwell in rivers, in oceans, in mountains, and in caves,
at the roots of trees, in cow-pens, in forests and dense thickets, // VamPSm_26.157 //
at crossroads, in streets, in squares, and in assembly halls,
in stables of elephants, horses, and chariots, and in old gardens and dwellings, // VamPSm_26.158 //

children.text: ye ca pañcasu bhūteṣu diśāsu vidiśāsu ca /
children.translated_text: and those who are in the five elements, in the directions and intermediate directions,
those who have gone between the moon and the sun, and those who are in the rays of the moon and the sun, // VamPSm_26.159 //

children.text: rasātalagatā ye ca ye ca tasmāt paraṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: those who have gone to the netherworld, and those who have gone beyond that —
salutations to them, salutations to them, salutations to them always! // VamPSm_26.160 //

children.text: yeṣāṃ na vidyate saṃkhyā pramāṇaṃ rūpameva ca /
children.translated_text: Those whose count, measure, and form are unknown —
the innumerable hosts of <s>Rudras</s> — salutations to them always! // VamPSm_26.161 //

children.text: prasīda mama bhadraṃ te tava bhāvagatasya ca /
children.translated_text: Be gracious to me; may there be blessing for you, and for one who has devoted his heart to you;

children.text: tvayi me hṛdayaṃ deva tvayi buddhirmatistvayi // VamPSm_26.162 //
children.translated_text: in you is my heart, O god; in you my intellect, and my mind is in you. // VamPSm_26.162 //

children.text: stutvaivaṃ sa mahādevaṃ virarāma dvijottmaḥ // VamPSm_26.163 //
children.translated_text: Having thus praised <s>Mahādeva</s> (the great god), the best of the twice-born ceased. // VamPSm_26.163 //
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the glorious <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Then the god <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva), the lord of the three worlds, spoke to him
a supreme utterance, consoling him, he who was skilled in speech. // VamPSm_27.1 //

children.text: aho tuṣṭo 'smi te rājan stavenānena suvrata /
children.translated_text: Ah, I am pleased with you, O king, by this hymn, O one of good vows!
What need of many words here? You shall dwell near me. // VamPSm_27.2 //

children.text: uṣitvā suciraṃ kālaṃ mama gātrodbhavaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having dwelt for a very long time, born again from my body,

children.text: asuro hyandhako nāma bhaviṣyasi surāntakṛt // VamPSm_27.3 //
children.translated_text: you shall become a demon named <s>Andhaka</s>, a slayer of the gods. // VamPSm_27.3 //
Obtaining birth in the house of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, you will grow to greatness;
