through the terrible <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) committed previously, and through the reviling of the <s>Vedas</s>, // VamPSm_27.4 //
when you become desirous of the mother of the world, then

children.text: dehaṃ śulena hatvāhaṃ pāvayiṣyāmi samārbudam // VamPSm_27.5 //
children.translated_text: having slain your body with my trident, I shall purify the multitude of sins. // VamPSm_27.5 //

children.text: tatrāpyakalmaṣo bhūtvā stutvā māṃ bhaktitaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: There too, having become sinless, having praised me again with devotion,

children.text: khyātogaṇādhipo bhūtvā nāmnā bhṛṅgiriṭiḥ smṛtaḥ // VamPSm_27.6 //
children.translated_text: you will become a renowned lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>, known by the name <s>Bhṛṅgiriṭi</s>. // VamPSm_27.6 //

children.text: matsannidhāne sthitvā tvaṃ tataḥ siddhiṃ gamiṣyasi /
children.translated_text: Standing in my presence, you shall then attain perfection.

children.text: venaproktaṃ stavamimaṃ kīrtayed yaḥ śṛṇoti ca // VamPSm_27.7 //
children.translated_text: Whoever recites or hears this hymn spoken by <s>Vena</s>, // VamPSm_27.7 //
shall not obtain anything inauspicious and shall attain long life.

children.text: yathā sarveṣu deveṣu viśiṣṭo bhagavāñśivaḥ // VamPSm_27.8 //
children.translated_text: Just as among all the gods, the Blessed <s>Śiva</s> is the most distinguished, // VamPSm_27.8 //
so is this hymn the most excellent of hymns, composed by <s>Vena</s>;
it is recited for the sake of fame, sovereignty, happiness, lordship, wealth, and honor. // VamPSm_27.9 //
It should be heard with devotion, and by those desiring knowledge, with effort;
one who is afflicted, suffering, wretched, or beset by fear of thieves and kings, // VamPSm_27.10 //
or one freed from royal duty — is released from great danger;

children.text: anenaiva tu dehena gaṇānāṃ śreṣṭhatāṃ vrajet // VamPSm_27.11 //
children.translated_text: in this very body, one attains the highest status among the <s>gaṇas</s>. // VamPSm_27.11 //

children.text: tejasā yaśasā caiva yukto bhavati nirmalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with radiance and glory, one becomes pure;

children.text: na rākṣasāḥ piśācā vā na bhūtā na vināyakāḥ // VamPSm_27.12 //
children.translated_text: neither <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons), nor <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls), nor <s>Bhūtas</s> (spirits), nor <s>Vināyakas</s> (obstacle-creating beings) // VamPSm_27.12 //

children.text: vighnaṃ kuryurgṛhe tatra yatrāyaṃ paṭhyate stavaḥ /
children.translated_text: create obstacles in that house where this hymn is recited.

children.text: śruṇuyād yā stavaṃ nārī anujñāṃ prāpya bhartṛtaḥ // VamPSm_27.13 //
children.translated_text: A woman who hears this hymn, having obtained her husband's permission, // VamPSm_27.13 //

children.text: mātṛpakṣe pituḥ pakṣe pūjyā bhavati devavat /
children.translated_text: becomes honored like a deity on both her mother's and father's side.

children.text: śruṇuyād yaḥ stavaṃ divyaṃ kīrtayed vā samāhitaḥ // VamPSm_27.14 //
children.translated_text: Whoever hears this divine hymn, or recites it with concentration, // VamPSm_27.14 //

children.text: tasya sarvāṇi kāryāṇa siddhiṃ gacchanti nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: all that one's undertakings are always crowned with success.

children.text: manasā cintitaṃ yacca yacca vācānukīrtitam // VamPSm_27.15 //
children.translated_text: Whatever is thought of in the mind, and whatever is recited with the voice, // VamPSm_27.15 //
all that is accomplished through the recitation of this hymn.
Sin committed by mind, body, and speech is destroyed.

children.text: varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yattvayā manasepsitam // VamPSm_27.16 //
children.translated_text: Choose a boon — may there be blessing for you — whatever is desired by your mind. // VamPSm_27.16 //
<s>Vena</s> said:

children.text: asya liṅgasya māhātmyāt tathā liṅgasya darśanāt /
children.translated_text: Through the greatness of this <s>liṅga</s>, and through the sight of the <s>liṅga</s>,

children.text: mukto 'haṃ pātakaiḥ sarvaistava darśanataḥ kila // VamPSm_27.17 //
children.translated_text: I have been freed from all sins, indeed through seeing you. // VamPSm_27.17 //

children.text: yadi tuṣṭo 'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama /
children.translated_text: If you are pleased with me, O god, if a boon is to be given to me —
this one, born in a dog's womb due to eating what belongs to the gods, who is your servant, // VamPSm_27.18 //
please bestow your grace upon this one too, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>;
for it was out of fear for this one that I plunged into the middle of the lake. // VamPSm_27.19 //
Previously I was prevented by the gods from bathing at this <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford);
this one has rendered me a service — for this reason I choose [this boon] for him. // VamPSm_27.20 //

children.text: tasyaitad vacanaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭaḥ provāca śaṅkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard these words of his, <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva), pleased, spoke:

children.text: eṣo 'pi pāpinirmukto bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ // VamPSm_27.21 //
children.translated_text: This one too shall be freed from sin — there is no doubt. // VamPSm_27.21 //
By my grace, O mighty-armed one, he shall go to the world of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tathā stavamimaṃ śrutvā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ // VamPSm_27.22 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, hearing this hymn, one is freed from all sins. // VamPSm_27.22 //
The glory of <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, and of this lake, O king,

children.text: mama liṅgasya cotpattiṃ śrutvā pāpaiḥ pramucyate // VamPSm_27.23 //
children.translated_text: and the origin of my <s>liṅga</s> — hearing this, one is freed from sins. // VamPSm_27.23 //
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One, saluted by all the worlds,
disappeared right there, before the eyes of all the worlds. // VamPSm_27.24 //

children.text: sa ca śvā tatkṣaṇādeva smṛtvā janma purātanam /
children.translated_text: And that dog, at that very moment, remembering his former birth,
assuming a divine form, approached that king. // VamPSm_27.25 //
Then <s>Vainya</s> (the son of <s>Vena</s>), having bathed, longing for the sight of his father,

children.text: sthāṇatīrthe kuṭīṃ śūnyāṃ dṛṣṭvā śokasamanvitaḥ // VamPSm_27.26 //
children.translated_text: seeing the empty hut at the <s>Sthāṇu</s> <s>tīrtha</s>, became overwhelmed with grief. // VamPSm_27.26 //
Seeing him, <s>Vena</s> spoke these words, filled with great joy:

children.text: satputreṇa tvayā vatsa trāto 'haṃ narakārmavāt // VamPSm_27.27 //
children.translated_text: By you, a true son, my child, I have been saved from the ocean of hell. // VamPSm_27.27 //
[He said:] 'By you I am always consecrated, standing on the sandy bank of the <s>tīrtha</s>;

children.text: asya sādhoḥ prasādena sthāṇordevasya darśanāt // VamPSm_27.28 //
children.translated_text: by the grace of this holy one, through the sight of the deity <s>Sthāṇu</s> (Śiva),

children.text: muktāpāpaśca svarlokaṃ yāsye yatra śivaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: freed from sin, I shall go to the heavenly world where <s>Śiva</s> resides.'
Having spoken thus, and having installed <s>Maheśvara</s> (the great lord) for the king,

children.text: sthāṇutīrthe yayau siddhiṃ tena putreṇa tāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: he attained perfection at the <s>Sthāṇu</s> <s>tīrtha</s>, having been saved by that son.

children.text: sa ca śvā paramāṃ siddhiṃ sthāṇutīrthaprabhāvataḥ // VamPSm_27.30 //
children.translated_text: And that dog [too attained] supreme perfection through the power of the <s>Sthāṇu</s> <s>tīrtha</s>;
freed from all impurities, he went to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.
The king, freed from the debt to his ancestors, having protected the earth,
having produced sons through <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), having performed unrestrained sacrifices,
having given desirable things to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having enjoyed manifold pleasures,

children.text: suhṛdo 'tha ṛṇairmuktvā kāmaiḥ saṃtarpya ca striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: having freed friends from debts, and having satisfied women with desires,

children.text: abhiṣicya sutaṃ rājye kurukṣetraṃ yayau nṛpaḥ // VamPSm_27.33 //
children.translated_text: having consecrated his son to the kingdom, the king went to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.

children.text: tatra taptvā tapo ghoraṃ pūjayitvā ca śaṅkaram /
children.translated_text: There, having performed fierce austerity and having worshipped <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva),

children.text: ātmecchayā tanuṃ tyaktvā prayātaḥ paramaṃ padam // VamPSm_27.34 //
children.translated_text: he abandoned his body by his own will and attained the supreme abode.
A person who hears this glory of the <s>tīrtha</s> of <s>Sthāṇu</s>,
freed from all sins, attains the supreme destination.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter of the <s>Saromāhātmya</s> in the glorious <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>.
